------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. INPUT TYPES (the same for ALL 11 sync functions, their async versions and crc32)
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Rule: if `data instanceof Uint8Array` (Buffer, Uint8Array, subclasses, views over a
SharedArrayBuffer), the view's bytes are used directly and byteOffset/byteLength are respected.
Anything else goes through Buffer.from(data, undefined), with every quirk of this runtime's
Buffer.from. Results below are the bytes the codec actually saw (checked by round trip):
  'hello'                                      -> 68656c6c6f
  'héllo€' (UTF-8)                             -> 68c3a96c6c6fe282ac
  '\ud800x' (runtime's Buffer.from quirk)      -> f48fa08078   (Node gives efbfbd78)
  '' / Buffer.alloc(0)                         -> empty input (valid; see section 3)
  Buffer.from('abc')                           -> 616263
  new Uint8Array([1,2,3])                      -> 010203
  new Uint8Array([10..17]).subarray(2,5)       -> 0c0d0e  (view respected)
  new Uint16Array([0x4142,0x4344,0x4546])      -> 424446  ELEMENT-WISE, each element truncated to a byte (NOT underlying bytes; Node gives 424144434645)
  new Uint16Array(buf_of_1..8, 2, 2)           -> 0305    (elements 0x0403,0x0605 truncated)
  new Int32Array([1,-1])                       -> 01ff
  new Int16Array([-129,300])                   -> 7f2c
  new Float64Array([1.5])                      -> 01
  new Float32Array([255.9,256,-0.5,NaN])       -> ff000000
  new Uint8ClampedArray([7,8])                 -> 0708 (also goes through Buffer.from)
  new BigUint64Array([1n])                     -> TypeError "Cannot convert a BigInt value to a number"
  DataView (any)                               -> treated as EMPTY input (0 bytes), no error.
                                                  Buffer.from(dataView) returns an empty Buffer here;
                                                  Node uses the bytes.
  ArrayBuffer containing 'abc'                 -> 616263 (whole buffer)
  SharedArrayBuffer                            -> TypeError "Buffer.from: unsupported value"
  [104,105]                                    -> 6869 (Node: ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE)
  [256,-1,'a',1.7,'7',null,true]               -> 00ff0001070001
  {length:2,0:65,1:66}                         -> 4142
  {length:'2',...}                             -> TypeError "Buffer.from: unsupported value"
  {length:-1}                                  -> RangeError "index out of range"
  function(){} (length 0)                      -> empty input, no error
  new String('hey')                            -> 000000 (treated as array-like; chars become NaN, then 0)
  5, 0, true, null, undefined, {a:1}, 5n, Symbol(), and calling with no argument
                                               -> TypeError "Buffer.from: unsupported value"
  Object.create(Uint8Array.prototype)          -> TypeError "zlib expects a Buffer/TypedArray"
                                                  (crc32: "zlib.crc32 expects a Buffer/TypedArray")
Every error above is a plain TypeError or RangeError. Its own props are ["message"] only: no code,
no errno, Object.keys(e) = []. e.stack exists (non-own). Example stack:
"TypeError: Buffer.from: unsupported value\n    at from\n    at <anonymous>...".
Decompressors convert strings to UTF-8 the same way, so a latin1 "binary" string of compressed
data gets corrupted. inflateSync(z.toString('latin1')) -> Error "inflate: unexpected end of input".
Only 1-arg Buffer.from calls are made for results. The input call has 2 args (data, undefined).

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. RETURN VALUES (sync)
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- The result is always a fresh Buffer, made by Buffer.from(nativeUint8Array), i.e. a copy:
  Buffer.isBuffer(r) is true, r instanceof Uint8Array is true, r.constructor.name is "Buffer",
  r.byteOffset is 0 and r.buffer.byteLength === r.length (not a slice of a bigger pool). The
  same holds for empty results: decompressing an empty payload gives length 0 and
  buffer.byteLength 0.
- Compressed output of empty input (hex):
    deflateSync('')        = 789c030000000001
    gzipSync('')           = 1f8b08000000000000ff03000000000000000000   (OS byte 0xff; Node uses 03)
    deflateRawSync('')     = 0300
    brotliCompressSync('') = 3b
    zstdCompressSync('')   = 28b52ffd240001000099e9d851
- Compressed output of 'hello':
    deflateSync        = 789ccb48cdc9c90700062c0215
    gzipSync           = 1f8b08000000000000ffcb48cdc9c9070086a6103605000000
    deflateRawSync     = cb48cdc9c90700
    brotliCompressSync = 0b028068656c6c6f03
    zstdCompressSync   = 28b52ffd240529000068656c6c6fa36d9f88
- Compressed output of 'hello hello hello hello hello world':
    deflateSync        = 789ccb48cdc9c957c04596e717e5a40000ebcf0d2d
    gzipSync           = 1f8b08000000000000ffcb48cdc9c957c04596e717e5a400009280058923000000
    deflateRawSync     = cb48cdc9c957c04596e717e5a40000
    brotliCompressSync = 0b118068656c6c6f2068656c6c6f2068656c6c6f2068656c6c6f2068656c6c6f20776f726c6403
    zstdCompressSync   = 28b52ffd242319010068656c6c6f2068656c6c6f2068656c6c6f2068656c6c6f2068656c6c6f20776f726c642cd015d9
  Deflate output is valid and Node can decode it, but it is not byte-identical to Node's zlib for
  longer inputs (equal for '', 'a', 'hello'). Node decodes the original's brotli output too.
  On 2250 bytes of repetitive text: brotli gives 1312 bytes (weak compression). zstd gives 2264
  bytes, i.e. it seems to emit only raw (uncompressed) blocks, with a checksum.
  Each decoder accepts Node/python-produced streams: node brotli q11 and q1, gzip level 9, zlib
  level 1, raw Huffman-only, python wbits=9.
- Size limit: the engine refuses typed arrays over 1 MiB (1048576 is OK, 1048577 throws). Any
  result over 1048576 bytes throws RangeError "Invalid typed array length". This applies to
  inflating 1048577 zero bytes, to inflate/gunzip of 2 MiB, and to deflate/gzip/deflateRaw of 1 MiB
  (or 1 MiB-64) of random data. brotli and zstd of 1 MiB-64 random data still fit (1048517 and
  1048549 bytes). Exactly 1048576 bytes of output works.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. OPTIONS: ignored completely, never even read
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- A Proxy passed as opts recorded ZERO property accesses (no get, has, ownKeys or gopd) for all 11
  sync functions and for the async functions.
- For every compressor, the output is byte-identical to the default for all of these:
  level 10/-2/1.5/'6'/NaN/0/1/9; windowBits 7/16/0/9; memLevel 0/10; strategy 5/-1/2;
  chunkSize 1/63/64; dictionary 'string'/123/Buffer; maxOutputLength 0/1/10/-1/'x';
  info:true; finishFlush 99/'x'/2; flush 99/2; params {}, {999:1}, {foo:'bar'}, 'x',
  BROTLI_PARAM_QUALITY 0/99, ZSTD_c_compressionLevel 19, ZSTD_c_checksumFlag 0,
  ZSTD_c_contentSizeFlag 0. The same holds when opts is null, 123, 'str', true, [], a function,
  or undefined.
- No input ever throws because of opts.
- For every decompressor the same option list (plus windowBits 47, maxOutputLength 34/35/
  Infinity, ZSTD_d_windowLogMax 10) gives the full normal output and never throws.
  - maxOutputLength is NOT enforced. inflateSync(1 MiB payload, {maxOutputLength:100}) returns
    1048576 bytes. Only the 1 MiB engine limit applies (RangeError "Invalid typed array length").
  - info:true changes nothing: the result is still a Buffer, not {buffer, engine}.
  - finishFlush: Z_SYNC_FLUSH does NOT allow truncated input. gunzipSync(truncated, {finishFlush:2})
    still throws Error "inflate: unexpected end of input".
  - dictionary is ignored. Zlib streams with FDICT set are not supported: python
    compressobj(zdict=...) data -> Error "inflate: invalid literal/length symbol", with or without
    a dictionary option.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. ASYNC CALLBACK FORMS
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Applies to deflate inflate gzip gunzip deflateRaw inflateRaw unzip brotliCompress
brotliDecompress zstdCompress zstdDecompress. All behave identically; results equal the sync
versions (checked for all 11).
- Signatures: x(data, cb) and x(data, opts, cb). If the 2nd arg is a function (typeof ===
  'function', including a Proxy of a function), it becomes the callback and the 3rd arg is ignored.
  Otherwise the 3rd arg is the callback. (buf, undefined, cb), (buf, null, cb), (buf, 'str', cb)
  and (buf, 0, cb) all work.
- Return value is undefined. Nothing is ever thrown synchronously, not even for bad input,
  corrupt data or a missing callback.
- Timing: the whole job runs in ONE promise-reaction microtask scheduled at call time: input
  conversion, compression, then the callback. Ordering test, in registration order:
      promise-before, microtask-before, [zlib.gzip call], promise-after
      -> promise-before, microtask-before, gzip-cb, promise-after
  The callback runs before setTimeout(0), setImmediate and (in this runtime) process.nextTick.
  With a 4-step .then chain started before the call: "tick1 gzip-cb gunzip-err-cb tick2 tick3 tick4".
  Multiple calls complete FIFO. Node, by contrast, calls back in a later macrotask.
  Because the work is deferred, mutating the input after the call changes the result:
    b=Buffer.from('aaaa'); zlib.deflate(b, cb); b.fill(0x62)  -> result inflates to "bbbb"
    the same for a Uint16Array or an Array mutated after the call.
- Success: cb(null, resultBuffer). arguments.length is 2. `this` is undefined (strict callback)
  or globalThis (sloppy).
- Failure: cb(err). arguments.length is 1 (no second arg). err is the same object the sync
  function would throw:
    zlib.inflate(Buffer.from([1,2,3]), cb) -> cb(Error "zlib: input too short")
    zlib.gzip(5, cb)                       -> cb(TypeError "Buffer.from: unsupported value")
    zlib.gzip(undefined, cb)               -> cb(TypeError "Buffer.from: unsupported value")
- If the callback throws on success, it is called AGAIN with that exception
  (try { cb(null, r) } catch (e) { cb(e) }):
    zlib.gzip('x', (err) => { n++; if (n===1) throw new Error('boom') })
    -> call #1 err=null, call #2 err=Error 'boom'
  If the callback throws again (or throws in the error case), the promise rejects unhandled. The
  runtime prints "Uncaught (in promise) Error: boom #2" to STDERR. The process continues and exits
  0. process.on('unhandledRejection') and process.on('uncaughtException') handlers are NOT called.
- Missing or non-function callback: zlib.gzip('hello'), zlib.gzip('hello', {}),
  zlib.gzip('hello','notfn'), zlib.gzip('hello',{},5), zlib.gzip('hello', null), and also
  corrupt or invalid input without a callback, all return undefined without throwing. Later STDERR
  shows "Uncaught (in promise) TypeError: cb is not a function" and the exit code is 0.
  (The callback variable is literally named `cb`. That engine message comes from calling an
  undefined `cb`. Engine quirk: once the same call site has thrown 8 times, the engine changes it to
  "undefined is not a function"; plain JS reproduces this too, so it is not zlib logic.)
  Node instead throws ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE synchronously.
- util.promisify(zlib.gzip)('hello') returns a Promise that resolves to a Buffer. With corrupt
  input it rejects with the plain Error (e.g. "gzip: bad magic"). util.promisify(zlib.deflate)
  ('abc', {level: 9}) works. zlib.gzip[util.promisify.custom] is undefined. There is no
  zlib.promises.

  Buffer.from not called). Everything else goes through Buffer.from(data, undefined), and strings
  are UTF-8.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. DECOMPRESSOR ERRORS AND CODEC BEHAVIOR (all errors are plain Error with only "message" as own prop)
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Each message is prefixed with the codec. Observed messages:
 inflateSync (zlib wrapper):
   length < 6 bytes                         -> "zlib: input too short"  (e.g. [], [0], [1,2,3])
   CM nibble (byte0 & 0x0f) != 8            -> "zlib: unsupported compression method" (garbage, ff.., gzip data, 7f9c)
   Not checked: FCHECK (789d accepted), CINFO (0800 accepted), FDICT, Adler-32 (missing, wrong or
   truncated trailer all accepted). The deflate stream is parsed from byte 2. Trailing junk and a
   second stream are ignored.
   inflate errors: "inflate: unexpected end of input", "inflate: invalid literal/length symbol",
   "inflate: distance too far back".
 inflateRawSync:
   []                                       -> "inflate: unexpected end of input"
   [0] or [1,2,3]                           -> "inflate: truncated stored block"
   '0123456789abcdef'                       -> "inflate: stored block overruns input"
   16 x 0xff                                -> "inflate: reserved block type"
   Stored-block NLEN is not checked against ~LEN. Trailing data is ignored.
 gunzipSync and unzipSync (identical):
   total length < 18 or magic != 1f8b       -> "gzip: bad magic"  (even a valid but truncated 17-byte gzip)
   CM != 8                                  -> "gzip: unsupported compression method"
   FEXTRA, FNAME, FCOMMENT and FHCRC are handled. Reserved flag bits are ignored.
   The deflate data is header..(len-8). The 8-byte trailer is stripped and NEVER checked (wrong
   CRC/ISIZE accepted). Losing trailer bytes therefore yields "inflate: unexpected end of input",
   while body + any 8 junk bytes works.
   Only the FIRST member is decoded: gzip('abc')+gzip('def') -> "abc" (Node gives "abcdef").
   unzipSync does NOT auto-detect the zlib format: unzipSync(deflateSync(x)) -> "gzip: bad magic".
 brotliDecompressSync:
   [], [0], [1,2,3]  -> "brotli: unexpected end of input"
   other messages seen: "brotli: non-zero padding bits", "brotli: uncompressed block overruns input",
   "brotli: corrupt code-length code", "brotli: reserved bit set".
   16 x 0xff -> returns an empty Buffer (no error). Trailing junk and a second stream are ignored.
 zstdDecompressSync:
   []                -> "zstd: empty input"
   [0] or [1,2,3]    -> "zstd: truncated frame"
   bad magic         -> "zstd: bad magic number" (trailing junk after a frame gives this too)
   others: "zstd: truncated raw block", "zstd: truncated content checksum",
   "zstd: content checksum mismatch".
   Two concatenated frames -> both outputs concatenated.

8. DIFFERENCES FROM NODE (v18 unless noted)

    out = bytearray(prev); lp = 0

steps.message:
I tested every export listed in the brief against `/tmp/orig`, plus the stream classes briefly. The full report is below and also saved to `/tmp/agent_a1/REPORT.txt`.

**Disclosure:** once, by accident, `console.log(zlib.Gunzip)` printed the class source, because console.log uses String(v). After that I never printed functions. Every stream-class claim below was confirmed with black-box tests.

**What matters most for the implementer:**
- **Options are never read.** A Proxy passed as `opts` recorded zero property accesses, sync and async. So there is no validation, `maxOutputLength` is not enforced, and `info: true` still returns a Buffer.
- **Z_MAX_CHUNK is literally `null`, not Infinity.** The brief's assumption is wrong.
- **Async callbacks run in a single microtask.** The input is read inside that microtask, so mutating it after the call changes the result.
- **A throwing success callback is called a second time with its own error.**
- **`unzipSync` handles gzip only.** It does not auto-detect zlib-format data.

**Files** (all in `/tmp/agent_a1/`):
- `REPORT.txt`
- `constants_keys.json` (the exact key order you asked for)
- `constants.json`
- `constants_values.txt`
- `codes.json`

---

# lumen `require('zlib')`: black-box behaviour report

## 0. A JS model that reproduces everything observed

```js
toU8   = (d) => (d instanceof Uint8Array ? d : Buffer.from(d, undefined))  // 2 args; the 2nd is undefined
xSync  = (data, opts = undefined) => Buffer.from(native_x(toU8(data)))    // name "", length 1; opts never read
x      = (data, opts, cb) => {                                            // name "", length 3; returns undefined
           if (typeof opts === 'function') cb = opts;                      // 3rd arg is then ignored
           Promise.resolve().then(() => {                                  // exactly 1 microtask tick
             try { cb(null, xSync_internal(data, opts)); } catch (e) { cb(e); }
           });
         }
crc32  = (data, value = 0) => native_crc32(toU8(data), value >>> 0)      // name "", length 1; returns a uint32 Number
class X (name "cls", length 1) extends stream.Transform  // buffers all chunks, runs the codec on flush
zlib.X  = lazy accessor that becomes a data property on first access
createX = (options) => new <exports object>.X(options)   // name "", length 1
```

Notes on the model:
- **Native type check:** a value that passes `instanceof Uint8Array` but is not a real typed array (e.g. `Object.create(Uint8Array.prototype)`) throws TypeError `"zlib expects a Buffer/TypedArray"`. For crc32 the message is `"zlib.crc32 expects a Buffer/TypedArray"`.
- **Internal references:** the async functions and the streams use internal codec functions. Monkey-patching `zlib.gzipSync` or `zlib.gunzipSync` does not affect `zlib.gzip()` or the streams.
- **Buffer.from:** zlib calls `Buffer.from` on the real Buffer object, so patching `Buffer.from` intercepts both input conversion and result wrapping. Setting `globalThis.Buffer = undefined` does not break zlib.

## 1. Module surface

### 1.1 Keys
`Object.keys(require('zlib'))` returns exactly 47 keys in this order:

```
["gzipSync","gzip","Gzip","createGzip","gunzipSync","gunzip","Gunzip","createGunzip",
 "deflateSync","deflate","Deflate","createDeflate","inflateSync","inflate","Inflate","createInflate",
 "deflateRawSync","deflateRaw","DeflateRaw","createDeflateRaw","inflateRawSync","inflateRaw","InflateRaw","createInflateRaw",
 "brotliCompressSync","brotliCompress","BrotliCompress","createBrotliCompress",
 "brotliDecompressSync","brotliDecompress","BrotliDecompress","createBrotliDecompress",
 "zstdCompressSync","zstdCompress","ZstdCompress","createZstdCompress",
 "zstdDecompressSync","zstdDecompress","ZstdDecompress","createZstdDecompress",
 "unzipSync","unzip","Unzip","createUnzip","crc32","constants","codes"]
```

- `Object.getOwnPropertyNames` gives the same list. There are no symbol keys.
- There is no `zlib.default`, no `__esModule`, and no top-level `zlib.Z_*` constants (Node 18 has them as non-enumerable properties).
- The exports object is a plain, extensible object whose prototype is `Object.prototype`.
- `require('zlib') === require('node:zlib')`.

### 1.2 Property descriptors
- **Functions, `constants`, `codes`:** data properties, `{writable: true, enumerable: true, configurable: true}`.
- **The 11 classes start as accessors:** `{get, set: undefined, enumerable: true, configurable: true}`. The getter's name is `"get"` and its length is 0.
- **First read:** directly or through `createX()`, the getter redefines the property on the exports object as `{value: cls, writable: true, enumerable: true, configurable: true}`. The key keeps its position, and later reads return the same class.
- **Saved getter called again:** it builds a new, different class and redefines the property on the exports object, never on the receiver.
- **Assignment before first access:** sloppy mode ignores it silently. Strict mode throws TypeError `"cannot set getter-only property 'Deflate'"`.
- **createX lookups:** `delete zlib.ZstdCompress` followed by `createZstdCompress()` throws TypeError `"undefined is not a constructor"`. createX looks up `X` on the exports object at call time, ignores `this`, and passes only its first argument.

### 1.3 The 36 non-class functions
- `name` is `""` for every one.
- `length`: each `xSync` is 1, each async `x` is 3, each `createX` is 1, `crc32` is 1.
- Own properties are exactly `["length","name"]`, with no `prototype`. Those two are `{writable: false, enumerable: false, configurable: true}`.
- `new zlib.gzipSync('x')` throws TypeError `"object is not a constructor"`.
- They do not depend on `this`; destructuring and `bind` work.

### 1.4 Classes
- **Construction:**
  - All 11 are ES classes and all distinct. Each has `name === "cls"` and `length === 1`, and own properties `["length","name","prototype"]`.
  - `X.prototype` is non-writable and non-configurable.
  - Calling without `new` throws TypeError `"Class constructor cannot be invoked without 'new'"` (Node allows it).
- **Prototype members:** `["constructor","_transform","_flush"]`.
  - `_transform` has length 3 and `_flush` has length 1.
  - All three are writable, non-enumerable and configurable.
  - Each class has its own copies.
- **Prototype chain:**
  - `Object.getPrototypeOf(X) === stream.Transform`.
  - `instanceof` is true for Transform, Duplex, Readable and EventEmitter, but **false for `stream.Writable`**.
- **Instances:**
  - Own keys, in order: `["_events","_eventsCount","_maxListeners","_readableState","readable","_writableState","writable","_chunks"]`. `_chunks` is an Array of Buffers.
  - There are no `close`, `flush`, `params`, `reset`, `bytesWritten` or `_handle` members.
- **Constructor options:**
  - Only Transform's options are read: `objectMode`, `readableObjectMode`, `highWaterMark`, `encoding`, `read`, `writableObjectMode`, `write`, `writev`, `final`, `transform`, `flush`.
  - Nothing zlib-specific is validated: `{level: 99}`, `5`, `'str'` and `[]` all work.
  - `new Gzip(null)` throws TypeError `"cannot read property 'objectMode' of null"`.
  - The default `highWaterMark` is 65536.
- **Stream behaviour:**
  - `_transform` stores `Buffer.isBuffer(c) ? c : Buffer.from(c, enc)` in `_chunks`.
  - `_flush` pushes `codec(Buffer.concat(_chunks))` as one `'data'` chunk. A codec error goes to `done(err)` and becomes an `'error'` event with the same plain Error.
  - Example: `createGunzip().end(Buffer.from('notgzip'))` emits `'error'` with Error `"gzip: bad magic"`.
  - In objectMode, `write(5)` emits no `'error'` event. Instead stderr shows `Uncaught (in promise) TypeError: Buffer.from: unsupported value`.

### 1.5 `zlib.constants`
- **Mutability:** 170 own enumerable keys, every one writable and configurable. The object is not frozen and is extensible; writing, adding and deleting keys all succeed. Node's properties are non-writable.
- **`Z_MAX_CHUNK` is `null`:** `typeof` is `"object"`, not Infinity.
- **`ZLIB_VERNUM` is 4865;** Node 18 has 4864.
- **Key order:** Node 18's 107 keys in Node's exact order, with two changes:
  - `ZSTD_DECOMPRESS=11` then `ZSTD_COMPRESS=10` are inserted right after `BROTLI_ENCODE=9`.
  - 61 `ZSTD_*` keys are appended after `BROTLI_DECODER_ERROR_UNREACHABLE`.
- **Values:** every shared key has Node's value, except `ZLIB_VERNUM` and `Z_MAX_CHUNK`.

Full list in order:

### 1.6 `zlib.codes`
A plain, mutable object. `JSON.stringify(zlib.codes)` is exactly:

```
{"0":"Z_OK","1":"Z_STREAM_END","2":"Z_NEED_DICT","-6":"Z_VERSION_ERROR","-5":"Z_BUF_ERROR","-4":"Z_MEM_ERROR","-3":"Z_DATA_ERROR","-2":"Z_STREAM_ERROR","-1":"Z_ERRNO","Z_OK":0,"Z_STREAM_END":1,"Z_NEED_DICT":2,"Z_ERRNO":-1,"Z_STREAM_ERROR":-2,"Z_DATA_ERROR":-3,"Z_MEM_ERROR":-4,"Z_BUF_ERROR":-5,"Z_VERSION_ERROR":-6}
```

The engine orders keys per spec, so build it this way:
1. Insert the number→name entries for -6 through 2 in ascending order.
2. Insert the name→number entries `Z_OK` … `Z_VERSION_ERROR`.

Node's order differs.

### 1.7 ESM
- `import zlib from 'node:zlib'` gives the same object as `require('zlib')`.
- Named imports work, e.g. `gzipSync`, `crc32`, `Gzip`, `constants`, and they are identical to the CJS properties.
- `import * as ns from 'zlib'` gives the 47 keys plus `"default"`, sorted. `ns.default === zlib`.

## 2. Input types
This applies to all 11 sync functions, the async versions and crc32.
- **Uint8Array (and Buffer):** the view's bytes are used directly, respecting `byteOffset`/`byteLength`. This includes Buffer, subclasses and views over a SharedArrayBuffer.
- **Anything else:** converted with `Buffer.from(data, undefined)`, including that function's quirks.

Bytes the codec actually received (checked by round trip):

| Input | Bytes used |
|---|---|
| `'hello'` | `68656c6c6f` |
| `'héllo€'` (UTF-8) | `68c3a96c6c6fe282ac` |
| `'\ud800x'` | `f48fa08078` (Node gives `efbfbd78`) |
| `Uint8Array [10..17].subarray(2,5)` | `0c0d0e` |
| `Uint16Array [0x4142,0x4344,0x4546]` | `424446`: **each element truncated to a byte**, not the raw bytes (Node gives `424144434645`) |
| `Int32Array [1,-1]` | `01ff` |
| `Float64Array [1.5]` | `01` |
| `Float32Array [255.9,256,-0.5,NaN]` | `ff000000` |
| `Int16Array [-129,300]` | `7f2c` |
| `Uint8ClampedArray [7,8]` | `0708` |
| `BigUint64Array` | TypeError `"Cannot convert a BigInt value to a number"` |
| **any DataView** | **empty input, no error** (Node uses its bytes) |
| ArrayBuffer | the whole buffer |
| SharedArrayBuffer | TypeError `"Buffer.from: unsupported value"` |
| `[104,105]` | `6869` (Node rejects arrays) |
| `[256,-1,'a',1.7,'7',null,true]` | `00ff0001070001` |
| `{length:2,0:65,1:66}` | `4142` |
| `{length:'2',…}` | TypeError `"Buffer.from: unsupported value"` |
| `{length:-1}` | RangeError `"index out of range"` |
| `function(){}` | empty input |
| `new String('hey')` | `000000` |
| `5`, `0`, `true`, `null`, `undefined`, `{a:1}`, `5n`, `Symbol()`, no argument | TypeError `"Buffer.from: unsupported value"` |
| `Object.create(Uint8Array.prototype)` | TypeError `"zlib expects a Buffer/TypedArray"` (crc32: `"zlib.crc32 expects a Buffer/TypedArray"`) |

- **Error objects:** all of these are plain TypeError/RangeError. The only own property is `message`; there is no `code` or `errno`, and `Object.keys(e)` is `[]`.
- **Strings passed to decompressors:** they are UTF-8 encoded too, so a latin1 string of compressed data gets corrupted. `inflateSync(z.toString('latin1'))` throws `"inflate: unexpected end of input"`.

## 3. Return values (sync)
- **Shape:** every result is a fresh Buffer copy made by `Buffer.from(nativeU8)`, with `isBuffer` true, `byteOffset` 0 and `buffer.byteLength === length`. Empty results have length 0 and a 0-byte buffer.
- **1 MiB limit:** any result over 1,048,576 bytes throws RangeError `"Invalid typed array length"`. This is the engine's typed-array limit, and exactly 1,048,576 works.

Sample outputs (hex):

| Function | `''` | `'hello'` |
|---|---|---|
| deflateSync | `789c030000000001` | `789ccb48cdc9c90700062c0215` |
| gzipSync | `1f8b08000000000000ff03000000000000000000` | `1f8b08000000000000ffcb48cdc9c9070086a6103605000000` |
| deflateRawSync | `0300` | `cb48cdc9c90700` |
| brotliCompressSync | `3b` | `0b028068656c6c6f03` |
| zstdCompressSync | `28b52ffd240001000099e9d851` | `28b52ffd240529000068656c6c6fa36d9f88` |

- **gzip OS byte:** the original writes `0xff`; Node writes `03`.
- **Deflate interop:** the output is valid and Node decodes it, but it differs from Node's bytes for longer inputs.
- **Compression strength:** on 2250 bytes of repetitive text, brotli gives 1312 bytes (weak). zstd gives 2264 bytes, so it appears to emit only uncompressed blocks plus a checksum.
- **Decoding foreign data:** every decoder accepted streams produced by Node and Python.

## 4. Options
- **Never read:** a Proxy recorded zero accesses (get, has, ownKeys, getOwnPropertyDescriptor), sync and async.
- **Compressors:** output was byte-identical to the default for every value I tried: `level` 10/-2/1.5/'6'/NaN, `windowBits` 7/16/0, `memLevel` 0/10, `strategy` 5/-1, `chunkSize` 1/63/64, `dictionary` of any type, `maxOutputLength` 0/1/10/-1/'x', `info: true`, `finishFlush`, `flush`, and `params` (`{}`, invalid keys, real brotli and zstd parameters). The same holds when `opts` is null, 123, 'str', true, [] or a function. Nothing ever throws.
- **Decompressors:** same result; they always return the full output.
  - `maxOutputLength` is not enforced.
  - `info: true` still returns a Buffer.
  - `finishFlush: Z_SYNC_FLUSH` still throws `"inflate: unexpected end of input"` on truncated data.
  - Zlib data with a preset dictionary (FDICT) throws `"inflate: invalid literal/length symbol"`, with or without the option.

## 5. Async callback forms
This covers deflate, inflate, gzip, gunzip, deflateRaw, inflateRaw, unzip, brotliCompress, brotliDecompress, zstdCompress and zstdDecompress. All 11 behave the same and produce the same results as the sync versions.

- **Argument handling:**
  - If the 2nd argument is a function, it is the callback and the 3rd is ignored. Otherwise the 3rd argument is the callback.
  - `(buf, undefined, cb)`, `(buf, null, cb)`, `(buf, 'str', cb)` and `(buf, 0, cb)` all work.
- **Return and throwing:** the call returns `undefined` and never throws synchronously.
- **Timing:** the whole job runs in one promise microtask scheduled at call time: input conversion, compression, then the callback.
  - Observed order: `promise-before, microtask-before, gzip-cb, promise-after`.
  - With a 4-step `.then` chain started before the call: `tick1 gzip-cb gunzip-err-cb tick2 tick3 tick4`.
  - The callback runs before `setTimeout(0)`, `setImmediate` and `process.nextTick`. Multiple calls complete in FIFO order. Node calls back in a later macrotask.
- **Deferred input read:** `b = Buffer.from('aaaa'); zlib.deflate(b, cb); b.fill(0x62)` gives a result that inflates to `"bbbb"`.
- **Success:** `cb(null, buf)` with `arguments.length` 2. `this` is `undefined` in strict mode and `globalThis` in sloppy mode.
- **Failure:** `cb(err)` with `arguments.length` 1. Corrupt data and invalid input types (e.g. `gzip(5, cb)`) both arrive through the callback.
- **Throwing callback:** if the success callback throws, it is called again with that error. If it throws again, or throws while handling an error, the rejection goes unhandled:
  - stderr shows `Uncaught (in promise) Error: …`
  - the process keeps running and exits 0
  - `process.on('unhandledRejection')` and `process.on('uncaughtException')` handlers do not run
- **Missing or non-function callback:**
  - Nothing is thrown at call time.
  - Later, stderr shows `Uncaught (in promise) TypeError: cb is not a function` and the exit code is 0. Node throws ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE immediately.
  - After the same call site has thrown 8 times, the engine changes the message to `"undefined is not a function"`. Plain JS shows the same quirk, so it is not zlib logic.
- **Promises:** `util.promisify(zlib.gzip)` works and rejects with the plain Error on bad input. There is no `util.promisify.custom` on these functions and no `zlib.promises`.

## 6. `zlib.crc32(data[, value])`
- **Algorithm and return:** standard CRC-32; every value matches Python's `zlib.crc32(bytes, value)`. Returns an unsigned 32-bit Number.
- **`data`:** follows the section 2 rule; strings are UTF-8.

| Call | Result |
|---|---|
| `crc32('hello')` | 907060870 |
| `crc32('')` | 0 |
| `crc32('héllo€')` | 464142983 |
| `crc32(new Uint16Array([0x6568]))` | 2439710439 (CRC of the single byte `0x68`) |
| `crc32(DataView)` | 0 |
| `crc32(new String('hello'))` | 3324180253 (five zero bytes) |
| `crc32(5)`, `crc32(null)`, `crc32()` | TypeError `"Buffer.from: unsupported value"` |

- **`value`:** converted like `value >>> 0`, with no validation. `valueOf` is called once.
  - Order: `data` is converted first, then `value`, then the native type check runs.

| Call | Result |
|---|---|
| `crc32('world', crc32('hello '))` | 222957957, same as `crc32('hello world')` |
| `crc32('hello', -1)` | 265137764, same as passing 4294967295 |
| `crc32('hello', 4294967296)`, or with NaN, Infinity, `'abc'` | 907060870 |
| `crc32('hello', 1.9)` or `true` | 191926070 |
| `crc32('', -1)` | 4294967295 |
| `crc32('', '0x10')` | 16 |
| `crc32('hello', 5n)` | TypeError `"Cannot mix BigInt and other types, use explicit conversions"` |
| `crc32('hello', Symbol())` | TypeError `"Cannot convert a Symbol value to a number"` |

- `new zlib.crc32('x')` throws TypeError `"object is not a constructor"`.

## 7. Decompressor errors
All are plain Error objects with no code or errno.

- **inflateSync:**
  - Input shorter than 6 bytes: `"zlib: input too short"`.
  - `(byte0 & 0x0f) != 8`: `"zlib: unsupported compression method"`.
  - Not checked: FCHECK, FDICT, Adler-32. Trailing junk is ignored.
- **inflateRawSync:**
  - Messages: `"inflate: unexpected end of input"`, `"inflate: truncated stored block"`, `"inflate: stored block overruns input"`, `"inflate: reserved block type"`, `"inflate: invalid literal/length symbol"`, `"inflate: distance too far back"`.
  - Stored-block NLEN is not checked.
- **gunzipSync and unzipSync** (identical):
  - Input shorter than 18 bytes or wrong magic: `"gzip: bad magic"`.
  - Bad compression method: `"gzip: unsupported compression method"`.
  - The header flags (FEXTRA, FNAME, FCOMMENT, FHCRC) are parsed correctly.
  - The last 8 bytes are stripped and never checked, so a truncated trailer gives `"inflate: unexpected end of input"`.
  - Only the first member of a multi-member gzip is decoded (Node returns all members).
  - `unzipSync(deflateSync(x))` throws `"gzip: bad magic"`.
- **brotliDecompressSync:**
  - Messages: `"brotli: unexpected end of input"`, `"brotli: non-zero padding bits"`, `"brotli: uncompressed block overruns input"`, `"brotli: corrupt code-length code"`, `"brotli: reserved bit set"`.
  - 16 bytes of `0xff` returns an empty Buffer.
- **zstdDecompressSync:**
  - Messages: `"zstd: empty input"`, `"zstd: truncated frame"`, `"zstd: bad magic number"` (also raised by trailing junk), `"zstd: truncated raw block"`, `"zstd: truncated content checksum"`, `"zstd: content checksum mismatch"`.
  - Concatenated frames decode to the concatenated output.

## 8. Differences from Node 18
- **Exports:** the original adds zstd and crc32 and uses a different key order. Its classes are lazy getters, and there are no top-level `Z_*` constants.
- **Functions and classes:** function names are `""`, classes are named `"cls"`, sync functions have length 1, and the classes require `new`. Instances lack close, flush, params and reset.
- **Constants and codes:** `constants` and `codes` are mutable. `Z_MAX_CHUNK` is `null`, `ZLIB_VERNUM` is 4865, and `codes` has a different key order.
- **Input conversion:**
  - Other typed arrays are converted element by element.
  - A DataView counts as empty.
  - Arrays and array-likes are accepted.
  - Bad types throw TypeError `"Buffer.from: unsupported value"` with no code.
- **Options:** never read, so there is no validation, `info`, `maxOutputLength`, `dictionary` or `finishFlush` support.
- **Errors and checks:**
  - Errors are plain Errors with codec-prefixed messages and no code or errno.
  - No checksum checks are done.
  - Only the first gzip member is decoded, and `unzip` handles gzip only.
- **Async:** completes in one microtask and reports every error through the callback. A missing callback becomes an unhandled rejection. A throwing callback is called twice.

## 9. Not tested
- Stream internals beyond the basics above: backpressure, pipe, destroy, `flush()`.
- Detached ArrayBuffers: `structuredClone` with `transfer` does not detach here.
- Byte formats beyond the samples above.
- Whether ESM named exports are live bindings.

def ncount_tokens(tablelog, tokens, pad_to_byte=True):
    """raw NCount writer driven by explicit tokens, mimicking the reader's nbBits evolution.
    tokens: ('c', count)  count in -1..   (value written = count+1)
            ('z', r)      2-bit zero-repeat flag (only meaningful after a 0 count)
            ('bits', v, n) raw bits
            ('log', v)    override the 4-bit accuracy field value (default tablelog-5)
    returns bytes"""
    bits = []
    def put(v, nb):
        for i in range(nb):
            bits.append((v >> i) & 1)
    toks = list(tokens)
    logv = tablelog - 5
    if toks and toks[0][0] == 'log':
        logv = toks[0][1]; toks = toks[1:]
    put(logv, 4)
    size = 1 << tablelog
    remaining = size + 1
    threshold = size
    nbBits = tablelog + 1
    for t in toks:
        if t[0] == 'z':
            put(t[1], 2)
        elif t[0] == 'bits':
            put(t[1], t[2])
        else:
            count = t[1]
            mx = (2 * threshold - 1) - remaining
            v = count + 1
            if v >= threshold:
                v += mx
            if v < mx:
                put(v, nbBits - 1)
            else:
                put(v, nbBits)
            remaining -= abs(count)
            while remaining < threshold and threshold > 1:
                nbBits -= 1
                threshold >>= 1
    if pad_to_byte:
        while len(bits) % 8:
            bits.append(0)
    out = bytearray()
    for i in range(0, len(bits), 8):
        b = 0
        for j in range(8):
            if i + j < len(bits):
                b |= bits[i + j] << j
        out.append(b)
    return bytes(out)

from pc_common import *
cases = []
# literal context map tests: NBLTYPESL=1, cmode 0 (LSB6: ctx = p1 & 63), NTREESL = n
# data chosen so contexts vary; each tree outputs a single symbol (simple nsym1) -> output reveals the map
def cmap_stream(ntrees, cmap, mlen, cmap_opts=None, cmap_writer=None, tree_syms=None, cmode=0, trunc=None, after_cmap=None):
    bw = BW(); wbits(bw, 22)
    mb_header(bw, mlen, islast=True)
    bw.put(0, 3); bw.put(0, 2); bw.put(0, 4); bw.put(cmode, 2)
    if cmap_writer: cmap_writer(bw)
    else: write_cmap(bw, ntrees, cmap, **(cmap_opts or {}))
    if after_cmap: return after_cmap(bw)
    bw.put(0, 1)  # NTREESD = 1
    for t in range(ntrees):
        write_simple(bw, 256, [tree_syms[t] if tree_syms else (0x41 + t)])
    s, ie, ien = ins_cmd(mlen); write_simple(bw, 704, [s]); write_simple(bw, 64, [0]); bw.put(ie, ien)
    return bw.bytes()
# output: first literal ctx = 0 (p1=0), then ctx = p1 & 63 of previous output.
# tree t outputs byte 0x41+t ('A'+t): ctx('A')=1, 'B'=2, ...
# map: ctx0 -> tree1 ('B'), ctx2 ('B') -> tree 2 ('C'), ctx3 -> tree 0 ('A'), ctx1 ('A') -> tree 1 -> 'B' -> 'C' -> 'A'...
cm = [0] * 64; cm[0] = 1; cm[2] = 2; cm[3] = 0; cm[1] = 1
cases.append(('cmap_basic_noRLE', cmap_stream(3, cm, 6)))
for rle in (1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 16):
    cases.append(('cmap_basic_rlemax%d' % rle, cmap_stream(3, cm, 6, dict(rlemax=rle))))
for rle in (0, 3):
    cases.append(('cmap_basic_imtf_rlemax%d' % rle, cmap_stream(3, cm, 6, dict(rlemax=rle, imtf=True))))
# IMTF with many trees and varied map
cm2 = [(i * 7 + 3) % 5 for i in range(64)]
cases.append(('cmap_5trees_imtf', cmap_stream(5, cm2, 12, dict(rlemax=2, imtf=True))))
cases.append(('cmap_5trees_plain', cmap_stream(5, cm2, 12, dict(rlemax=0, imtf=False))))
# NTREES = 256 (all distinct-ish map; each tree a single symbol)
cm3 = [(i * 37) % 256 for i in range(64)]
cases.append(('cmap_256trees', cmap_stream(256, cm3, 10, dict(rlemax=0), tree_syms=[(t * 13 + 7) % 256 for t in range(256)])))
cases.append(('cmap_256trees_imtf_rle16', cmap_stream(256, cm3, 10, dict(rlemax=16, imtf=True), tree_syms=[(t * 13 + 7) % 256 for t in range(256)])))
# RLE run overflowing the map: cmap all zeros of 64 using rlemax=6: symbol 6 with extra 0 -> 64 zeros fits; extra 1 -> 65 overflow
def cm_over(rle, sym, extra, prefix_vals=()):
    def w(bw):
        varlen8(bw, 2 - 1)  # 2 trees
        bw.put(1, 1); bw.put(rle - 1, 4)
        syms = [(v + rle if v else 0, 0, 0) for v in prefix_vals] + [(sym, extra, sym)]
        code = write_simple(bw, 2 + rle, sorted(set([s for s, _, _ in syms] + [0])))
        for s, e, nb in syms: code.put(bw, s); bw.put(e, nb)
        bw.put(0, 1)
    return w
cases.append(('cmap_rle_exact64', cmap_stream(2, None, 4, cmap_writer=cm_over(6, 6, 0))))
cases.append(('cmap_rle_overflow65', cmap_stream(2, None, 4, cmap_writer=cm_over(6, 6, 1))))
cases.append(('cmap_rle_overflow_after1', cmap_stream(2, None, 4, cmap_writer=cm_over(6, 6, 0, prefix_vals=(1,)))))
cases.append(('cmap_rle_overflow_127', cmap_stream(2, None, 4, cmap_writer=cm_over(6, 6, 63))))
# overflow then EOF immediately (no IMTF bit etc.)
def cm_over_eof(bw):
    varlen8(bw, 1); bw.put(1, 1); bw.put(5, 4)  # rlemax 6
    code = write_simple(bw, 8, [0, 6]); code.put(bw, 6); bw.put(1, 6)
    return bw.bytes()
cases.append(('cmap_rle_overflow_then_eof', cmap_stream(2, None, 4, after_cmap=cm_over_eof)))
# context map symbol out of range in simple code: NTREES=3, RLEMAX=0 -> alphabet 3 (2 bits): symbol 3
def cm_badsym(bw):
    varlen8(bw, 2); bw.put(0, 1)
    write_simple(bw, 3, [3]);
    bw.put(0, 1)
cases.append(('cmap_simple_sym_out_of_range', cmap_stream(3, None, 4, cmap_writer=cm_badsym)))
# alphabet = ntrees + rlemax : NTREES=2, RLEMAX=1 -> alphabet 3, symbol 3 invalid
def cm_badsym2(bw):
    varlen8(bw, 1); bw.put(1, 1); bw.put(0, 4)
    write_simple(bw, 3, [0, 3]);
cases.append(('cmap_simple_sym_out_of_range_rle1', cmap_stream(2, None, 4, cmap_writer=cm_badsym2)))
# trees referenced by map but ntrees unused trees: map uses only tree 0 though NTREES=3
cases.append(('cmap_unused_trees', cmap_stream(3, [0] * 64, 4)))
# a context map that uses RLE symbol with rlemax but value symbols > rlemax mapping
run_all(cases)

LUMEN (/tmp/orig): node:zlib STREAM CLASSES + CompressionStream / DecompressionStream
Black-box observations only. Outputs are copied verbatim from /tmp/orig unless marked "node:" (Node v18, for comparison).
The scratch scripts that produced them are /tmp/agent_a2/t1.js ... t70.js and demo1-3.js.

======================================================================
0. TL;DR: A MODEL THAT REPRODUCES EVERYTHING OBSERVED
======================================================================
I inferred this from behaviour, not from source. The only names used are ones that show up in error stacks
("at _flush", "at toU8", "at transform", "at flush", "at close").

zlib stream classes. Each one is a DIRECT subclass of the runtime's own require('stream').Transform:

  function make(codecSync) {                    // zlib.gzipSync, zlib.gunzipSync, ...
    return class cls extends Transform {        // note: every class's .name is "cls"
      constructor(opts) { super(opts); this._chunks = []; }
      _transform(chunk, enc, cb) {
        this._chunks.push(typeof chunk === 'string' ? Buffer.from(chunk, enc)
                        : Buffer.isBuffer(chunk) ? chunk      // stored BY REFERENCE (no copy)
                        : Buffer.from(chunk));                // throws for number/null/bool/object
        cb();
      }
      _flush(cb) {
        let out;
        try { out = codecSync(Buffer.concat(this._chunks)); } catch (e) { cb(e); return; }
        this.push(out);                         // exactly ONE chunk, even when it is 0 bytes long
        cb();
      }
    };
  }
  Gzip=gzipSync  Gunzip=gunzipSync  Deflate=deflateSync  Inflate=inflateSync  DeflateRaw=deflateRawSync
  InflateRaw=inflateRawSync  Unzip=unzipSync (gzip ONLY)  BrotliCompress=brotliCompressSync
  BrotliDecompress=brotliDecompressSync  ZstdCompress=zstdCompressSync  ZstdDecompress=zstdDecompressSync
  zlib.createX = (opts) => new X(opts)          // anonymous (name ""), length 1
  (_chunks is never cleared after the flush.)

- Every zlib option is ignored and nothing is validated. Only the base-stream options (objectMode, highWaterMark) have an effect.
- A hand-written `new Transform({transform(c,e,cb){cb()}, flush(cb){...}})` gives the SAME event order and the
  SAME microtask timing as the zlib streams, for success, cb(err) and throw. Reuse the runtime's Transform as-is.
- Stream output is byte-identical to the matching *Sync function applied to the concatenation of all input.
  I checked 66 decompressor cases (outputs and error messages) and every compressor/input combination I ran
  (including multi-chunk writes). There were zero mismatches.

CompressionStream / DecompressionStream. Each is a class with one own property, `_ts = new TransformStream({...})`:
- `readable` and `writable` are prototype getters that return this._ts.readable and this._ts.writable.
- transform(chunk): toU8(chunk) keeps a reference to a view of any ArrayBuffer/ArrayBufferView. Anything else
  throws TypeError "CompressionStream expects BufferSource chunks". This exact text is used by BOTH classes.
- flush(): out = codecSync(concat(chunks)). If out is non-empty, enqueue ONE plain Uint8Array.
  A codec error is rethrown as new TypeError(err.message). Other errors (e.g. RangeError) pass through unchanged.
- Codecs: CS 'gzip'/'deflate'/'deflate-raw' = gzipSync/deflateSync/deflateRawSync.
  DS 'gzip'/'deflate'/'deflate-raw' = gunzipSync/inflateSync/inflateRawSync.
  I checked 54 cases (outputs and messages); there were zero mismatches.

======================================================================
1. zlib STREAM CLASSES: SHAPE
======================================================================
1.1 Exports
- zlib keys, in order: gzipSync,gzip,Gzip,createGzip,gunzipSync,gunzip,Gunzip,createGunzip,deflateSync,deflate,Deflate,
  createDeflate,inflateSync,inflate,Inflate,createInflate,deflateRawSync,deflateRaw,DeflateRaw,createDeflateRaw,
  inflateRawSync,inflateRaw,InflateRaw,createInflateRaw,brotliCompressSync,brotliCompress,BrotliCompress,
  createBrotliCompress,brotliDecompressSync,brotliDecompress,BrotliDecompress,createBrotliDecompress,zstdCompressSync,
  zstdCompress,ZstdCompress,createZstdCompress,zstdDecompressSync,zstdDecompress,ZstdDecompress,createZstdDecompress,
  unzipSync,unzip,Unzip,createUnzip,crc32,constants,codes
- require('node:zlib') === require('zlib').

1.2 Classes (identical for all 11)
  zlib.Gzip: typeof=function name=cls length=1
  new zlib.Gzip() works. zlib.Gzip() -> TypeError: Class constructor cannot be invoked without 'new'
- s.constructor.name === 'cls' (node: 'Gzip').
- s instanceof zlib.Gzip -> true. zlib.createGunzip() instanceof zlib.Gzip -> false.
- zlib.Gzip.prototype.constructor === zlib.Gzip.
- Object.getPrototypeOf(zlib.Gzip) === require('stream').Transform -> true. There is no shared Zlib/ZlibBase class.
- Each class has its own _transform/_flush functions (Gzip.prototype._transform !== Gunzip.prototype._transform).
- Subclassing works: class My extends zlib.Gzip { constructor(o){ super(o); this.mine = true } } round-trips data.
- createGzip etc.: name "", length 1. `new zlib.createGzip()` throws "object is not a constructor".
- Prototype chain, with the own keys of each level:
   cls        [constructor,_transform,_flush]
   Transform  [constructor,_transform,_write,_final]
   Duplex     [constructor,_write,write,_queueBatch,end,cork,uncork,setDefaultEncoding,writableLength,
               writableHighWaterMark,writableObjectMode]
   Readable   [constructor,_read,readableLength,readableHighWaterMark,readableObjectMode,push,read,setEncoding,on,
               addListener,once,resume,pause,isPaused,pipe,unpipe,destroy] + Symbol.asyncIterator
   Stream     [constructor]
   EventEmitter [...the usual 16 methods]
- instanceof: Transform=true Duplex=true Readable=true EventEmitter=true, Writable=FALSE (node: true).
  Object.prototype.toString.call(s) -> "[object Object]".
- Instance own enumerable keys: ["_events","_eventsCount","_maxListeners","_readableState","readable",
  "_writableState","writable","_chunks"]. Own symbol: Symbol(kCapture).
- Initial _readableState: {"flowing":null,"ended":false,"endEmitted":false,"buffer":[],"length":0,"objectMode":false,
  "highWaterMark":65536,"encoding":null,"destroyed":false,"reading":false,"errored":null}
- Initial _writableState: {"ended":false,"finished":false,"destroyed":false,"corked":0,"corkBuffer":[],"errored":null,
  "tail":{},"objectMode":false,"highWaterMark":65536,"length":0,"needDrain":false}
- readableHighWaterMark and writableHighWaterMark are both 65536 (node zlib: 16384).

1.3 APIs that DO NOT EXIST (they are undefined)
- Methods: flush, params, reset, close, unshift, wrap, _destroy, _writev, _processChunk.
- Properties: bytesWritten, bytesRead, _handle, _chunkSize, _level, _strategy, _info, readableEnded, writableEnded,
  writableFinished, destroyed, closed, errored, readableFlowing, allowHalfOpen, writableCorked, writableNeedDrain,
  readableAborted, readableDidRead, readableEncoding, writableBuffer, readableBuffer.
- So calling any of the missing methods throws synchronously:
    s.flush()                                          -> TypeError: (intermediate value).flush is not a function
    s[m]() for m in flush/params/reset/close           -> TypeError: undefined is not a function
  (The text is the engine's generic not-a-function message.) The same happens for s.flush(Z_SYNC_FLUSH, cb) and
  s.flush(cb); the callback is never called.
- Present methods: destroy(len 1), pipe, unpipe, pause, resume, isPaused, setEncoding, on/once/off/emit/...,
  cork, uncork, setDefaultEncoding (a NO-OP, see 3), read, push, write(len 3), end(len 3).
- Flushing mid-way is therefore impossible. With the throwing flush() wrapped in try/catch:
    write('part one '); try{flush()}catch{}; write('part two'); end()
  the output equals gzipSync('part one part two') -> true. node: false, because node emits a sync-flush block.

1.4 Options
- Ignored, with no validation: level (99, -5, 'x', 0, 1, 9 all give identical bytes), chunkSize (1, 'abc'),
  windowBits (100), memLevel (100), strategy (99), dictionary (Deflate output has no FDICT; Inflate ignores it),
  params (brotli quality 1 and 11 give identical output; unknown key 12345 accepted), flush, finishFlush,
  maxOutputLength.
  node throws RangeError/TypeError ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE / ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE / ERR_BROTLI_INVALID_PARAM.
- createGzip(null) -> TypeError: cannot read property 'objectMode' of null (node: accepted).
  createGzip('str') and createGzip(5) are accepted.
- Base-stream options are honoured:
  createGzip({objectMode:true, highWaterMark:5}) -> readableObjectMode=true writableObjectMode=true rHWM=5 wHWM=5.
  createGzip({readableHighWaterMark:7, writableHighWaterMark:9, readableObjectMode:true}) -> rHWM=16 wHWM=65536 rOM=true
  (the split HWM options are ignored).
  objectMode does not change the output (still one Buffer).

======================================================================
2. zlib STREAMS: DATA FLOW, EVENTS, TIMING
======================================================================
2.1 Buffering
- NOTHING is emitted before end(), for compressors as well as decompressors (all 11 checked: 0 'data' events in the
  30 ms after write(), 1 after end()). node emits the gzip header and 16 KiB chunks as it goes.
- After end() there is EXACTLY ONE 'data' chunk (a Buffer) holding the whole output:
    createGzip, 200000 random bytes  -> chunks=1 sizes=[210882]   (node: 14 chunks of 16384...)
    createGzip({chunkSize:1024})     -> chunks=1 sizes=[210882]   (node: 197 chunks of 1024)
    createGzip({highWaterMark:1024}) -> chunks=1 sizes=[210882]
    createGunzip -> 300000-byte output -> chunks=1 sizes=[300000] (node: 19 chunks)
    The same holds for Deflate/DeflateRaw/Brotli*/Zstd*/Inflate*/Unzip.
- Empty output still emits a 0-length 'data' event (node emits none). For example, createGunzip().end(gzipSync(''))
  gives "data(0) end", and the same for Inflate/InflateRaw/Unzip/BrotliDecompress/ZstdDecompress.
  The generic Transform in this runtime also emits 'data' for push(Buffer.alloc(0)).

2.2 Event order (demo1.js)
  const s = zlib.createGzip();
  ['data','end','finish','close','drain','error','prefinish','resume','pause'].forEach(ev => s.on(ev, ...));
  log('write1 -> ' + s.write('hello ', () => log('write1 cb')));
  log('write2 -> ' + s.write('world', () => log('write2 cb')));
  log('end -> this? ' + (s.end(() => log('end cb')) === s));
  process.nextTick(() => log('nextTick')); setTimeout(() => log('timeout0'), 0);
 orig output:
  write1 -> true
  write2 -> true
  end -> this? true
  write1 cb
  write2 cb
  data 31
  end cb
  finish
  end
  nextTick
  timeout0
- NEVER emitted on normal completion: 'close' (only destroy() emits it), 'prefinish', 'resume', 'pause' (not even for
  explicit pause()/resume() calls). node emits resume ... finish, end, close.
- Order: 'data', then the end() callback, then 'finish', then 'end'. node: finish, data, end, close.
- Decompressors behave identically (Gunzip/Inflate trace: write1 cb, write2 cb, data 11, end cb, finish, end).
- Microtask timing (measured against a chain of Promise.resolve().then markers mt1, mt2, ... started before the writes):
    write #0 callback          at mt1
    write #k callback          at mt(1+3k)
    'data' + end cb + 'finish' at 3 hops after the last write callback (mt1 when there were no writes)
    'end'                      1 hop later
  Examples: 0 writes -> data/endcb/finish@mt1, end@mt2. 1 write -> wcb@mt1, data/endcb/finish@mt4, end@mt5.
  3 writes -> wcb@mt1,mt4,mt7, data@mt10, end@mt11. write(x)+end(y) -> wcb@mt1, data@mt7, end@mt8
  (the chunk passed to end() counts as one more write).
  Everything above happens inside microtasks, i.e. before ANY process.nextTick/setImmediate/setTimeout callback queued
  in the same synchronous block. (General runtime quirk: process.nextTick runs like a macrotask, after the microtask
  queue drains and FIFO with setImmediate.)
- The 'readable' event works (paused mode):
    s.on('readable', () => { while ((c = s.read()) !== null) ... }); s.write('hello'); s.end('world')
  gives: "readable read=[30]", "finish", "end". node: readable [10], readable [20], finish, readable [], end, close.
- No consumer at all: 'finish' and the end callback fire, readableLength=30, flowing=null. 'end' fires only after
  s.read() drains the buffer. read(5) and read(100) slice the buffer like node.
- setEncoding works and returns this: 'utf8' -> "string:héllo", 'hex' -> "string:68c3a96c6c6f",
  'base64' -> "string:aMOpbGxv", 'latin1' -> "string:hÃ©llo".
- pause() then end(...): isPaused=true, readableLength=3. resume() delivers data(3) then end.
- 'pipe' event: src.pipe(gz) emits 'pipe' on gz with src as the argument.

2.3 write() / end() return values and backpressure
- write() returns false iff writableLength, after adding the chunk, is >= writableHighWaterMark (65536):
    single write of 65535 bytes -> true; 65536 -> false; 40000 -> true, +25535 -> true, +1 more -> false.
  Strings count by .length (30000 x '€' -> writableLength=30000, returns true). node: 16384 threshold.
- 'drain' is emitted once, 1 microtask after the callback of the write that brought the length back down.
  Writes are "consumed" immediately because they are only buffered.
- end() returns this. end(null), end(undefined), end(''), end(cb), end(chunk, cb) and end('6869','hex',cb) all work;
  end(null) is treated as "no chunk".

2.4 Lifecycle of the state flags (t51.js)
  initial            readable=true  writable=true  rs.flowing=null  rs.ended=false ws.ended=false ws.finished=false
  after on('data')   rs.flowing=true
  after end()        writable=true (node: false)   ws.ended=true
  in 'finish'        readable=false writable=true  rs.flowing=false rs.ended=true rs.endEmitted=true ws.finished=true
  in 'end' and later same as in 'finish'. `writable` stays true forever.
  destroyed/readableEnded/writableEnded/writableFinished/closed/readableFlowing are always undefined.

3. zlib STREAMS: INPUT CHUNK HANDLING
======================================================================
I wrote each value to createGzip(), called end(), then decoded the output with gunzipSync:

  s.write('68656c6c6f','hex')    ok, decoded=68656c6c6f;  'base64' and 'latin1' are also honoured
  s.write(new Uint8Array([104,105]))       ok, 6869 (copied)
  s.write(arrayBuffer)                     ok, 6869 (accepted; node throws ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE)
  s.write(new Uint16Array([0x6968,0x2121])) ok, decoded=6821 (element-wise truncation, Buffer.from(typedArray))
  s.write([104,105])                       ok, 6869 (array accepted)
  s.write(new DataView(...))               ok, but contributes ZERO bytes (decoded=""; Buffer.from(DataView) is empty
                                           in this runtime)
  s.write('') / s.write(Buffer.alloc(0))   ok, no bytes
  s.write(123) / null / undefined / true / {a:1}:
     write() RETURNS true synchronously (node throws TypeError ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE / ERR_STREAM_NULL_VALUES).
     Then stderr shows:  Uncaught (in promise) TypeError: Buffer.from: unsupported value
     No write callback, no 'error' event. The stream STALLS for good: later writes and end() never produce
     'data'/'finish'/'end'. Example state afterwards: writableLength=6 after write(123)+write('abc'),

- Buffers are kept BY REFERENCE until end(): s._chunks[0] === b is true, and mutating b after write() but before end()
  changes the output ("zaaabb"). Uint8Arrays are copied.
- The generic Transform passes chunks through untouched (a string stays a string, enc=undefined unless given).
  The conversion is done in the zlib _transform.

4. zlib STREAMS: ERRORS
======================================================================
4.1 Corrupt, truncated or empty input (demo2.js)
  const s = zlib.createGunzip(); (listeners for data/error/end/finish/close)
  s.write(Buffer.from('not gzip'), err => log('write cb err=' + err)); s.end(() => log('end cb'));
 orig output:
  write cb err=undefined
  error: Error "gzip: bad magic" code=undefined errno=undefined own=["message"]
  end
- Errors are detected ONLY at end(), inside _flush. Writing garbage without calling end() never errors.
- Sequence: write callbacks (success), then 'error', then 'end' 1 microtask later.
  There is NO 'finish', NO end() callback and NO 'close'. node: ... finish, error, close, and no 'end'.
  'end' fires even when the stream is not flowing (no 'data' listener).
- After the error: rs.errored=null, rs.destroyed=false, rs.ended=true, rs.endEmitted=true, ws.finished=false,
  ws.errored=null, readable=false, writable=true.
- Error object: a plain Error (proto === Error.prototype). Own property names: ["message"] only.
  No code, no errno; Object.keys(e) is []. e.stack is a string such as "Error: gzip: bad magic\n    at <anonymous>\n
  at _flush". It is the same object shape as the *Sync error. node: code Z_DATA_ERROR / Z_BUF_ERROR, errno -3/-5,
  node messages "incorrect header check" / "unexpected end of file".
- Per class (input -> stream result). Each message is identical to what the matching *Sync throws:
  Gunzip     corrupt "not gzip data at all!" -> error "gzip: bad magic"
             truncated (first half)          -> error "inflate: unexpected end of input"
             trailing garbage                -> OK, data(780), garbage ignored (node: error "incorrect header check")
             empty / no write                -> error "gzip: bad magic" (node: "unexpected end of file")
             two concatenated members        -> OK, data(780) = FIRST MEMBER ONLY (node: 1560 / "abcdef")
  Inflate    corrupt -> "zlib: unsupported compression method"; truncated -> "inflate: unexpected end of input";
             trailing -> OK 780; empty -> "zlib: input too short"; double -> OK 780 (first stream only)
  InflateRaw corrupt -> "inflate: reserved block type"; truncated -> "inflate: unexpected end of input";
             trailing -> OK 780; empty -> "inflate: unexpected end of input"; double -> OK 780
  Unzip      same as Gunzip. It is GZIP-ONLY: zlib-format (deflateSync) input -> error "gzip: bad magic"
             (node auto-detects). unzipSync(deflateSync('abc')) also throws "gzip: bad magic".
  BrotliDecompress corrupt "not gzip data at all!" -> NO error, data(0) (lax decoder; other garbage gives
             "brotli: non-zero padding bits"); truncated -> "brotli: unexpected end of input";
             trailing -> OK 780; empty -> "brotli: unexpected end of input"; double -> OK 780
  ZstdDecompress corrupt -> "zstd: bad magic number"; truncated -> "zstd: truncated raw block";
             trailing garbage -> ERROR "zstd: bad magic number"; empty -> "zstd: empty input";
             two frames -> OK data(1560), ALL frames decoded
  Dictionary streams (FDICT set, made by node with {dictionary}) -> "inflate: invalid literal/length symbol",
  with or without the dictionary option (node: "Missing dictionary" / success).
  finishFlush: Z_SYNC_FLUSH on truncated input does NOT help: error "inflate: unexpected end of input", output 0
  (node returns the partial output without error).
- Total input > 1 MiB (e.g. 2 x 600000-byte writes): the Buffer.concat in _flush throws, which shows up as
  'error' "RangeError: Invalid typed array length", then 'end'. Every exception thrown inside _flush is routed the
  same way.

4.2 No 'error' listener
  s.write(Buffer.from('not gzip')); s.end(...); (only data/end/finish/close listeners attached)
  stdout: sync done / end / timer still runs
  stderr: Uncaught (in promise) Error: gzip: bad magic
  exit code: 0. The process keeps running. process.on('uncaughtException'/'unhandledRejection') handlers are NOT called.
  The emit('error') throw happens inside a promise job, so it becomes an unhandled rejection.
  node: prints the stack, exit 1.
  (For comparison: a top-level EventEmitter emit('error') without a listener prints "Uncaught Error: y" and exits 1.)

4.3 Write after end, and double end (t22.js)
  s.write('abc'); s.end();
  s.write('def', cb)  -> returns false; cb gets Error "write after end" (code undefined) asynchronously.
                         NO 'error' event. The stream still finishes normally (data(23), finish, end).
  s.end(cb2) again    -> returns this; cb2 is NEVER called.
  later, after finish:
  s.write('ghi', cb)  -> false; cb gets "write after end"; no 'error' event
  s.end('jkl', cb)    -> emits 'error' "write after end" synchronously (returns this when a listener exists). With no
                         listener, end() THROWS "write after end".
  node: the first write-after-end emits 'error' ERR_STREAM_WRITE_AFTER_END, then 'close'.

4.4 destroy() (t10.js). It only destroys the readable side:
  s.write('abc', cb); s.destroy()  -> returns this. Immediately: rs.destroyed=true, ws.destroyed=false, readable=false,
     writable=true. Then: write cb(undefined), 'close'.
     Further write('x', cb) -> returns true, cb(undefined). end() works and emits 'finish' and 'end', but no 'data'.
  s.destroy(new Error('boom'))     -> 'error'(boom), then 'close'. rs.errored=boom. The writable side keeps working.
  destroy() after end()            -> 'close'; a later write() returns false with cb "write after end".
  node: both sides destroyed; later writes fail with "Cannot call write after a stream was destroyed".

5. zlib STREAMS: PIPING, ITERATION, PIPELINE (all work)
======================================================================
- fs.createReadStream(in.txt).pipe(zlib.createGzip()).pipe(fs.createWriteStream(out)): pipe returns dest.
  Events: gz data 11178 (one chunk), ws finish, ws close. The file equals gzipSync(input).
- process.stdin.pipe(zlib.createGzip()).pipe(process.stdout) and the gunzip direction both work; exit code 0.
- for await (const c of gz): 1 chunk, Buffer. When the stream errors the loop throws the Error
  ("for await error case: threw Error: gzip: bad magic").
- stream.pipeline(rs, createGzip(), ws, cb): cb err=null on success (node: undefined).
  With a bad gunzip: cb err="gzip: bad magic". stream.promises.pipeline and require('stream/promises').pipeline exist.
- stream.finished(s, cb) -> err=null on success, err=<the Error> on failure. events.once(s,'end') resolves.
- Readable.from([Buffer,Buffer]).pipe(createGzip()) works.
- gzip.pipe(gunzip), brotli->brotli and zstd->zstd round trips work. Deflate->Unzip fails with "gzip: bad magic".
- pipe() FORWARDS source errors: createGunzip() fed garbage and piped to a Writable makes the destination emit 'error'
  (the SAME error object), then 'close', then 'finish' (dest.end() runs because the source emits 'end').
  If the destination has no error listener: "Uncaught (in promise) Error: gzip: bad magic" on stderr, even when the
  gunzip itself has a listener. node does not forward the error and does not end the destination.
  (This is generic stream behaviour, but it is visible in zlib pipe chains.)
- Side note, codec: the round trip in my pipe test FAILED. gunzipSync(gzipSync(in.txt)) throws "inflate: invalid Huffman
  code", and node cannot decode the file either ("invalid distance code"). See 7.

======================================================================
6. CompressionStream / DecompressionStream
======================================================================
6.1 Shape
- Globals: typeof 'function'. name "CompressionStream" / "DecompressionStream", length 1.
  Property descriptor: writable, ENUMERABLE (node: non-enumerable), configurable.
- prototype own names: ["constructor","readable","writable"]. readable and writable are getters (no setter),
  enumerable=false (node: true), configurable=true. Object.keys(CompressionStream.prototype) -> [].
- Parent is Object. cs instanceof TransformStream -> false.
- Instance: own keys ["_ts"]; cs._ts.constructor.name === 'TransformStream'; cs.readable === cs._ts.readable.
  The getters are stable (same object every time). cs.readable instanceof ReadableStream and
  cs.writable instanceof WritableStream are both true.
- Getter on a foreign object: get.call({}) -> TypeError: cannot read property 'readable' of undefined.
  get.call({_ts:{readable:42}}) -> 42.
- Object.prototype.toString.call(cs) -> "[object Object]"; cs[Symbol.toStringTag] -> undefined;
  JSON.stringify(cs) shows {"_ts":{...}}.
- Called without new: TypeError: Class constructor cannot be invoked without 'new'.
- Subclassing works. A second constructor argument is ignored.

6.2 Format argument: converted with ToString (template-literal semantics), then compared EXACTLY
  Accepted: 'gzip', 'deflate', 'deflate-raw' (node 18 rejects 'deflate-raw'). Also any object whose toString() returns
  one of these: ['gzip'], {toString(){return 'gzip'}}, and {valueOf(){return 'bogus2'}, toString(){return 'gzip'}}
  (toString wins). {valueOf(){return 'deflate-raw'}, toString(){return 'bogus'}} -> rejected with 'bogus'.
  Rejected, with TypeError (not DOMException, no code):
    new CompressionStream('brotli') -> TypeError: Unsupported CompressionStream format: 'brotli'
    'br' -> ...'br'   'zstd' -> ...'zstd'   'GZIP' -> ...'GZIP'   'Gzip'   ' gzip'   'deflate64'   'x-gzip'
    ''        -> TypeError: Unsupported CompressionStream format: ''
    undefined -> ...'undefined'  (no argument gives the same)
    null      -> ...'null'   123 -> ...'123'   {} -> ...'[object Object]'
    Symbol('x') -> TypeError: Cannot convert a Symbol value to a string
    an object whose toString throws RangeError('ts boom') -> that RangeError propagates
  DecompressionStream uses the same texts with "DecompressionStream": "Unsupported DecompressionStream format: 'br'".
  node: TypeError "The argument 'format' is invalid. Received 'br'" code ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE.

6.3 Data flow (demo3.js)
  const cs = new CompressionStream('gzip'); const w = cs.writable.getWriter(), r = cs.readable.getReader();
  log desiredSize; w.write(enc('hello ')); w.write(Uint8Array 'world'); log desiredSize; w.close(); read all
 orig output:
  desiredSize=1
  desiredSize after 2 writes=-1
  write1 resolved
  write2 resolved
  chunk Uint8Array len=31
  done; equals gzipSync: true
  close resolved
- All input is buffered. NO output appears before close(): a pending read() stays unresolved while writes are made
  and only settles after close(). Output is ONE chunk containing everything, as a plain Uint8Array
  (not a Buffer; byteOffset 0; buffer.byteLength == length).
  Examples: 200000 random bytes in 4 writes -> chunks=1 [210840]. DS of a 300000-byte payload written in 23 pieces of
  100 bytes -> chunks=1 [300000]. node: 16 KiB chunks plus an early 10-byte gzip header chunk.
- Bytes are identical to gzipSync/deflateSync/deflateRawSync of the concatenated input. Single-byte chunks give the
  same bytes, and DS with single-byte input chunks round-trips correctly.
- Writer: initial desiredSize=1 (HWM 1, every chunk counts 1). It drops by 1 per write and can go negative (-1, -2).
  writer.ready is ALWAYS already resolved, even at desiredSize <= 0. Write promises resolve whether or not anyone reads.
- close() resolves even with NO reader attached. The chunk waits in the readable; a reader attached later
  (setTimeout 5 ms) gets the chunk, then done.
- Microtask timing (single write, then close, measured like 2.2):
  writer.ready resolves at mt1, write() at mt5, a pending read() with the chunk at mt6, read #2 {done:true} and
  reader.closed at mt7, writer.closed then the close() promise at mt9 ('closed' settles BEFORE close(); node is the
  other way round). Everything finishes before nextTick/timers.
- Input chunks are kept BY REFERENCE until close(): mutating a written Uint8Array or ArrayBuffer before close changes
  the output ("zaa"). (Buffer.from(arrayBuffer) COPIES in this runtime, so a Buffer built that way is not affected.)
- Works: custom ReadableStream.pipeThrough(cs) (1 chunk), .pipeTo(new WritableStream(...)),
  for await over cs.readable (1 Uint8Array), blob.stream().pipeThrough(cs) read with a reader,
  ds.readable.pipeThrough(new TextDecoderStream()) ("décodé").
- Response LIMITATION: the body is consumed SYNCHRONOUSLY at arrayBuffer()/text() time.
    await new Response(new Blob(['abc']).stream().pipeThrough(new CompressionStream('gzip'))).arrayBuffer()
      -> rejects: TypeError: a body ReadableStream must produce its data synchronously in this runtime
         (the Response constructor itself succeeds; the rejection comes from arrayBuffer())
    w.write(x); w.close(); await new Response(cs.readable).arrayBuffer()        -> the same TypeError
    const p = w.close(); const resp = new Response(cs.readable); await p; await resp.arrayBuffer() -> OK (25 bytes)
    After `await w.close()`, new Response(cs.readable).arrayBuffer() -> OK, equals gzipSync
    new Response(new Blob(['xyz']).stream()).arrayBuffer() -> OK
  node: all of these work. (fetch('data:...') -> TypeError: fetch: unsupported scheme 'data'.)

6.4 Chunk types for writer.write() (both classes)
  Accepted (bytes of the VIEW are used): Uint8Array, Buffer, ArrayBuffer, DataView (offset/length honoured),
    Int8Array, Int16Array([0x6968]) -> bytes 68 69, Float64Array([1.5]) -> 000000000000f83f, subarray views.
    node 18 accepts only Buffer/Uint8Array (and strings).
  Rejected: string, number, null, undefined, plain object, Array, SharedArrayBuffer. In every case:
    write() promise rejects: TypeError: CompressionStream expects BufferSource chunks
      (DecompressionStream uses the SAME text "CompressionStream expects ...". Own props ["message"];
       stack "at toU8 / at transform / at write")
    close() rejects with the same TypeError. writable._state='errored'. writer.desiredSize=null.
    Further write() calls reject with the same error.
    The readable is NOT errored: readable._state stays 'readable' and reader.read() NEVER settles (hangs).
    Through pipeThrough, the read() also hangs.

6.5 Decompression errors (DecompressionStream)
  ds.writable.getWriter().write(new Uint8Array([1,2,3])) -> resolves
  await w.close() -> rejects: TypeError: gzip: bad magic
  ds.readable.getReader().read() -> still pending after 100ms
- The error surfaces ONLY as the rejection of writer.close(), as a TypeError carrying the codec message
  (own props ["message"], no cause; stack "at flush / at close"). write() promises resolve. A directly held
  reader.read() HANGS forever; writer.closed and reader.closed never settle.
- State afterwards: writable._state='writable' (!), readable._state='readable', desiredSize=1, writer.ready resolved.
  A further write() RESOLVES, and a second close() rejects again with the same TypeError.
- Through pipes: readable.pipeThrough(new DecompressionStream('gzip')).getReader().read() REJECTS with the TypeError,
  for-await throws it, and rs.pipeTo(ds.writable) rejects with it.
- Messages (identical to *Sync, but as TypeError): 'gzip' corrupt or empty -> "gzip: bad magic"; truncated ->
  "inflate: unexpected end of input". 'deflate' corrupt -> "zlib: unsupported compression method"; empty or <6 bytes ->
  "zlib: input too short". 'deflate-raw' corrupt -> "inflate: invalid Huffman code"; empty ->
  "inflate: unexpected end of input".
  node: Error "incorrect header check" with code Z_DATA_ERROR, readable errored too.
- Trailing garbage after a valid stream -> NO error, output = first stream. Two concatenated gzip members -> first only.
- Total input > 1 MiB -> close() rejects with RangeError: Invalid typed array length (NOT converted to TypeError).
- writer.abort(new Error('my abort')) -> resolves; writable and readable both 'errored'; read() rejects with that Error.
- reader.cancel(err) -> resolves; readable 'closed', writable stays 'writable'. write() still resolves, but close()
  rejects with TypeError: stream is not in a readable state.

6.6 Edge cases
- Empty input (no writes, or one empty write). CS gives ONE chunk:
    gzip        1f8b08000000000000ff03000000000000000000 (20 bytes; OS byte 0xff, node 0x03)
    deflate     789c030000000001
    deflate-raw 0300
  DS of those empty streams -> ZERO chunks, then done (no empty Uint8Array is enqueued; contrast with 2.1).
- Double close: w.close(); w.close() made synchronously -> BOTH resolve, and the readable then yields the compressed
  output TWICE (2 identical 21-byte chunks), then done. Calling close() after the stream is closed rejects:
  TypeError: stream is not in a readable state. write() after a successful close RESOLVES.
- Second getWriter() -> TypeError: WritableStream is already locked.
  Second getReader() -> TypeError: stream is already locked to a reader.

======================================================================
7. SIDE NOTES ON THE SHARED CODECS (affect the stream output too)
======================================================================
- The deflate ENCODER is buggy for match distances > 32768. A repeat at distance 32768 round-trips; at 32769 or 40000
  the original's inflate says "inflate: unexpected end of input", and at 65536 or 70000
  "inflate: invalid literal/length symbol". node rejects the same bytes. My 73893-byte text file
  ("line of text number N\n" x3000) fails from a 34240-byte prefix on.
- Compressed sizes are not zlib's: gzip of 200000 random bytes = 210882 bytes; brotli and zstd of small inputs are
  stored or raw; zstd of 22500 repetitive bytes = 22514 bytes. The gzip header OS byte is 0xff, with no level/XFL
  variation.
- gunzip: input < 18 bytes -> "gzip: bad magic" even with a valid magic. CRC32/ISIZE are not verified.
  inflate: Adler-32 is not verified (dropping the 4-byte trailer still succeeds); input < 6 bytes ->
  "zlib: input too short".
- More zstd messages: "zstd: truncated frame", "zstd: truncated frame header", "zstd: truncated block header",
  "zstd: truncated content checksum", "zstd: content checksum mismatch".
- zlib.constants has 170 keys. Z_NO_FLUSH=0 Z_PARTIAL_FLUSH=1 Z_SYNC_FLUSH=2 Z_FULL_FLUSH=3 Z_FINISH=4 Z_BLOCK=5,
  BROTLI_OPERATION_PROCESS/FLUSH/FINISH/EMIT_METADATA=0/1/2/3, ZSTD_e_continue/flush/end=0/1/2.
  zlib.Z_SYNC_FLUSH (top level) is undefined.

8. NOT TESTED
======================================================================

  > 1 MiB (assumed to be the same RangeError path as gzip); the zlib callback/promise APIs (zlib.gzip(buf, cb)).
