LUMEN (/tmp/orig): node:zlib STREAM CLASSES + CompressionStream / DecompressionStream
Black-box observations only. Outputs are copied verbatim from /tmp/orig unless marked "node:" (Node v18, for comparison).
The scratch scripts that produced them are /tmp/agent_a2/t1.js ... t70.js and demo1-3.js.

======================================================================
0. TL;DR: A MODEL THAT REPRODUCES EVERYTHING OBSERVED
======================================================================
I inferred this from behaviour, not from source. The only names used are ones that show up in error stacks
("at _flush", "at toU8", "at transform", "at flush", "at close").

zlib stream classes. Each one is a DIRECT subclass of the runtime's own require('stream').Transform:

  function make(codecSync) {                    // zlib.gzipSync, zlib.gunzipSync, ...
    return class cls extends Transform {        // note: every class's .name is "cls"
      constructor(opts) { super(opts); this._chunks = []; }
      _transform(chunk, enc, cb) {
        this._chunks.push(typeof chunk === 'string' ? Buffer.from(chunk, enc)
                        : Buffer.isBuffer(chunk) ? chunk      // stored BY REFERENCE (no copy)
                        : Buffer.from(chunk));                // throws for number/null/bool/object
        cb();
      }
      _flush(cb) {
        let out;
        try { out = codecSync(Buffer.concat(this._chunks)); } catch (e) { cb(e); return; }
        this.push(out);                         // exactly ONE chunk, even when it is 0 bytes long
        cb();
      }
    };
  }
  Gzip=gzipSync  Gunzip=gunzipSync  Deflate=deflateSync  Inflate=inflateSync  DeflateRaw=deflateRawSync
  InflateRaw=inflateRawSync  Unzip=unzipSync (gzip ONLY)  BrotliCompress=brotliCompressSync
  BrotliDecompress=brotliDecompressSync  ZstdCompress=zstdCompressSync  ZstdDecompress=zstdDecompressSync
  zlib.createX = (opts) => new X(opts)          // anonymous (name ""), length 1
  (_chunks is never cleared after the flush.)

- Every zlib option is ignored and nothing is validated. Only the base-stream options (objectMode, highWaterMark) have an effect.
- A hand-written `new Transform({transform(c,e,cb){cb()}, flush(cb){...}})` gives the SAME event order and the
  SAME microtask timing as the zlib streams, for success, cb(err) and throw. Reuse the runtime's Transform as-is.
- Stream output is byte-identical to the matching *Sync function applied to the concatenation of all input.
  I checked 66 decompressor cases (outputs and error messages) and every compressor/input combination I ran
  (including multi-chunk writes). There were zero mismatches.

CompressionStream / DecompressionStream. Each is a class with one own property, `_ts = new TransformStream({...})`:
- `readable` and `writable` are prototype getters that return this._ts.readable and this._ts.writable.
- transform(chunk): toU8(chunk) keeps a reference to a view of any ArrayBuffer/ArrayBufferView. Anything else
  throws TypeError "CompressionStream expects BufferSource chunks". This exact text is used by BOTH classes.
- flush(): out = codecSync(concat(chunks)). If out is non-empty, enqueue ONE plain Uint8Array.
  A codec error is rethrown as new TypeError(err.message). Other errors (e.g. RangeError) pass through unchanged.
- Codecs: CS 'gzip'/'deflate'/'deflate-raw' = gzipSync/deflateSync/deflateRawSync.
  DS 'gzip'/'deflate'/'deflate-raw' = gunzipSync/inflateSync/inflateRawSync.
  I checked 54 cases (outputs and messages); there were zero mismatches.

======================================================================
1. zlib STREAM CLASSES: SHAPE
======================================================================
1.1 Exports
- zlib keys, in order: gzipSync,gzip,Gzip,createGzip,gunzipSync,gunzip,Gunzip,createGunzip,deflateSync,deflate,Deflate,
  createDeflate,inflateSync,inflate,Inflate,createInflate,deflateRawSync,deflateRaw,DeflateRaw,createDeflateRaw,
  inflateRawSync,inflateRaw,InflateRaw,createInflateRaw,brotliCompressSync,brotliCompress,BrotliCompress,
  createBrotliCompress,brotliDecompressSync,brotliDecompress,BrotliDecompress,createBrotliDecompress,zstdCompressSync,
  zstdCompress,ZstdCompress,createZstdCompress,zstdDecompressSync,zstdDecompress,ZstdDecompress,createZstdDecompress,
  unzipSync,unzip,Unzip,createUnzip,crc32,constants,codes
- require('node:zlib') === require('zlib').

1.2 Classes (identical for all 11)
  zlib.Gzip: typeof=function name=cls length=1
  new zlib.Gzip() works. zlib.Gzip() -> TypeError: Class constructor cannot be invoked without 'new'
- s.constructor.name === 'cls' (node: 'Gzip').
- s instanceof zlib.Gzip -> true. zlib.createGunzip() instanceof zlib.Gzip -> false.
- zlib.Gzip.prototype.constructor === zlib.Gzip.
- Object.getPrototypeOf(zlib.Gzip) === require('stream').Transform -> true. There is no shared Zlib/ZlibBase class.
- Each class has its own _transform/_flush functions (Gzip.prototype._transform !== Gunzip.prototype._transform).
- Subclassing works: class My extends zlib.Gzip { constructor(o){ super(o); this.mine = true } } round-trips data.
- createGzip etc.: name "", length 1. `new zlib.createGzip()` throws "object is not a constructor".
- Prototype chain, with the own keys of each level:
   cls        [constructor,_transform,_flush]
   Transform  [constructor,_transform,_write,_final]
   Duplex     [constructor,_write,write,_queueBatch,end,cork,uncork,setDefaultEncoding,writableLength,
               writableHighWaterMark,writableObjectMode]
   Readable   [constructor,_read,readableLength,readableHighWaterMark,readableObjectMode,push,read,setEncoding,on,
               addListener,once,resume,pause,isPaused,pipe,unpipe,destroy] + Symbol.asyncIterator
   Stream     [constructor]
   EventEmitter [...the usual 16 methods]
- instanceof: Transform=true Duplex=true Readable=true EventEmitter=true, Writable=FALSE (node: true).
  Object.prototype.toString.call(s) -> "[object Object]".
- Instance own enumerable keys: ["_events","_eventsCount","_maxListeners","_readableState","readable",
  "_writableState","writable","_chunks"]. Own symbol: Symbol(kCapture).
- Initial _readableState: {"flowing":null,"ended":false,"endEmitted":false,"buffer":[],"length":0,"objectMode":false,
  "highWaterMark":65536,"encoding":null,"destroyed":false,"reading":false,"errored":null}
- Initial _writableState: {"ended":false,"finished":false,"destroyed":false,"corked":0,"corkBuffer":[],"errored":null,
  "tail":{},"objectMode":false,"highWaterMark":65536,"length":0,"needDrain":false}
- readableHighWaterMark and writableHighWaterMark are both 65536 (node zlib: 16384).

1.3 APIs that DO NOT EXIST (they are undefined)
- Methods: flush, params, reset, close, unshift, wrap, _destroy, _writev, _processChunk.
- Properties: bytesWritten, bytesRead, _handle, _chunkSize, _level, _strategy, _info, readableEnded, writableEnded,
  writableFinished, destroyed, closed, errored, readableFlowing, allowHalfOpen, writableCorked, writableNeedDrain,
  readableAborted, readableDidRead, readableEncoding, writableBuffer, readableBuffer.
- So calling any of the missing methods throws synchronously:
    s.flush()                                          -> TypeError: (intermediate value).flush is not a function
    s[m]() for m in flush/params/reset/close           -> TypeError: undefined is not a function
  (The text is the engine's generic not-a-function message.) The same happens for s.flush(Z_SYNC_FLUSH, cb) and
  s.flush(cb); the callback is never called.
- Present methods: destroy(len 1), pipe, unpipe, pause, resume, isPaused, setEncoding, on/once/off/emit/...,
  cork, uncork, setDefaultEncoding (a NO-OP, see 3), read, push, write(len 3), end(len 3).
- Flushing mid-way is therefore impossible. With the throwing flush() wrapped in try/catch:
    write('part one '); try{flush()}catch{}; write('part two'); end()
  the output equals gzipSync('part one part two') -> true. node: false, because node emits a sync-flush block.

1.4 Options
- Ignored, with no validation: level (99, -5, 'x', 0, 1, 9 all give identical bytes), chunkSize (1, 'abc'),
  windowBits (100), memLevel (100), strategy (99), dictionary (Deflate output has no FDICT; Inflate ignores it),
  params (brotli quality 1 and 11 give identical output; unknown key 12345 accepted), flush, finishFlush,
  maxOutputLength.
  node throws RangeError/TypeError ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE / ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE / ERR_BROTLI_INVALID_PARAM.
- createGzip(null) -> TypeError: cannot read property 'objectMode' of null (node: accepted).
  createGzip('str') and createGzip(5) are accepted.
- Base-stream options are honoured:
  createGzip({objectMode:true, highWaterMark:5}) -> readableObjectMode=true writableObjectMode=true rHWM=5 wHWM=5.
  createGzip({readableHighWaterMark:7, writableHighWaterMark:9, readableObjectMode:true}) -> rHWM=16 wHWM=65536 rOM=true
  (the split HWM options are ignored).
  objectMode does not change the output (still one Buffer).

======================================================================
2. zlib STREAMS: DATA FLOW, EVENTS, TIMING
======================================================================
2.1 Buffering
- NOTHING is emitted before end(), for compressors as well as decompressors (all 11 checked: 0 'data' events in the
  30 ms after write(), 1 after end()). node emits the gzip header and 16 KiB chunks as it goes.
- After end() there is EXACTLY ONE 'data' chunk (a Buffer) holding the whole output:
    createGzip, 200000 random bytes  -> chunks=1 sizes=[210882]   (node: 14 chunks of 16384...)
    createGzip({chunkSize:1024})     -> chunks=1 sizes=[210882]   (node: 197 chunks of 1024)
    createGzip({highWaterMark:1024}) -> chunks=1 sizes=[210882]
    createGunzip -> 300000-byte output -> chunks=1 sizes=[300000] (node: 19 chunks)
    The same holds for Deflate/DeflateRaw/Brotli*/Zstd*/Inflate*/Unzip.
- Empty output still emits a 0-length 'data' event (node emits none). For example, createGunzip().end(gzipSync(''))
  gives "data(0) end", and the same for Inflate/InflateRaw/Unzip/BrotliDecompress/ZstdDecompress.
  The generic Transform in this runtime also emits 'data' for push(Buffer.alloc(0)).

2.2 Event order (demo1.js)
  const s = zlib.createGzip();
  ['data','end','finish','close','drain','error','prefinish','resume','pause'].forEach(ev => s.on(ev, ...));
  log('write1 -> ' + s.write('hello ', () => log('write1 cb')));
  log('write2 -> ' + s.write('world', () => log('write2 cb')));
  log('end -> this? ' + (s.end(() => log('end cb')) === s));
  process.nextTick(() => log('nextTick')); setTimeout(() => log('timeout0'), 0);
 orig output:
  write1 -> true
  write2 -> true
  end -> this? true
  write1 cb
  write2 cb
  data 31
  end cb
  finish
  end
  nextTick
  timeout0
- NEVER emitted on normal completion: 'close' (only destroy() emits it), 'prefinish', 'resume', 'pause' (not even for
  explicit pause()/resume() calls). node emits resume ... finish, end, close.
- Order: 'data', then the end() callback, then 'finish', then 'end'. node: finish, data, end, close.
- Decompressors behave identically (Gunzip/Inflate trace: write1 cb, write2 cb, data 11, end cb, finish, end).
- Microtask timing (measured against a chain of Promise.resolve().then markers mt1, mt2, ... started before the writes):
    write #0 callback          at mt1
    write #k callback          at mt(1+3k)
    'data' + end cb + 'finish' at 3 hops after the last write callback (mt1 when there were no writes)
    'end'                      1 hop later
  Examples: 0 writes -> data/endcb/finish@mt1, end@mt2. 1 write -> wcb@mt1, data/endcb/finish@mt4, end@mt5.
  3 writes -> wcb@mt1,mt4,mt7, data@mt10, end@mt11. write(x)+end(y) -> wcb@mt1, data@mt7, end@mt8
  (the chunk passed to end() counts as one more write).
  Everything above happens inside microtasks, i.e. before ANY process.nextTick/setImmediate/setTimeout callback queued
  in the same synchronous block. (General runtime quirk: process.nextTick runs like a macrotask, after the microtask
  queue drains and FIFO with setImmediate.)
- The 'readable' event works (paused mode):
    s.on('readable', () => { while ((c = s.read()) !== null) ... }); s.write('hello'); s.end('world')
  gives: "readable read=[30]", "finish", "end". node: readable [10], readable [20], finish, readable [], end, close.
- No consumer at all: 'finish' and the end callback fire, readableLength=30, flowing=null. 'end' fires only after
  s.read() drains the buffer. read(5) and read(100) slice the buffer like node.
- setEncoding works and returns this: 'utf8' -> "string:héllo", 'hex' -> "string:68c3a96c6c6f",
  'base64' -> "string:aMOpbGxv", 'latin1' -> "string:hÃ©llo".
- pause() then end(...): isPaused=true, readableLength=3. resume() delivers data(3) then end.
- 'pipe' event: src.pipe(gz) emits 'pipe' on gz with src as the argument.

2.3 write() / end() return values and backpressure
- write() returns false iff writableLength, after adding the chunk, is >= writableHighWaterMark (65536):
    single write of 65535 bytes -> true; 65536 -> false; 40000 -> true, +25535 -> true, +1 more -> false.
  Strings count by .length (30000 x '€' -> writableLength=30000, returns true). node: 16384 threshold.
- 'drain' is emitted once, 1 microtask after the callback of the write that brought the length back down.
  Writes are "consumed" immediately because they are only buffered.
- end() returns this. end(null), end(undefined), end(''), end(cb), end(chunk, cb) and end('6869','hex',cb) all work;
  end(null) is treated as "no chunk".

2.4 Lifecycle of the state flags (t51.js)
  initial            readable=true  writable=true  rs.flowing=null  rs.ended=false ws.ended=false ws.finished=false
  after on('data')   rs.flowing=true
  after end()        writable=true (node: false)   ws.ended=true
  in 'finish'        readable=false writable=true  rs.flowing=false rs.ended=true rs.endEmitted=true ws.finished=true
  in 'end' and later same as in 'finish'. `writable` stays true forever.
  destroyed/readableEnded/writableEnded/writableFinished/closed/readableFlowing are always undefined.

======================================================================
3. zlib STREAMS: INPUT CHUNK HANDLING
======================================================================
I wrote each value to createGzip(), called end(), then decoded the output with gunzipSync:
  s.write('héllo')               ok, decoded=68c3a96c6c6f (utf8)
  s.write('68656c6c6f','hex')    ok, decoded=68656c6c6f;  'base64' and 'latin1' are also honoured
  s.write(new Uint8Array([104,105]))       ok, 6869 (copied)
  s.write(arrayBuffer)                     ok, 6869 (accepted; node throws ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE)
  s.write(new Uint16Array([0x6968,0x2121])) ok, decoded=6821 (element-wise truncation, Buffer.from(typedArray))
  s.write([104,105])                       ok, 6869 (array accepted)
  s.write(new DataView(...))               ok, but contributes ZERO bytes (decoded=""; Buffer.from(DataView) is empty
                                           in this runtime)
  s.write('') / s.write(Buffer.alloc(0))   ok, no bytes
  s.write(123) / null / undefined / true / {a:1}:
     write() RETURNS true synchronously (node throws TypeError ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE / ERR_STREAM_NULL_VALUES).
     Then stderr shows:  Uncaught (in promise) TypeError: Buffer.from: unsupported value
     No write callback, no 'error' event. The stream STALLS for good: later writes and end() never produce
     'data'/'finish'/'end'. Example state afterwards: writableLength=6 after write(123)+write('abc'),
     ws.ended=true, finished=false. Exit code 0.
  s.write('abc','bogus') -> returns true, then "Uncaught (in promise) TypeError: Unknown encoding: bogus", same stall.
     (node throws synchronously.)
  s.setDefaultEncoding('hex'); s.end('6869') -> decoded=36383639, i.e. utf8. setDefaultEncoding is a no-op.
- Buffers are kept BY REFERENCE until end(): s._chunks[0] === b is true, and mutating b after write() but before end()
  changes the output ("zaaabb"). Uint8Arrays are copied.
- The generic Transform passes chunks through untouched (a string stays a string, enc=undefined unless given).
  The conversion is done in the zlib _transform.

======================================================================
4. zlib STREAMS: ERRORS
======================================================================
4.1 Corrupt, truncated or empty input (demo2.js)
  const s = zlib.createGunzip(); (listeners for data/error/end/finish/close)
  s.write(Buffer.from('not gzip'), err => log('write cb err=' + err)); s.end(() => log('end cb'));
 orig output:
  write cb err=undefined
  error: Error "gzip: bad magic" code=undefined errno=undefined own=["message"]
  end
- Errors are detected ONLY at end(), inside _flush. Writing garbage without calling end() never errors.
- Sequence: write callbacks (success), then 'error', then 'end' 1 microtask later.
  There is NO 'finish', NO end() callback and NO 'close'. node: ... finish, error, close, and no 'end'.
  'end' fires even when the stream is not flowing (no 'data' listener).
- After the error: rs.errored=null, rs.destroyed=false, rs.ended=true, rs.endEmitted=true, ws.finished=false,
  ws.errored=null, readable=false, writable=true.
- Error object: a plain Error (proto === Error.prototype). Own property names: ["message"] only.
  No code, no errno; Object.keys(e) is []. e.stack is a string such as "Error: gzip: bad magic\n    at <anonymous>\n
  at _flush". It is the same object shape as the *Sync error. node: code Z_DATA_ERROR / Z_BUF_ERROR, errno -3/-5,
  node messages "incorrect header check" / "unexpected end of file".
- Per class (input -> stream result). Each message is identical to what the matching *Sync throws:
  Gunzip     corrupt "not gzip data at all!" -> error "gzip: bad magic"
             truncated (first half)          -> error "inflate: unexpected end of input"
             trailing garbage                -> OK, data(780), garbage ignored (node: error "incorrect header check")
             empty / no write                -> error "gzip: bad magic" (node: "unexpected end of file")
             two concatenated members        -> OK, data(780) = FIRST MEMBER ONLY (node: 1560 / "abcdef")
  Inflate    corrupt -> "zlib: unsupported compression method"; truncated -> "inflate: unexpected end of input";
             trailing -> OK 780; empty -> "zlib: input too short"; double -> OK 780 (first stream only)
  InflateRaw corrupt -> "inflate: reserved block type"; truncated -> "inflate: unexpected end of input";
             trailing -> OK 780; empty -> "inflate: unexpected end of input"; double -> OK 780
  Unzip      same as Gunzip. It is GZIP-ONLY: zlib-format (deflateSync) input -> error "gzip: bad magic"
             (node auto-detects). unzipSync(deflateSync('abc')) also throws "gzip: bad magic".
  BrotliDecompress corrupt "not gzip data at all!" -> NO error, data(0) (lax decoder; other garbage gives
             "brotli: non-zero padding bits"); truncated -> "brotli: unexpected end of input";
             trailing -> OK 780; empty -> "brotli: unexpected end of input"; double -> OK 780
  ZstdDecompress corrupt -> "zstd: bad magic number"; truncated -> "zstd: truncated raw block";
             trailing garbage -> ERROR "zstd: bad magic number"; empty -> "zstd: empty input";
             two frames -> OK data(1560), ALL frames decoded
  Dictionary streams (FDICT set, made by node with {dictionary}) -> "inflate: invalid literal/length symbol",
  with or without the dictionary option (node: "Missing dictionary" / success).
  finishFlush: Z_SYNC_FLUSH on truncated input does NOT help: error "inflate: unexpected end of input", output 0
  (node returns the partial output without error).
- Total input > 1 MiB (e.g. 2 x 600000-byte writes): the Buffer.concat in _flush throws, which shows up as
  'error' "RangeError: Invalid typed array length", then 'end'. Every exception thrown inside _flush is routed the
  same way.

4.2 No 'error' listener
  s.write(Buffer.from('not gzip')); s.end(...); (only data/end/finish/close listeners attached)
  stdout: sync done / end / timer still runs
  stderr: Uncaught (in promise) Error: gzip: bad magic
  exit code: 0. The process keeps running. process.on('uncaughtException'/'unhandledRejection') handlers are NOT called.
  The emit('error') throw happens inside a promise job, so it becomes an unhandled rejection.
  node: prints the stack, exit 1.
  (For comparison: a top-level EventEmitter emit('error') without a listener prints "Uncaught Error: y" and exits 1.)

4.3 Write after end, and double end (t22.js)
  s.write('abc'); s.end();
  s.write('def', cb)  -> returns false; cb gets Error "write after end" (code undefined) asynchronously.
                         NO 'error' event. The stream still finishes normally (data(23), finish, end).
  s.end(cb2) again    -> returns this; cb2 is NEVER called.
  later, after finish:
  s.write('ghi', cb)  -> false; cb gets "write after end"; no 'error' event
  s.end('jkl', cb)    -> emits 'error' "write after end" synchronously (returns this when a listener exists). With no
                         listener, end() THROWS "write after end".
  node: the first write-after-end emits 'error' ERR_STREAM_WRITE_AFTER_END, then 'close'.

4.4 destroy() (t10.js). It only destroys the readable side:
  s.write('abc', cb); s.destroy()  -> returns this. Immediately: rs.destroyed=true, ws.destroyed=false, readable=false,
     writable=true. Then: write cb(undefined), 'close'.
     Further write('x', cb) -> returns true, cb(undefined). end() works and emits 'finish' and 'end', but no 'data'.
  s.destroy(new Error('boom'))     -> 'error'(boom), then 'close'. rs.errored=boom. The writable side keeps working.
  destroy() after end()            -> 'close'; a later write() returns false with cb "write after end".
  node: both sides destroyed; later writes fail with "Cannot call write after a stream was destroyed".

======================================================================
5. zlib STREAMS: PIPING, ITERATION, PIPELINE (all work)
======================================================================
- fs.createReadStream(in.txt).pipe(zlib.createGzip()).pipe(fs.createWriteStream(out)): pipe returns dest.
  Events: gz data 11178 (one chunk), ws finish, ws close. The file equals gzipSync(input).
- process.stdin.pipe(zlib.createGzip()).pipe(process.stdout) and the gunzip direction both work; exit code 0.
- for await (const c of gz): 1 chunk, Buffer. When the stream errors the loop throws the Error
  ("for await error case: threw Error: gzip: bad magic").
- stream.pipeline(rs, createGzip(), ws, cb): cb err=null on success (node: undefined).
  With a bad gunzip: cb err="gzip: bad magic". stream.promises.pipeline and require('stream/promises').pipeline exist.
- stream.finished(s, cb) -> err=null on success, err=<the Error> on failure. events.once(s,'end') resolves.
- Readable.from([Buffer,Buffer]).pipe(createGzip()) works.
- gzip.pipe(gunzip), brotli->brotli and zstd->zstd round trips work. Deflate->Unzip fails with "gzip: bad magic".
- pipe() FORWARDS source errors: createGunzip() fed garbage and piped to a Writable makes the destination emit 'error'
  (the SAME error object), then 'close', then 'finish' (dest.end() runs because the source emits 'end').
  If the destination has no error listener: "Uncaught (in promise) Error: gzip: bad magic" on stderr, even when the
  gunzip itself has a listener. node does not forward the error and does not end the destination.
  (This is generic stream behaviour, but it is visible in zlib pipe chains.)
- Side note, codec: the round trip in my pipe test FAILED. gunzipSync(gzipSync(in.txt)) throws "inflate: invalid Huffman
  code", and node cannot decode the file either ("invalid distance code"). See 7.

======================================================================
6. CompressionStream / DecompressionStream
======================================================================
6.1 Shape
- Globals: typeof 'function'. name "CompressionStream" / "DecompressionStream", length 1.
  Property descriptor: writable, ENUMERABLE (node: non-enumerable), configurable.
- prototype own names: ["constructor","readable","writable"]. readable and writable are getters (no setter),
  enumerable=false (node: true), configurable=true. Object.keys(CompressionStream.prototype) -> [].
- Parent is Object. cs instanceof TransformStream -> false.
- Instance: own keys ["_ts"]; cs._ts.constructor.name === 'TransformStream'; cs.readable === cs._ts.readable.
  The getters are stable (same object every time). cs.readable instanceof ReadableStream and
  cs.writable instanceof WritableStream are both true.
- Getter on a foreign object: get.call({}) -> TypeError: cannot read property 'readable' of undefined.
  get.call({_ts:{readable:42}}) -> 42.
- Object.prototype.toString.call(cs) -> "[object Object]"; cs[Symbol.toStringTag] -> undefined;
  JSON.stringify(cs) shows {"_ts":{...}}.
- Called without new: TypeError: Class constructor cannot be invoked without 'new'.
- Subclassing works. A second constructor argument is ignored.

6.2 Format argument: converted with ToString (template-literal semantics), then compared EXACTLY
  Accepted: 'gzip', 'deflate', 'deflate-raw' (node 18 rejects 'deflate-raw'). Also any object whose toString() returns
  one of these: ['gzip'], {toString(){return 'gzip'}}, and {valueOf(){return 'bogus2'}, toString(){return 'gzip'}}
  (toString wins). {valueOf(){return 'deflate-raw'}, toString(){return 'bogus'}} -> rejected with 'bogus'.
  Rejected, with TypeError (not DOMException, no code):
    new CompressionStream('brotli') -> TypeError: Unsupported CompressionStream format: 'brotli'
    'br' -> ...'br'   'zstd' -> ...'zstd'   'GZIP' -> ...'GZIP'   'Gzip'   ' gzip'   'deflate64'   'x-gzip'
    ''        -> TypeError: Unsupported CompressionStream format: ''
    undefined -> ...'undefined'  (no argument gives the same)
    null      -> ...'null'   123 -> ...'123'   {} -> ...'[object Object]'
    Symbol('x') -> TypeError: Cannot convert a Symbol value to a string
    an object whose toString throws RangeError('ts boom') -> that RangeError propagates
  DecompressionStream uses the same texts with "DecompressionStream": "Unsupported DecompressionStream format: 'br'".
  node: TypeError "The argument 'format' is invalid. Received 'br'" code ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE.

6.3 Data flow (demo3.js)
  const cs = new CompressionStream('gzip'); const w = cs.writable.getWriter(), r = cs.readable.getReader();
  log desiredSize; w.write(enc('hello ')); w.write(Uint8Array 'world'); log desiredSize; w.close(); read all
 orig output:
  desiredSize=1
  desiredSize after 2 writes=-1
  write1 resolved
  write2 resolved
  chunk Uint8Array len=31
  done; equals gzipSync: true
  close resolved
- All input is buffered. NO output appears before close(): a pending read() stays unresolved while writes are made
  and only settles after close(). Output is ONE chunk containing everything, as a plain Uint8Array
  (not a Buffer; byteOffset 0; buffer.byteLength == length).
  Examples: 200000 random bytes in 4 writes -> chunks=1 [210840]. DS of a 300000-byte payload written in 23 pieces of
  100 bytes -> chunks=1 [300000]. node: 16 KiB chunks plus an early 10-byte gzip header chunk.
- Bytes are identical to gzipSync/deflateSync/deflateRawSync of the concatenated input. Single-byte chunks give the
  same bytes, and DS with single-byte input chunks round-trips correctly.
- Writer: initial desiredSize=1 (HWM 1, every chunk counts 1). It drops by 1 per write and can go negative (-1, -2).
  writer.ready is ALWAYS already resolved, even at desiredSize <= 0. Write promises resolve whether or not anyone reads.
- close() resolves even with NO reader attached. The chunk waits in the readable; a reader attached later
  (setTimeout 5 ms) gets the chunk, then done.
- Microtask timing (single write, then close, measured like 2.2):
  writer.ready resolves at mt1, write() at mt5, a pending read() with the chunk at mt6, read #2 {done:true} and
  reader.closed at mt7, writer.closed then the close() promise at mt9 ('closed' settles BEFORE close(); node is the
  other way round). Everything finishes before nextTick/timers.
- Input chunks are kept BY REFERENCE until close(): mutating a written Uint8Array or ArrayBuffer before close changes
  the output ("zaa"). (Buffer.from(arrayBuffer) COPIES in this runtime, so a Buffer built that way is not affected.)
- Works: custom ReadableStream.pipeThrough(cs) (1 chunk), .pipeTo(new WritableStream(...)),
  for await over cs.readable (1 Uint8Array), blob.stream().pipeThrough(cs) read with a reader,
  ds.readable.pipeThrough(new TextDecoderStream()) ("décodé").
- Response LIMITATION: the body is consumed SYNCHRONOUSLY at arrayBuffer()/text() time.
    await new Response(new Blob(['abc']).stream().pipeThrough(new CompressionStream('gzip'))).arrayBuffer()
      -> rejects: TypeError: a body ReadableStream must produce its data synchronously in this runtime
         (the Response constructor itself succeeds; the rejection comes from arrayBuffer())
    w.write(x); w.close(); await new Response(cs.readable).arrayBuffer()        -> the same TypeError
    const p = w.close(); const resp = new Response(cs.readable); await p; await resp.arrayBuffer() -> OK (25 bytes)
    After `await w.close()`, new Response(cs.readable).arrayBuffer() -> OK, equals gzipSync
    new Response(new Blob(['xyz']).stream()).arrayBuffer() -> OK
  node: all of these work. (fetch('data:...') -> TypeError: fetch: unsupported scheme 'data'.)

6.4 Chunk types for writer.write() (both classes)
  Accepted (bytes of the VIEW are used): Uint8Array, Buffer, ArrayBuffer, DataView (offset/length honoured),
    Int8Array, Int16Array([0x6968]) -> bytes 68 69, Float64Array([1.5]) -> 000000000000f83f, subarray views.
    node 18 accepts only Buffer/Uint8Array (and strings).
  Rejected: string, number, null, undefined, plain object, Array, SharedArrayBuffer. In every case:
    write() promise rejects: TypeError: CompressionStream expects BufferSource chunks
      (DecompressionStream uses the SAME text "CompressionStream expects ...". Own props ["message"];
       stack "at toU8 / at transform / at write")
    close() rejects with the same TypeError. writable._state='errored'. writer.desiredSize=null.
    Further write() calls reject with the same error.
    The readable is NOT errored: readable._state stays 'readable' and reader.read() NEVER settles (hangs).
    Through pipeThrough, the read() also hangs.

6.5 Decompression errors (DecompressionStream)
  ds.writable.getWriter().write(new Uint8Array([1,2,3])) -> resolves
  await w.close() -> rejects: TypeError: gzip: bad magic
  ds.readable.getReader().read() -> still pending after 100ms
- The error surfaces ONLY as the rejection of writer.close(), as a TypeError carrying the codec message
  (own props ["message"], no cause; stack "at flush / at close"). write() promises resolve. A directly held
  reader.read() HANGS forever; writer.closed and reader.closed never settle.
- State afterwards: writable._state='writable' (!), readable._state='readable', desiredSize=1, writer.ready resolved.
  A further write() RESOLVES, and a second close() rejects again with the same TypeError.
- Through pipes: readable.pipeThrough(new DecompressionStream('gzip')).getReader().read() REJECTS with the TypeError,
  for-await throws it, and rs.pipeTo(ds.writable) rejects with it.
- Messages (identical to *Sync, but as TypeError): 'gzip' corrupt or empty -> "gzip: bad magic"; truncated ->
  "inflate: unexpected end of input". 'deflate' corrupt -> "zlib: unsupported compression method"; empty or <6 bytes ->
  "zlib: input too short". 'deflate-raw' corrupt -> "inflate: invalid Huffman code"; empty ->
  "inflate: unexpected end of input".
  node: Error "incorrect header check" with code Z_DATA_ERROR, readable errored too.
- Trailing garbage after a valid stream -> NO error, output = first stream. Two concatenated gzip members -> first only.
- Total input > 1 MiB -> close() rejects with RangeError: Invalid typed array length (NOT converted to TypeError).
- writer.abort(new Error('my abort')) -> resolves; writable and readable both 'errored'; read() rejects with that Error.
- reader.cancel(err) -> resolves; readable 'closed', writable stays 'writable'. write() still resolves, but close()
  rejects with TypeError: stream is not in a readable state.

6.6 Edge cases
- Empty input (no writes, or one empty write). CS gives ONE chunk:
    gzip        1f8b08000000000000ff03000000000000000000 (20 bytes; OS byte 0xff, node 0x03)
    deflate     789c030000000001
    deflate-raw 0300
  DS of those empty streams -> ZERO chunks, then done (no empty Uint8Array is enqueued; contrast with 2.1).
- Double close: w.close(); w.close() made synchronously -> BOTH resolve, and the readable then yields the compressed
  output TWICE (2 identical 21-byte chunks), then done. Calling close() after the stream is closed rejects:
  TypeError: stream is not in a readable state. write() after a successful close RESOLVES.
- Second getWriter() -> TypeError: WritableStream is already locked.
  Second getReader() -> TypeError: stream is already locked to a reader.

======================================================================
7. SIDE NOTES ON THE SHARED CODECS (affect the stream output too)
======================================================================
- The deflate ENCODER is buggy for match distances > 32768. A repeat at distance 32768 round-trips; at 32769 or 40000
  the original's inflate says "inflate: unexpected end of input", and at 65536 or 70000
  "inflate: invalid literal/length symbol". node rejects the same bytes. My 73893-byte text file
  ("line of text number N\n" x3000) fails from a 34240-byte prefix on.
- Compressed sizes are not zlib's: gzip of 200000 random bytes = 210882 bytes; brotli and zstd of small inputs are
  stored or raw; zstd of 22500 repetitive bytes = 22514 bytes. The gzip header OS byte is 0xff, with no level/XFL
  variation.
- gunzip: input < 18 bytes -> "gzip: bad magic" even with a valid magic. CRC32/ISIZE are not verified.
  inflate: Adler-32 is not verified (dropping the 4-byte trailer still succeeds); input < 6 bytes ->
  "zlib: input too short".
- More zstd messages: "zstd: truncated frame", "zstd: truncated frame header", "zstd: truncated block header",
  "zstd: truncated content checksum", "zstd: content checksum mismatch".
- zlib.constants has 170 keys. Z_NO_FLUSH=0 Z_PARTIAL_FLUSH=1 Z_SYNC_FLUSH=2 Z_FULL_FLUSH=3 Z_FINISH=4 Z_BLOCK=5,
  BROTLI_OPERATION_PROCESS/FLUSH/FINISH/EMIT_METADATA=0/1/2/3, ZSTD_e_continue/flush/end=0/1/2.
  zlib.Z_SYNC_FLUSH (top level) is undefined.

======================================================================
8. NOT TESTED
======================================================================
- zlib streams: Readable.toWeb/Duplex.toWeb/stream.compose on zlib streams; cork()/uncork() interaction; early
  break out of for-await (destroy semantics); exact microtask timing of destroy(); brotli/zstd with total input
  > 1 MiB (assumed to be the same RangeError path as gzip); the zlib callback/promise APIs (zlib.gzip(buf, cb)).
- Web streams: BYOB readers; TransformStream strategies; writer.releaseLock() mid-stream; detached ArrayBuffers;
  very large (> 900 KB) DecompressionStream outputs.

# Random VALID streams from the crafting encoder; compare orig vs node vs expected.
import sys, random, json
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/agent_b')
from enc import *

def rand_cmap(rng, n, ntrees):
    if ntrees == 1: return [0] * n
    mode = rng.random()
    if mode < 0.3: return [rng.randrange(ntrees) for _ in range(n)]
    if mode < 0.6:  # mostly zeros with runs
        return [0 if rng.random() < 0.8 else rng.randrange(ntrees) for _ in range(n)]
    # blocky
    out = []
    while len(out) < n:
        out += [rng.randrange(ntrees)] * rng.randint(1, 20)
    return out[:n]

def gen_mb(rng, st, islast, big=False):
    npostfix = rng.choice([0, 0, 1, 2, 3])
    ndirect = rng.choice([0, 0, rng.randint(0, 15)]) << npostfix
    nbl = [rng.choice([1, 1, 2, 3, rng.randint(2, 6)]) for _ in range(3)]
    if big and rng.random() < 0.3: nbl[rng.randrange(3)] = rng.choice([128, 255, 256])
    cmodes = [rng.randrange(4) for _ in range(nbl[0])]
    ntreesl = rng.choice([1, 1, 2, 3, rng.randint(1, 8)])
    ntreesd = rng.choice([1, 1, 2, rng.randint(1, 5)])
    cmapl = rand_cmap(rng, 64 * nbl[0], ntreesl)
    cmapd = rand_cmap(rng, 4 * nbl[2], ntreesd)
    cmapl_opts = dict(rlemax=rng.choice([0, 0, 1, 3, 6, 16]), imtf=rng.random() < 0.4)
    cmapd_opts = dict(rlemax=rng.choice([0, 0, 2, 5]), imtf=rng.random() < 0.4)
    # commands
    cmds = []
    ncmd = rng.randint(1, 12)
    # simulate to pick valid distances: need State copy
    sim = State(st.wbits); sim.out = bytearray(st.out); sim.rb = list(st.rb)
    produced = 0
    alphabet = rng.choice([b'abc', b'abcdefghij', bytes(range(256)), b'the quick brown fox ', b'\x00\x01\xff\x80'])
    for i in range(ncmd):
        ins = bytes(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(rng.choice([0, 1, 2, 5, rng.randint(0, 40)])))
        sim.out += ins; produced += len(ins)
        last = (i == ncmd - 1)
        if last and rng.random() < 0.3 and ins:
            cmds.append(dict(ins=ins, copy=4, dist=None))
            break
        md = sim.max_dist()
        r = rng.random()
        if md >= 1 and r < 0.65:
            cp = rng.choice([2, 3, 4, 5, rng.randint(2, 40), rng.randint(2, 300)])
            # prefer recent distances sometimes
            cands = [d for d in sim.rb if 1 <= d <= md]
            if cands and rng.random() < 0.4:
                d = rng.choice(cands) + rng.choice([0, 0, -1, 1, 2, -2, 3, -3])
                d = max(1, min(md, d))
            else:
                d = rng.randint(1, md)
            implicit = (d == sim.rb[0]) and rng.random() < 0.5
            cmds.append(dict(ins=ins, copy=cp, dist=None if implicit else d))
            for _ in range(cp): sim.out.append(sim.out[-d])
            produced += cp
            dc = 0 if implicit else sim.find_dcode(d, npostfix, ndirect)[0]
            if dc != 0: sim.rb = [d] + sim.rb[:3]
        else:
            # dictionary reference
            cp = rng.randint(4, 24)
            while True:
                idx = rng.randrange(1 << NDBITS[cp]); t = rng.randrange(121)
                w = transform(dict_word(cp, idx), t)
                if len(w) > 0: break
            d = md + 1 + (idx | (t << NDBITS[cp]))
            cmds.append(dict(ins=ins, copy=cp, dist=d))
            sim.out += w; produced += len(w)
    mlen = produced
    if mlen == 0:
        cmds = [dict(ins=b'z', copy=4, dist=None)]; mlen = 1
    # blocks: counts per category from symbol usage is complicated -> random splits with large final block
    def rand_blocks(n):
        if n == 1: return None
        bl = [(0, rng.randint(1, 6))]
        prev = [1, 0]
        for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 8)):
            bl.append((rng.randrange(n), rng.randint(1, 6)))
        bl.append((rng.randrange(n), 1 << 20))
        return bl
    blocks = tuple(rand_blocks(n) for n in nbl)
    compressed_mb(bw_holder[0], st, mlen, cmds, islast=islast, nbl=tuple(nbl), blocks=blocks, npostfix=npostfix, ndirect=ndirect,
                  cmodes=cmodes, ntreesl=ntreesl, cmapl=cmapl, cmapl_opts=cmapl_opts, ntreesd=ntreesd, cmapd=cmapd,
                  cmapd_opts=cmapd_opts)

bw_holder = [None]
def gen_stream(rng):
    w = rng.choice([10, 11, 12, 16, 17, 18, 22, 24])
    bw, st = new_stream(w)
    bw_holder[0] = bw
    nmb = rng.randint(1, 4)
    for i in range(nmb):
        last = (i == nmb - 1)
        r = rng.random()
        if r < 0.12 and not last:
            data = bytes(rng.randrange(256) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 30)))
            uncompressed(bw, data); st.out += data
        elif r < 0.2 and not last:
            metadata(bw, bytes(rng.randrange(256) for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 10))))
        else:
            gen_mb(rng, st, islast=last and rng.random() < 0.7, big=rng.random() < 0.2)
    if not last or True:
        # if last generated block wasn't islast, close stream
        pass
    return bw, st

if __name__ == '__main__':
    seed0 = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 1
    n = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 100
    cases = []; expects = []
    for k in range(n):
        rng = random.Random(seed0 * 100000 + k)
        bw, st = gen_stream(rng)
        # ensure termination: append last-empty if needed (harmless if a previous islast exists? no -> check bits)
        b = bw.bytes()
        # we can't easily know whether last mb was islast; decode with ref to see; else append last_empty
        r = run_ref(b)
        if not r['ok']:
            bw.put(1, 1); bw.put(1, 1); b = bw.bytes()
        cases.append(('fuzz_%d_%d' % (seed0, k), b)); expects.append(bytes(st.out))
    o = run_orig(cases); nd = run_node(cases)
    bad = 0
    for (name, b), ro, rn, ex in zip(cases, o, nd, expects):
        okn = rn['ok'] and rn['out_hex'] == ex.hex()
        oko = ro['ok'] and ro['out_hex'] == ex.hex()
        if not (okn and oko):
            bad += 1
            print(name, 'len', len(b), 'node', fmt(rn, 40), '| orig', fmt(ro, 40), '| expected len', len(ex))
    print('done', n, 'bad', bad)

        if norm == counts[:len(norm)] and nb == len(d):

steps.message:
I tested all 11 zlib stream classes and both web stream classes. Below is the full report; it is also saved as `/tmp/agent_a2/REPORT.txt`. The scripts that produced the outputs are `/tmp/agent_a2/t1.js` … `t70.js` and `demo1-3.js`. Outputs are copied exactly from `/tmp/orig` unless marked "node:".

The biggest thing to know: every class (zlib streams and CompressionStream/DecompressionStream) buffers all input. It runs the matching `*Sync` codec once at `end()`/`close()` and emits exactly one output chunk. That output is byte-identical to the `*Sync` result.

# 0. Model that reproduces everything observed

I inferred this from behaviour, not from source. The only names used are ones that appear in error stacks ("at _flush", "at toU8", "at transform", "at flush", "at close").

**zlib streams.** Each class is a direct subclass of the runtime's own `stream.Transform`:
```js
function make(codecSync) {                    // zlib.gzipSync, zlib.gunzipSync, ...
  return class cls extends Transform {        // every class's .name is "cls"
    constructor(opts) { super(opts); this._chunks = []; }
    _transform(chunk, enc, cb) {
      this._chunks.push(typeof chunk === 'string' ? Buffer.from(chunk, enc)
                      : Buffer.isBuffer(chunk) ? chunk      // stored BY REFERENCE
                      : Buffer.from(chunk));                // throws for number/null/bool/object
      cb();
    }
    _flush(cb) {
      let out;
      try { out = codecSync(Buffer.concat(this._chunks)); } catch (e) { cb(e); return; }
      this.push(out);   // exactly ONE chunk, even when 0 bytes long
      cb();
    }
  };
}
```
- **Codec per class:**
  - Gzip=`gzipSync`, Gunzip=`gunzipSync`, Deflate=`deflateSync`, Inflate=`inflateSync`
  - DeflateRaw=`deflateRawSync`, InflateRaw=`inflateRawSync`
  - Unzip=`unzipSync`, which is **gzip only**
  - BrotliCompress, BrotliDecompress, ZstdCompress and ZstdDecompress follow the same pattern.
- **Factories:** `createX = (opts) => new X(opts)`. They are anonymous (name `""`), length 1. `_chunks` is never cleared after the flush.
- **Options:** every zlib option is ignored and nothing is validated. Only `objectMode` and `highWaterMark` (read by the base stream) have any effect.
- **Timing comes from the base class:** a hand-written `new Transform({transform(c,e,cb){cb()}, flush(cb){...})` gives the same events and the same microtask timing, for success, `cb(err)` and throw. Reuse the runtime's Transform as-is.
- **Output matches Sync:** I compared stream output with `*Sync` output in 66 decompressor cases (outputs and error messages) and every compressor/input combination I ran, including multi-chunk writes. There were no mismatches.

**CompressionStream / DecompressionStream.** Each is a class with one own property, `_ts = new TransformStream(...)`.
- `readable` and `writable` are prototype getters returning `this._ts.readable` / `this._ts.writable`.
- **transform(chunk):** `toU8(chunk)` keeps a reference to any ArrayBuffer or ArrayBufferView. Anything else throws `TypeError "CompressionStream expects BufferSource chunks"`. Both classes use this exact text.
- **flush():** runs the Sync codec on the concatenated chunks. If the result is non-empty it enqueues **one** plain `Uint8Array`.
  - A codec error is rethrown as `new TypeError(err.message)`.
  - Other errors (e.g. RangeError) pass through unchanged.
- **Codec mapping:**
  - CS: `'gzip'`/`'deflate'`/`'deflate-raw'` = `gzipSync`/`deflateSync`/`deflateRawSync`.
  - DS: the same formats = `gunzipSync`/`inflateSync`/`inflateRawSync`.
  - I checked 54 cases with no mismatches.

# 1. zlib classes: shape

**Classes (identical for all 11).**
- `zlib.Gzip`: typeof function, `name=cls`, `length=1`.
- `new zlib.Gzip()` works. Calling `zlib.Gzip()` throws `TypeError: Class constructor cannot be invoked without 'new'`.
- `s.constructor.name === 'cls'` (node: `'Gzip'`).
- `s instanceof zlib.Gzip` is true, but `createGunzip() instanceof zlib.Gzip` is false.
- `Object.getPrototypeOf(zlib.Gzip) === require('stream').Transform` is true. There is no Zlib/ZlibBase class.
- Subclassing `class My extends zlib.Gzip` works.
- `new zlib.createGzip()` throws "object is not a constructor".

**Prototype chain (own keys per level).**
```
cls        [constructor,_transform,_flush]
Transform  [constructor,_transform,_write,_final]
Duplex     [constructor,_write,write,_queueBatch,end,cork,uncork,setDefaultEncoding,writableLength,
            writableHighWaterMark,writableObjectMode]
Readable   [constructor,_read,readableLength,readableHighWaterMark,readableObjectMode,push,read,setEncoding,
            on,addListener,once,resume,pause,isPaused,pipe,unpipe,destroy] + Symbol.asyncIterator
Stream     [constructor]
EventEmitter
```
- `instanceof`: Transform, Duplex, Readable and EventEmitter are true. **Writable is false** (node: true).
- `Object.prototype.toString.call(s)` gives `[object Object]`.

**Instance state.**
- Own keys: `["_events","_eventsCount","_maxListeners","_readableState","readable","_writableState","writable","_chunks"]`, plus `Symbol(kCapture)`.
- Initial `_readableState`:
  `{"flowing":null,"ended":false,"endEmitted":false,"buffer":[],"length":0,"objectMode":false,"highWaterMark":65536,"encoding":null,"destroyed":false,"reading":false,"errored":null}`
- Initial `_writableState`:
  `{"ended":false,"finished":false,"destroyed":false,"corked":0,"corkBuffer":[],"errored":null,"tail":{},"objectMode":false,"highWaterMark":65536,"length":0,"needDrain":false}`
- Both high-water marks are 65536 (node zlib: 16384).

**Missing APIs (all undefined).**
- Methods: `flush`, `params`, `reset`, `close`, `unshift`, `wrap`, `_destroy`, `_writev`.
- Properties: `bytesWritten`, `bytesRead`, `_handle`, `readableEnded`, `writableEnded`, `writableFinished`, `destroyed`, `closed`, `errored`, `readableFlowing`, `allowHalfOpen`, `writableCorked`, `writableNeedDrain`.
- So `s.flush()` throws `TypeError: (intermediate value).flush is not a function`, and `s[m]()` throws `TypeError: undefined is not a function`. The callback in `flush(kind, cb)` is never called.
- Because `flush()` throws, flushing mid-stream is impossible. With the throw caught (`write('part one '); try{flush()}catch{}; write('part two'); end()`), the output equals `gzipSync('part one part two')` (node: differs).

**Options.**
- These are all accepted, ignored and give identical bytes: `level` (99, -5, `'x'`, 0, 1, 9), `chunkSize` (1, `'abc'`), `windowBits:100`, `memLevel:100`, `strategy:99`, `dictionary`, brotli `params` (quality 1 vs 11, unknown key 12345), `flush`, `finishFlush`, `maxOutputLength`. Node would throw ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE, ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE or ERR_BROTLI_INVALID_PARAM.
- `createGzip(null)` throws `TypeError: cannot read property 'objectMode' of null`. `createGzip('str')` and `createGzip(5)` are fine.
- `{objectMode:true, highWaterMark:5}` gives both object modes true and both HWMs 5.
- `{readableHighWaterMark:7, writableHighWaterMark:9, readableObjectMode:true}` gives rHWM=16, wHWM=65536 (the split options are ignored).

# 2. zlib streams: data flow and timing

**Buffering.**
- Nothing is emitted before `end()`. I checked all 11 classes: no `'data'` in 30 ms after `write()`, exactly one after `end()`. Node emits the gzip header and 16 KiB chunks as it goes.
- After `end()` there is exactly one Buffer `'data'` chunk, whatever the size or options:

| Stream | Result (node for comparison) |
|---|---|
| `createGzip`, 200000 random bytes | `chunks=1 sizes=[210882]` (node: 14 × 16384…) |
| `createGzip({chunkSize:1024})` | `[210882]` (node: 197 × 1024) |
| `createGzip({highWaterMark:1024})` | `[210882]` |
| `createGunzip`, 300 KB output | `[300000]` |

- Empty output still emits a 0-length `'data'` event (node emits none). For example, `createGunzip().end(gzipSync(''))` gives `data(0) end`. This holds for every decompressor.

**Event order (demo1.js).** Three writes/ends, then `process.nextTick` and `setTimeout(0)`:
```
write1 -> true
write2 -> true
end -> this? true
write1 cb
write2 cb
data 31
end cb
finish
end
nextTick
timeout0
```
- Never emitted on normal completion: `'close'` (only `destroy()` emits it), `'prefinish'`, `'resume'`, `'pause'` (not even for explicit `pause()`/`resume()`).
- Node's order is finish, data, end, close.
- Decompressors give the same trace.

**Microtask timing.** Measured against a chain of `Promise.resolve().then` markers mt1, mt2, … started before the writes:
- Write callback #k runs at mt(1+3k).
- `'data'`, the end callback and `'finish'` run 3 hops after the last write callback (mt1 if there were no writes).
- `'end'` runs 1 hop after that.
- Examples:
  - 0 writes: data/endcb/finish at mt1, end at mt2.
  - 1 write: callback at mt1, data at mt4, end at mt5.
  - 3 writes: callbacks at mt1, mt4, mt7; data at mt10; end at mt11.
  - `write(x)` + `end(y)`: data at mt7.
- All of this runs before any nextTick, setImmediate or timer callback. (Runtime quirk: `process.nextTick` behaves like a macrotask, FIFO with setImmediate.)

**Other reading modes.**
- **`'readable'` mode:** with `write('hello'); end('world')` you get `readable read=[30]`, `finish`, `end`.
- **No consumer:** `'finish'` and the end callback fire, `readableLength=30`. `'end'` fires only after `read()`. `read(5)` and `read(100)` slice like node.
- **`setEncoding`** works and returns `this`. utf8 gives `"string:héllo"`, hex `"string:68c3a96c6c6f"`, base64 `"string:aMOpbGxv"`, latin1 `"string:hÃ©llo"`.
- **`pause()`/`resume()`** buffer and release data normally.
- **`'pipe'` event:** `src.pipe(gz)` emits it on `gz`.

**Return values and backpressure.**
- `write()` returns false exactly when writableLength (after adding the chunk) reaches 65536:
  - a single 65535-byte write returns true; 65536 returns false;
  - 40000 then 25535 return true, true; one more byte returns false.
- Strings count by `.length` (30000 × `'€'` gives writableLength 30000).
- `'drain'` fires once, one microtask after the write callback that brings the length below the HWM.
- `end()` returns `this`. `end(null)`, `end(undefined)`, `end('')`, `end(cb)`, `end(chunk, cb)` and `end('6869','hex',cb)` all work.

**State flags.**
- After `end()`, `writable` stays true (node: false).
- Inside `'finish'`, `readable` is already false and `rs.ended`/`rs.endEmitted`/`ws.finished` are true.
- `writable` stays true forever.

# 3. zlib input chunks

| Write | Result (decoded with gunzipSync) |
|---|---|
| `'héllo'` | `68c3a96c6c6f` (utf8) |
| `'68656c6c6f','hex'` | `68656c6c6f`; base64 and latin1 are also honoured |
| `Uint8Array [104,105]` | `6869` (copied) |
| ArrayBuffer | `6869` (node throws) |
| `Uint16Array [0x6968,0x2121]` | `6821` (element-wise truncation) |
| Array `[104,105]` | `6869` |
| DataView | **zero bytes** |
| `''` / empty Buffer | no bytes |

**Invalid chunks** (`123`, `null`, `undefined`, `true`, `{}`):
- `write()` returns **true** synchronously. Node throws ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE or ERR_STREAM_NULL_VALUES.
- stderr then shows `Uncaught (in promise) TypeError: Buffer.from: unsupported value`.
- There is no write callback and no `'error'` event.
- The stream **stalls for good**: no data, finish or end ever arrives. Exit code is 0.

**Other input behaviour.**
- `write('abc','bogus')` behaves the same way: `Uncaught (in promise) TypeError: Unknown encoding: bogus`, then a stall.
- `setDefaultEncoding('hex')` is a no-op: `end('6869')` decodes to `36383639`.
- Buffers are stored by reference. `_chunks[0] === b`, and mutating `b` before `end()` changes the output.

# 4. zlib errors

**Corrupt input (demo2.js):**
```js
s = zlib.createGunzip(); s.write(Buffer.from('not gzip'), cb); s.end(endcb)
```
```
write cb err=undefined
error: Error "gzip: bad magic" code=undefined errno=undefined own=["message"]
end
```
- Errors are detected only at `end()`. Writing garbage without `end()` never errors.
- Sequence: write callbacks, then `'error'`, then `'end'` one microtask later. There is **no** `'finish'`, no end callback and no `'close'`. `'end'` fires even with no `'data'` listener.
- Node's sequence is finish, error, close, with no `'end'`.
- **State afterwards:** `rs.errored=null`, `rs.destroyed=false`, `rs.ended=true`, `rs.endEmitted=true`, `ws.finished=false`.
- **Error object:** a plain Error with own property names `["message"]` only, no code/errno. The stack includes `at _flush`.

| Class | corrupt | truncated | trailing garbage | empty | 2 concatenated |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Gunzip | `gzip: bad magic` | `inflate: unexpected end of input` | OK, garbage ignored (node errors) | `gzip: bad magic` | **first member only** (node: both) |
| Inflate | `zlib: unsupported compression method` | `inflate: unexpected end of input` | OK | `zlib: input too short` | first only |
| InflateRaw | `inflate: reserved block type` | `inflate: unexpected end of input` | OK | `inflate: unexpected end of input` | first only |
| Unzip | same as Gunzip | same | same | same | same |
| BrotliDecompress | `"not gzip data at all!"` gives **no error, data(0)** (other garbage: `brotli: non-zero padding bits`) | `brotli: unexpected end of input` | OK | `brotli: unexpected end of input` | first only |
| ZstdDecompress | `zstd: bad magic number` | `zstd: truncated raw block` | **error** `zstd: bad magic number` | `zstd: empty input` | **all frames** |

- Unzip does not auto-detect. zlib-format input gives `gzip: bad magic`.
- Streams with a preset dictionary (FDICT) give `inflate: invalid literal/length symbol`, with or without the `dictionary` option.
- `finishFlush: Z_SYNC_FLUSH` on truncated input still errors.
- Total input over 1 MiB fails in `_flush`: `'error'` with `RangeError: Invalid typed array length`, then `'end'`.

**No `'error'` listener.**
- stderr shows `Uncaught (in promise) Error: gzip: bad magic`.
- The exit code is **0** and the process keeps running.
- `process.on('uncaughtException')` and `process.on('unhandledRejection')` are not called.

**Write after end.**
- **Write before finish:** `write()` returns false and its callback gets Error `"write after end"`. No `'error'` event; the stream finishes normally.
- **Second `end(cb)`:** returns `this`; `cb` is never called.
- **`end('jkl')` after finish:** emits `'error'` `"write after end"` synchronously. With no listener, `end()` throws.

**`destroy()` only destroys the readable side.**
- Right after `destroy()`: `rs.destroyed=true`, `ws.destroyed=false`, `readable=false`, `writable=true`. `'close'` fires asynchronously.
- Later writes still return true with a successful callback. `end()` still emits `'finish'` and `'end'`, but no `'data'`.
- `destroy(err)` emits `'error'`, then `'close'`.

# 5. Piping and iteration (all work)

- **File pipe:** `fs.createReadStream(f).pipe(createGzip()).pipe(fs.createWriteStream(o))` emits one gz `'data'` chunk, then ws finish, then ws close. The file equals `gzipSync`.
- **stdin/stdout:** piping `process.stdin` through gzip and gunzip to `process.stdout` works.
- **Async iteration:** `for await` yields one Buffer and throws the Error on corrupt input.
- **pipeline:** `stream.pipeline` callback gets `err=null` on success (node: undefined) and `"gzip: bad magic"` on failure. `stream.promises.pipeline` and `require('stream/promises')` exist.
- **Other helpers:** `stream.finished` works, `events.once(s,'end')` works, and `Readable.from([...]).pipe(createGzip())` works.
- **pipe forwards source errors:** if a gunzip piped into a Writable fails, the destination emits `'error'` with the same object, then `'close'`, then `'finish'`. If the destination has no listener you get `Uncaught (in promise) Error: ...`. Node does neither.

# 6. CompressionStream / DecompressionStream

**Shape.**
- `name` is `"CompressionStream"` / `"DecompressionStream"`, length 1. The global is **enumerable** (node: not).
- Prototype keys are `["constructor","readable","writable"]`. Both are getters: non-enumerable (node: enumerable), configurable.
- The instance's own keys are `["_ts"]`; `_ts` is a TransformStream. `cs instanceof TransformStream` is false.
- `cs.readable instanceof ReadableStream` and `cs.writable instanceof WritableStream` are true, and the getters return the same object every time.
- Calling a getter on a foreign object `{}` throws `TypeError: cannot read property 'readable' of undefined`.
- `Object.prototype.toString.call(cs)` gives `[object Object]`. There is no `Symbol.toStringTag`.
- Calling without `new` throws `TypeError: Class constructor cannot be invoked without 'new'`.
- Subclassing works; a second constructor argument is ignored.

**Format argument.**
- It is converted with ToString (template-literal semantics), then compared exactly.
- **Accepted:** `'gzip'`, `'deflate'`, `'deflate-raw'` (node 18 rejects `'deflate-raw'`). So are `['gzip']` and any object whose `toString()` returns one of them. `toString` wins over `valueOf`.
- **Rejected:** throws a TypeError (not a DOMException, no code):
  - `'brotli'` gives `TypeError: Unsupported CompressionStream format: 'brotli'`.
  - `'br'`, `'zstd'`, `'GZIP'`, `'Gzip'`, `' gzip'`, `'deflate64'`, `'x-gzip'` and `''` give the same message with the value in quotes.
  - `undefined` or no argument gives `'undefined'`; `null` gives `'null'`; `123` gives `'123'`; `{}` gives `'[object Object]'`.
  - `Symbol()` gives `TypeError: Cannot convert a Symbol value to a string`.
  - A throwing `toString` propagates its own error.
- DecompressionStream uses the same text with its own name, e.g. `Unsupported DecompressionStream format: 'br'`.

**Data flow (demo3.js):**
```
desiredSize=1
desiredSize after 2 writes=-1
write1 resolved
write2 resolved
chunk Uint8Array len=31
done; equals gzipSync: true
close resolved
```
- No output appears before `close()`; a pending `read()` only settles after close. Then you get one plain `Uint8Array` (not a Buffer, byteOffset 0).
  - 200 KB written in 4 writes gives 1 chunk of `[210840]`.
  - A DecompressionStream with a 300 KB result gives 1 chunk of `[300000]`.
- Bytes equal `gzipSync`/`deflateSync`/`deflateRawSync`; single-byte writes give the same bytes.
- **Writer behaviour:**
  - The HWM is 1. `desiredSize` drops by one per write and goes negative.
  - `writer.ready` is always already resolved.
  - `write()` resolves even with no reader.
  - `close()` resolves even with no reader; a reader attached later still gets the chunk.
- **Microtask timing:** `ready` at mt1, `write` at mt5, pending read at mt6, done read and `reader.closed` at mt7, `writer.closed` then `close()` at mt9.
- Input chunks are kept by reference until close, so mutating them changes the output.
- **What works:** `pipeThrough`, `pipeTo`, `for await`, `blob.stream().pipeThrough(cs)` read with a reader, and `ds.readable.pipeThrough(new TextDecoderStream())`.

**Response limitation.** Response reads its body synchronously when `arrayBuffer()`/`text()` is called:
- `await new Response(blob.stream().pipeThrough(new CompressionStream('gzip'))).arrayBuffer()` rejects with `TypeError: a body ReadableStream must produce its data synchronously in this runtime`.
  - The rejection comes from `arrayBuffer()`, not the constructor.
- The same happens for `w.write(x); w.close(); new Response(cs.readable).arrayBuffer()`.
- It works if `close()` has been awaited first.

**Chunk types for `writer.write()` (both classes).**
- **Accepted:** Uint8Array, Buffer, ArrayBuffer, DataView (offset honoured), Int8Array, Int16Array, Float64Array and subarrays. The view's bytes are used.
- **Rejected** (string, number, null, undefined, object, Array, SharedArrayBuffer):
  - `write()` rejects with `TypeError: CompressionStream expects BufferSource chunks` (same text in DecompressionStream).
  - `close()` rejects with the same error. The writable becomes `'errored'` and `desiredSize` becomes null.
  - The readable stays `'readable'`, and `read()` **hangs forever**, including through `pipeThrough`.

**Decompression errors.**
- A failure shows up only as the `writer.close()` rejection: a TypeError with the codec message (e.g. `TypeError: gzip: bad magic`).
- `write()` promises resolve. A directly held `reader.read()` **hangs**; `writer.closed` and `reader.closed` never settle.
- **State afterwards:** writable `'writable'`, readable `'readable'`, `desiredSize=1`. A further `write()` resolves; a second `close()` rejects again.
- **Through pipes:** with `pipeThrough`, `read()` rejects with the TypeError, `for await` throws it, and `pipeTo` rejects with it.
- **Messages:**
  - gzip: corrupt or empty gives `gzip: bad magic`; truncated gives `inflate: unexpected end of input`.
  - deflate: corrupt gives `zlib: unsupported compression method`; empty gives `zlib: input too short`.
  - deflate-raw: corrupt gives `inflate: invalid Huffman code`; empty gives `inflate: unexpected end of input`.
- **Lenient cases:**
  - Trailing garbage is ignored, and only the first of two gzip members is decoded.
  - Over 1 MiB, `close()` rejects with `RangeError: Invalid typed array length` (not converted to TypeError).
- **`abort(err)`:** resolves; both sides become `'errored'` and `read()` rejects with `err`.
- **`reader.cancel()`:** the readable becomes `'closed'`. A later `close()` rejects with `TypeError: stream is not in a readable state`.

**Edge cases.**
- **Empty input** (no writes, or one empty write) gives one chunk:
  - gzip: `1f8b08000000000000ff03000000000000000000` (OS byte 0xff; node 0x03)
  - deflate: `789c030000000001`
  - deflate-raw: `0300`
- Decompressing those empty streams gives **zero** chunks, unlike the zlib streams' 0-length `'data'`.
- **Calling `w.close()` twice in a row:** both resolve and the output is enqueued **twice** (two identical chunks).
- **After close:** `close()` once the stream is closed rejects with `stream is not in a readable state`, and `write()` resolves.
- A second `getWriter()` or `getReader()` throws TypeError ("already locked").

# 7. Codec quirks that also show up in stream output

- **Deflate encoder bug:** matches at distances over 32768 produce invalid data.
  - A repeat at distance 32768 round-trips. At 32769 the original's inflater says `inflate: unexpected end of input`; at 65536 it says `invalid literal/length symbol`. Node cannot decode these either.
  - My 73893-byte text file fails from a 34240-byte prefix on. That is why my file-pipe round trip failed even though the bytes matched `gzipSync`.
- **Weak compression:** gzip of 200000 random bytes is 210882 bytes. Brotli and zstd of small inputs come out stored/raw; zstd of 22500 repetitive bytes is 22514 bytes.
- **Gunzip:**
  - Input under 18 bytes gives `gzip: bad magic` even with a valid magic.
  - The CRC32/ISIZE trailer is not checked.
- **Inflate:**
  - Adler-32 is not checked, so dropping the 4-byte trailer still succeeds.
  - Input under 6 bytes gives `zlib: input too short`.
- **More zstd messages:** `truncated frame`, `truncated frame header`, `truncated block header`, `truncated content checksum`, `content checksum mismatch`.
- **Constants:** `zlib.constants` has 170 keys: `Z_SYNC_FLUSH=2`, `Z_FULL_FLUSH=3`, `Z_FINISH=4`, `BROTLI_OPERATION_FLUSH=1`, `ZSTD_e_flush=1`. `zlib.Z_SYNC_FLUSH` at the top level is undefined.

# 8. Not tested

- `Readable.toWeb`/`Duplex.toWeb`/`stream.compose` on zlib streams.
- `cork()`/`uncork()` interaction.
- Breaking out of `for await` early (destroy semantics).
- Exact microtask timing of `destroy()`.
- Brotli/zstd streams with over 1 MiB of input (assumed to fail with the same RangeError).
- The zlib callback APIs (`zlib.gzip(buf, cb)`).
- BYOB readers, TransformStream strategies, `releaseLock()` mid-stream, detached ArrayBuffers.
- DecompressionStream outputs over 900 KB.

import json, sys, collections
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/agent_b')
from br import *
def sweep(name, comp, inp, step=1, maxcases=None):
    cases = [('%s_trunc%d' % (name, n), comp[:n]) for n in range(0, len(comp) + 1, step)]
    # batch so that json < 900KB
    res_o = []; res_n = []
    batch = []; size = 0
    def flush():
        nonlocal batch, size
        if batch:
            res_o.extend(run_orig(batch)); res_n.extend(run_node(batch)); batch = []; size = 0
    for c in cases:
        s = len(c[1]) * 2 + 100
        if size + s > 400000: flush()
        batch.append(c); size += s
    flush()
    runs = []  # (start, end, msg) run-length summary
    for (nm, b), ro, rn in zip(cases, res_o, res_n):
        if ro['ok']:
            m = 'OK' + ('(full)' if ro['out_hex'] == inp.hex() else '(partial %d)' % (len(ro['out_hex']) // 2))
        else:
            m = ro['message']
        mn = 'OK' if rn['ok'] else rn['message'] + ('/' + rn.get('code', '') if rn.get('code') else '')
        key = (m, mn)
        n = len(b)
        if runs and runs[-1][2] == key and runs[-1][1] == n - step:
            runs[-1][1] = n
        else:
            runs.append([n, n, key])
    return cases, res_o, res_n, runs
if __name__ == '__main__':
    src = {}
    for f in ('trunc_src.json', 'trunc_src2.json'):
        src.update(json.load(open('/tmp/agent_b/' + f)))
    names = sys.argv[1:] or list(src)
    allrec = []
    for name in names:
        comp = bytes.fromhex(src[name]['comp']); inp = bytes.fromhex(src[name]['input'])
        cases, ro, rn, runs = sweep(name, comp, inp)
        cnt = collections.Counter((r['message'] if not r['ok'] else 'OK') for r in ro)
        print('==', name, 'len', len(comp), dict(cnt))

import collections, json

    'l19chk': (text[:3000], {LEVEL: 19, CHK: 1}, None),

    'l1nosize': (text[:1500], {LEVEL: 1, CSF: 0, CHK: 1}, None),
}

for nm, (data, params, chunks) in inputs.items():
    c = compress(data, params, chunks)
    assert libzstd(c)['out_hex'] == data.hex()
    frames[nm] = (c, data)
    print(nm, len(data), '->', len(c))
def regions(c):
    """return list of (start, end, label) for byte positions"""
    log, err = parse_log(c)
    assert err is None, err
    regs = []
    blocks = [e for e in log if e[0] == 'block']
    first = blocks[0][1]
    regs.append((0, 4, 'magic'))
    regs.append((4, first, 'frame_header'))
    end = None
    for e in blocks:
        p = e[1]; info = e[2]
        regs.append((p, p + 3, 'block_header(type%d)' % info['type']))
        csz = 1 if info['type'] == 1 else info['size']
        regs.append((p + 3, p + 3 + csz, 'block_content(type%d)' % info['type']))
        end = p + 3 + csz
    if end < len(c):
        regs.append((end, len(c), 'checksum'))
    return regs
def region_of(regs, L):
    # truncation to length L: the first missing byte is at index L
    for s, e, lab in regs:
        if s <= L < e:
            return lab + ('@start' if L == s else '@mid')
    return 'end'
cases = []
for nm, (c, data) in frames.items():
    for L in range(0, len(c)):
        cases.append(('sweep_%s_len%d' % (nm, L), c[:L]))
    cases.append(('sweep_%s_full' % nm, c))
res = run_orig(cases)
summary = {}
allout = []
for nm, (c, data) in frames.items():
    regs = regions(c)
    agg = collections.OrderedDict()
    for L in range(0, len(c) + 1):
        key = 'sweep_%s_len%d' % (nm, L) if L < len(c) else 'sweep_%s_full' % nm
        r = res[key]
        msg = r['message'] if not r['ok'] else ('OK' if r['out_hex'] == data.hex() else 'OK-MISMATCH')
        reg = region_of(regs, L) if L < len(c) else 'full'
        agg.setdefault((reg, msg), []).append(L)
        allout.append({'name': key, 'hex': c[:L].hex(), 'orig': r})
    print('==', nm, 'len', len(c), 'regions:', [(s, e, l) for s, e, l in regs][:12], '...' if len(regs) > 12 else '')
    for (reg, msg), Ls in agg.items():
        rng = '%d..%d' % (Ls[0], Ls[-1]) if len(Ls) > 1 else str(Ls[0])
        print('   %-32s %-45s n=%d L=%s' % (reg, msg, len(Ls), rng if len(Ls) < 2 or Ls[-1] - Ls[0] + 1 == len(Ls) else str(Ls[:6]) + '...'))
    summary[nm] = {'len': len(c), 'regions': regs, 'agg': [[reg, msg, Ls] for (reg, msg), Ls in agg.items()]}
json.dump(summary, open('/tmp/agent_c/sweep_summary.json', 'w'))
json.dump(allout, open('/tmp/agent_c/res_sweep.json', 'w'))

from pc_common import *
cases = []
def hdr(bw, mlen, lits, cmds, dists, islast=True, npostfix=0, ndirect=0):
    return cmb_simple(bw, mlen, islast=islast, lit_syms=lits, cmd_syms=cmds, dist_syms=dists, npostfix=npostfix, ndirect=ndirect)
# implicit distance (cmd < 128) at pos 0 -> distance 4 -> dictionary ref
for cl in (2, 3, 4, 9):
    s = cmd_sym(0, cl - 2, False)
    bw = BW(); wbits(bw, 22); lc, cc, dc = hdr(bw, cl if cl >= 4 else cl, [A], [s], [0]); cc.put(bw, s)
    cases.append(('implicit_dist_at_pos0_copy%d' % cl, bw.bytes()))
# ring buffer not updated by dictionary refs / code 0: at pos 0: cmd(copy4, dcode 0) dict; then cmd(copy4, dcode 1) -> rb[1]=11 > pos 4 => dict word 11-4-1=6
s4 = cmd_sym(0, 2, True)
for seq in ([0, 1], [0, 0], [3, 2], [5, 1, 0], [15, 14, 13, 0]):
    bw = BW(); wbits(bw, 22)
    lc, cc, dc = hdr(bw, 4 * len(seq), [A], [s4], sorted(set(seq)) if len(set(seq)) <= 4 else [0])
    for d in seq: cc.put(bw, s4); dc.put(bw, d)
    cases.append(('rb_dictrefs_seq_' + '_'.join(map(str, seq)), bw.bytes()))
# uncompressed: nonzero padding AND overrun -> which first
bw = BW(); wbits(bw, 16); uncompressed(bw, b'abcdef', pad=1); b = bw.bytes()[:-2]; cases.append(('unc_pad1_and_overrun', b))
bw = BW(); wbits(bw, 16); uncompressed(bw, b'abcdef'); b = bw.bytes()[:-1]; cases.append(('unc_overrun_by1', b))
bw = BW(); wbits(bw, 16); uncompressed(bw, b'abcdef'); b = bw.bytes(); cases.append(('unc_exact_fit_no_last', b))
bw = BW(); wbits(bw, 16); uncompressed(bw, b'abcdef'); last_empty(bw); b = bw.bytes(); cases.append(('unc_exact_fit_then_last', b))
# uncompressed with header ending exactly at a byte boundary and EOF (no data at all)
bw = BW(); wbits(bw, 22); uncompressed(bw, b'abc'); b = bw.bytes()[:3]; cases.append(('unc_header_only_eof', b))
# uncompressed MLEN > 1MiB with data truncated
bw = BW(); wbits(bw, 24); mb_header(bw, (1 << 20) + 5, uncompressed=True, nibbles=6); bw.align(); bw.put(0, 8); cases.append(('unc_mlen_1MiB+5_truncated', bw.bytes()))
# metadata reserved + overrun: which first
bw = BW(); wbits(bw, 22); metadata(bw, b'abc', reserved=1); b = bw.bytes()[:-2]; cases.append(('meta_reserved_and_overrun', b))
bw = BW(); wbits(bw, 22); metadata(bw, b'abc' * 100, skipbytes=2); b = bw.bytes()[:10]; cases.append(('meta_skip2_overrun', b))
# metadata exuberant + overrun
bw = BW(); wbits(bw, 22); metadata(bw, b'abc', skipbytes=2); b = bw.bytes()[:-2]; cases.append(('meta_exub_and_overrun', b))
# metadata (exact fit) then last empty
bw = BW(); wbits(bw, 22); metadata(bw, b'abc'); last_empty(bw); cases.append(('meta_then_lastempty', bw.bytes()))
# two metadata blocks back to back then data
bw = BW(); wbits(bw, 22); metadata(bw, b'abc'); metadata(bw, b''); metadata(bw, b'x' * 20, skipbytes=1); uncompressed(bw, b'q'); last_empty(bw); cases.append(('meta_x3_then_unc', bw.bytes()))
# ISLAST + ISLASTEMPTY=0 + MNIBBLES=3 + reserved bit set
bw = BW(); wbits(bw, 22); bw.put(1, 1); bw.put(0, 1); bw.put(3, 2); bw.put(1, 1); cases.append(('islast_meta_reserved', bw.bytes()))
# compressed meta-block with ISLAST=0, then stream ends exactly after the meta-block (missing next header)
bw = BW(); wbits(bw, 22); lit_mb(bw, b'abc', islast=False); cases.append(('cmp_nonlast_then_eof', bw.bytes()))
# compressed then uncompressed then compressed last
bw = BW(); wbits(bw, 22); lit_mb(bw, b'abc', islast=False); uncompressed(bw, b'def'); lit_mb(bw, b'ghi', islast=True); cases.append(('cmp_unc_cmp', bw.bytes()))
run_all(cases)
EOF

from pc_common import *
import random
cases = []
def hdr(bw, mlen, lits, cmds, dists, islast=True, npostfix=0, ndirect=0, nibbles=None):
    return cmb_simple(bw, mlen, islast=islast, lit_syms=lits, cmd_syms=cmds, dist_syms=dists, npostfix=npostfix, ndirect=ndirect, nibbles=nibbles)
# valid 5-nibble compressed meta-block: 1 literal + copy 65536 at distance 1
s_big = cmd_sym(1, 23, True)
bw = BW(); wbits(bw, 24); lc, cc, dc = hdr(bw, 65537, [A], [s_big], [16]); cc.put(bw, s_big); bw.put(65536 - 2118, 24); lc.put(bw, A); dc.put(bw, 16); bw.put(0, 1)
cases.append(('cmp_mlen65537_nib5', bw.bytes()))
# valid 4-nibble max (65536)
bw = BW(); wbits(bw, 24); lc, cc, dc = hdr(bw, 65536, [A], [s_big], [16]); cc.put(bw, s_big); bw.put(65535 - 2118, 24); lc.put(bw, A); dc.put(bw, 16); bw.put(0, 1)
cases.append(('cmp_mlen65536_nib4', bw.bytes()))
# compact NBLTYPESL vectors with 2 trees, IMTF+RLE context map
def lit_types_small(n, blocks):
    data = bytearray()
    for b in blocks:
        t, c = b[0], b[1]
        data += bytes([0x30 + (t % 2)]) * c
    bw, st = new_stream(22)
    cmapl = []
    for t in range(n): cmapl += [t % 2] * 64
    compressed_mb(bw, st, len(data), [dict(ins=bytes(data), copy=4, dist=None)], islast=True, nbl=(n, 1, 1),
                  blocks=(blocks, None, None), cmodes=[0] * n, ntreesl=2, cmapl=cmapl, cmapl_opts=dict(rlemax=6, imtf=True))
    return bw.bytes()
for n in (64, 65, 128, 129, 255, 256):
    blocks = [(0, 2), (1, 1), (n - 1, 2), (n // 2, 1), (0, 1)]
    cases.append(('nbltypesL_%d_ntrees2' % n, lit_types_small(n, blocks)))
# compact context-mode vectors: 48 bytes of mixed data, NTREESL=64 identity map
rng = random.Random(3)
data = 'Aé€ b1;Z\x00\x7f'.encode() + bytes(rng.randrange(256) for _ in range(30))
for mode in range(4):
    bw, st = new_stream(22)
    compressed_mb(bw, st, len(data), [dict(ins=data, copy=4, dist=None)], islast=True, cmodes=[mode], ntreesl=64, cmapl=list(range(64)),
                  cmapl_opts=dict(rlemax=0, imtf=False))
    cases.append(('cmode%d_small_64trees' % mode, bw.bytes()))
# window cases with smaller prefix: WBITS=10 needs pos > 1008, keep as is (about 1.1KB). Add WBITS 10 + compressed prefix instead of uncompressed
bw, st = new_stream(10)
cmds = [dict(ins=b'xy', copy=1100, dist=1)]  # 1102 bytes of 'xyyyy'?? (copy from distance 1 repeats 'y')
compressed_mb(bw, st, 1102, cmds, islast=False)
# now pos = 1102; distance 1009 > window(1008) -> dict word ; distance 1008 -> copy
d = 1009
compressed_mb(bw, st, 4, [dict(ins=b'', copy=4, dist=d, short=False)], islast=False)
compressed_mb(bw, st, 4, [dict(ins=b'', copy=4, dist=1008, short=False)], islast=True)
cases.append(('win10_compact_d1009_dict_then_d1008_copy', bw.bytes()))
print('expected tail', bytes(st.out[-8:]))
run_all(cases, maxhex=40)
for n, b in cases: print(n, len(b))

# Assemble /tmp/agent_b/cases.json from the results DB plus curated truncation series.
import json, sys, os
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/agent_b')
from br import *

db = json.load(open(RESULTS_FILE))

EXCLUDE = {
    'complex_oversubscribed', 'complex_complete_early_stop', 'meta_w16_pad20', 'unc_pad1', 'unc_pad2',
    'exub_nib5_eof_before_isunc2', 'win10_pos1100_d1008_copy', 'win10_pos1100_d1009_dict', 'win10_pos1100_d1050_dict',
    'win10_pos1000_d1000_copy', 'win10_pos1000_d1001_dict',
    'cmode0_64trees_identity_map', 'cmode1_64trees_identity_map', 'cmode2_64trees_identity_map', 'cmode3_64trees_identity_map',
    'cmodes_01_switching', 'cmodes_23_switching', 'cmodes_30_switching', 'cmodes_12_switching',
}
RENAME = {
    'complex_valid_hskip2': 'complex_hskip2_but_lengths_need_cl_sym1_2__cl_incomplete',
    'complex_valid_hskip3': 'complex_hskip3_but_lengths_need_cl_sym1_2__cl_incomplete',
    'complex_cl_over_1_1_1': 'complex_cl_complete_after_2_entries_then_sym_lengths_oversubscribed_then_eof',
    'insert_overrun_then_eof_2symlit': 'insert_overrun_mlen3_ins5_2symlit_bits_present',
    'simple_lit_nsym4_eof_at_treeselect': 'simple_lit_nsym4_then_truncated_later',
    'dict_transform120_len4': 'dict_transform120_len4_word_overruns_mlen4',
    'complex_sym_over_121_zeros': 'complex_sym_oversub_then_zero_bytes',
    'exub_nib5_eof_before_isunc': 'exub_nib5_input_ends_before_isuncompressed_bit',
}

def fill_hex(name, hx, o):
    """records for big outputs lack out_hex -> regenerate from reference decoder and verify len/fnv"""
    if o.get('ok') and 'out_hex' not in o:
        r = run_ref(bytes.fromhex(hx))
        assert r['ok'], name
        out = bytes.fromhex(r['out_hex'])
        h = 2166136261
        for x in out:
            h ^= x; h = (h * 16777619) & 0xffffffff
        assert len(out) == o['out_len'] and h == o['out_fnv'], (name, len(out), o)
        return {'ok': True, 'out_hex': r['out_hex']}
    if not o.get('ok'):
        res = {'ok': False, 'message': o['message']}
        if o.get('ctor'): res['error_type'] = o['ctor']
        return res
    return {'ok': True, 'out_hex': o['out_hex']}

cases = []
seen = set()
for name in sorted(db):
    if name in EXCLUDE: continue
    v = db[name]
    if len(v['hex']) // 2 > 1500: continue
    nm = RENAME.get(name, name)
    cases.append({'name': nm, 'hex': v['hex'], 'orig': fill_hex(name, v['hex'], v['orig'])})
    seen.add(v['hex'])

# curated truncation series: every byte-length prefix of a few small crafted streams
series = ['basic_meta', 'basic_uncomp', 'enc_lit_blocks', 'complex_valid16x4_hskip2', 'cmap_5trees_imtf',
          'nbltypesI_3', 'npostfix2_ndirect4', 'meta_skip2_len257']
tr = []
for s in series:
    if s not in db: print('missing series', s); continue
    b = bytes.fromhex(db[s]['hex'])
    for n in range(len(b)):
        tr.append(('trunc__%s__len%d_of%d' % (s, n, len(b)), b[:n]))
res = run_orig(tr)
for (nm, b), r in zip(tr, res):
    cases.append({'name': nm, 'hex': b.hex(), 'orig': fill_hex(nm, b.hex(), r)})

json.dump(cases, open('/tmp/agent_b/cases.json', 'w'), indent=1)
print('cases', len(cases), 'bytes', os.path.getsize('/tmp/agent_b/cases.json'))
import collections
print(collections.Counter((c['orig']['message'] if not c['orig']['ok'] else 'OK') for c in cases).most_common())

=====================================================================
Vectors: /tmp/agent_b/cases.json, 1021 cases, each {name, hex, orig}. All re-verified against /tmp/orig.
