Crafting library: /tmp/agent_b/br.py and enc.py. Batch runner: /tmp/agent_b/runner.js (works in orig and node).

Every brotli error is a plain Error with message "brotli: <text>". Its only own property is "message":
there is no stack, code or errno.

1. MESSAGES AND EXACT TRIGGERS (21 distinct; none others seen in 120k mutation-fuzz cases)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
"brotli: unexpected end of input"
    Raised by any read that needs a bit beyond the end of the input, at the moment that field or symbol
    is read. Missing bits are never treated as zero.
    - Empty input gives this error.
    - Huffman decoding may look ahead past EOF safely. A 1-bit code that ends exactly at the last input
      bit decodes fine. It fails only if the actual codeword is longer than the bits that remain.
    - Probe: a stream whose remaining literals are all the zero-bit codeword still fails when
      truncated, so there is no zero-fill.
    - Ex: "" ; "0b0180616263" (uncompressed block, then no next header).
"brotli: uncompressed block overruns input"
    ISUNCOMPRESSED=1 and the padding is valid, but MLEN > number of whole bytes left. This is checked
    up front, before any data is copied, including when 0 bytes are left.
    - Ex: "0b0180" ; "5000106162636465".
"brotli: metadata overruns input"
    Metadata block whose padding is valid, but MSKIPLEN > bytes left.
    - Ex: "6b09007879".
"brotli: large-window streams are not supported"
    The 7-bit WBITS pattern 0010001: first bit 1, then 3 bits = 0, then 3 bits = 1.
    - Raised immediately. Following bits do not matter (reserved bit 0 or 1, any 6-bit window), and
      it is raised even if the input ends there.
    - Ex: "11", "91", "11ca".
    - Every other pattern is valid: 16, 17, 18..24, 10..15. There is no other WBITS error.
"brotli: exuberant size nibble"
    MNIBBLES = 5 or 6 and the last (most significant) nibble read is 0.
    - Checked right after the nibbles, before ISUNCOMPRESSED is read; "040000" errors even though the
      input ends there.
    - Applies to uncompressed, compressed and ISLAST blocks.
    - Ex: "2b0000084103".
"brotli: reserved bit set"
    MNIBBLES field = 3 (metadata) and the reserved bit is 1. Checked immediately.
    - Ex: "eb", "eb0003".
"brotli: exuberant metadata size byte"
    MSKIPBYTES >= 2 and the last (most significant) MSKIPLEN byte is 0. Checked right after that byte,
    before padding.
    - Ex: "6b160000".
    - MSKIPBYTES=1 with byte 00 (MSKIPLEN=1) is fine.
"brotli: non-zero padding bits"
    Fill bits up to the byte boundary are not all zero, either after the metadata header (also when
    MSKIPBYTES=0) or after ISUNCOMPRESSED=1.
    - Ex: "20003061626303", "8c03".
    - NOT checked for the final padding after the last meta-block (see section 4).
"brotli: simple code symbol out of range"
    A simple prefix code (HSKIP=1) symbol >= alphabet size. Symbols are ALPHABET_BITS =
    bitlen(alphabet_size-1) bits wide.
    - Checked as each symbol is read, so an invalid first symbol errors even if the input ends right
      after it.
    - Alphabet sizes:
        literal 256 (never triggers)
        insert&copy 704 (704..1023 invalid)
        distance 16+NDIRECT+(48<<NPOSTFIX) (e.g. NDIRECT=1: 65..127 invalid; NPOSTFIX=3,NDIRECT=120: 520+)
        block type NBLTYPES+2
        block count 26 (26..31 invalid)
        context map NTREES+RLEMAX
    - Ex: "1b0300118406" (block-count symbol 26).
"brotli: duplicate simple code symbol"
    Two equal symbols in a simple code.
    - Checked only after all NSYM symbols are read and range-checked. So range wins over a duplicate
      even if the duplicate comes first, and EOF while reading later symbols wins over a duplicate.
    - Checked before the NSYM=4 tree-select bit is read.
    - Ex: "1b010000a0c2c202820004".
"brotli: corrupt code-length code"
    Complex code: the code-length-code lengths (static 2..4-bit code, read in order 1,2,3,4,0,5,17,6,16,
    7..15 starting at index HSKIP) do not form a complete code.
    - Kraft space starts at 32; each length L subtracts 32>>L; reading stops as soon as space == 0.
    - space < 0 errors immediately (no more bits read).
    - Otherwise, after all 18-HSKIP entries, space != 0 errors unless exactly one length is non-zero.
      That covers under-full and all-zero.
    - Exactly one non-zero CL length is accepted: that symbol gets a 0-bit code (e.g. only sym 8 gives
      256 x len-8; only 16 also works).
    - Ex: "1b03000080db01" (1,2,1 over-full), "1b010000800d00000020200800" (2,2 then zeros).
    - HSKIP=2/3 that skips lengths the code needs gives this error too.
"brotli: code-length run overflows alphabet"
    A 16 or 17 repeat (including consecutive-repeat growth) would assign lengths past alphabet_size.
    - A run ending exactly at the alphabet end is OK.
    - This check precedes the space check.
    - Ex: "1b0300000080e3fe1f".
"brotli: prefix code is under/over-subscribed"
    Symbol code lengths are read until the alphabet is full or space (32768) == 0; reading stops at
    space == 0 and the rest are zero.
    - Over-subscription (space < 0) errors immediately. Node instead reads to the alphabet end, so it
      often reports EOF.
    - Errors if the alphabet is exhausted with space > 0. That includes the all-zero code and a complex
      code with a single used symbol.

11	1. MESSAGES AND EXACT TRIGGERS (21 distinct; none others seen in 120k mutation-fuzz cases)
12	-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
13	"brotli: unexpected end of input"
14	    Raised by any read that needs a bit beyond the end of the input, at the moment that field or symbol
15	    is read. Missing bits are never treated as zero.
16	    - Empty input gives this error.
17	    - Huffman decoding may look ahead past EOF safely. A 1-bit code that ends exactly at the last input
18	      bit decodes fine. It fails only if the actual codeword is longer than the bits that remain.
19	    - Probe: a stream whose remaining literals are all the zero-bit codeword still fails when
20	      truncated, so there is no zero-fill.
21	    - Ex: "" ; "0b0180616263" (uncompressed block, then no next header).
22	"brotli: uncompressed block overruns input"
23	    ISUNCOMPRESSED=1 and the padding is valid, but MLEN > number of whole bytes left. This is checked
24	    up front, before any data is copied, including when 0 bytes are left.
25	    - Ex: "0b0180" ; "5000106162636465".
26	"brotli: metadata overruns input"
27	    Metadata block whose padding is valid, but MSKIPLEN > bytes left.
28	    - Ex: "6b09007879".
29	"brotli: large-window streams are not supported"
30	    The 7-bit WBITS pattern 0010001: first bit 1, then 3 bits = 0, then 3 bits = 1.
31	    - Raised immediately. Following bits do not matter (reserved bit 0 or 1, any 6-bit window), and
32	      it is raised even if the input ends there.
33	    - Ex: "11", "91", "11ca".
34	    - Every other pattern is valid: 16, 17, 18..24, 10..15. There is no other WBITS error.
35	"brotli: exuberant size nibble"
36	    MNIBBLES = 5 or 6 and the last (most significant) nibble read is 0.
37	    - Checked right after the nibbles, before ISUNCOMPRESSED is read; "040000" errors even though the
38	      input ends there.
39	    - Applies to uncompressed, compressed and ISLAST blocks.
40	    - Ex: "2b0000084103".
41	"brotli: reserved bit set"
42	    MNIBBLES field = 3 (metadata) and the reserved bit is 1. Checked immediately.
43	    - Ex: "eb", "eb0003".
44	"brotli: exuberant metadata size byte"
45	    MSKIPBYTES >= 2 and the last (most significant) MSKIPLEN byte is 0. Checked right after that byte,
46	    before padding.
47	    - Ex: "6b160000".
48	    - MSKIPBYTES=1 with byte 00 (MSKIPLEN=1) is fine.
49	"brotli: non-zero padding bits"
50	    Fill bits up to the byte boundary are not all zero, either after the metadata header (also when
51	    MSKIPBYTES=0) or after ISUNCOMPRESSED=1.
52	    - Ex: "20003061626303", "8c03".
53	    - NOT checked for the final padding after the last meta-block (see section 4).
54	"brotli: simple code symbol out of range"
55	    A simple prefix code (HSKIP=1) symbol >= alphabet size. Symbols are ALPHABET_BITS =
56	    bitlen(alphabet_size-1) bits wide.
57	    - Checked as each symbol is read, so an invalid first symbol errors even if the input ends right
58	      after it.
59	    - Alphabet sizes:
60	        literal 256 (never triggers)
61	        insert&copy 704 (704..1023 invalid)
62	        distance 16+NDIRECT+(48<<NPOSTFIX) (e.g. NDIRECT=1: 65..127 invalid; NPOSTFIX=3,NDIRECT=120: 520+)
63	        block type NBLTYPES+2
64	        block count 26 (26..31 invalid)
65	        context map NTREES+RLEMAX
66	    - Ex: "1b0300118406" (block-count symbol 26).
67	"brotli: duplicate simple code symbol"
68	    Two equal symbols in a simple code.
69	    - Checked only after all NSYM symbols are read and range-checked. So range wins over a duplicate
70	      even if the duplicate comes first, and EOF while reading later symbols wins over a duplicate.
71	    - Checked before the NSYM=4 tree-select bit is read.
72	    - Ex: "1b010000a0c2c202820004".
73	"brotli: corrupt code-length code"
74	    Complex code: the code-length-code lengths (static 2..4-bit code, read in order 1,2,3,4,0,5,17,6,16,
75	    7..15 starting at index HSKIP) do not form a complete code.
76	    - Kraft space starts at 32; each length L subtracts 32>>L; reading stops as soon as space == 0.
77	    - space < 0 errors immediately (no more bits read).
78	    - Otherwise, after all 18-HSKIP entries, space != 0 errors unless exactly one length is non-zero.
79	      That covers under-full and all-zero.
80	    - Exactly one non-zero CL length is accepted: that symbol gets a 0-bit code (e.g. only sym 8 gives
81	      256 x len-8; only 16 also works).
82	    - Ex: "1b03000080db01" (1,2,1 over-full), "1b010000800d00000020200800" (2,2 then zeros).
83	    - HSKIP=2/3 that skips lengths the code needs gives this error too.
84	"brotli: code-length run overflows alphabet"
85	    A 16 or 17 repeat (including consecutive-repeat growth) would assign lengths past alphabet_size.
86	    - A run ending exactly at the alphabet end is OK.
87	    - This check precedes the space check.
88	    - Ex: "1b0300000080e3fe1f".
89	"brotli: prefix code is under/over-subscribed"
90	    Symbol code lengths are read until the alphabet is full or space (32768) == 0; reading stops at
91	    space == 0 and the rest are zero.
92	    - Over-subscription (space < 0) errors immediately. Node instead reads to the alphabet end, so it
93	      often reports EOF.
94	    - Errors if the alphabet is exhausted with space > 0. That includes the all-zero code and a complex
95	      code with a single used symbol.
96	    - Repeat semantics match RFC/node: 16 repeats the last non-zero length (initially 8). A 0 literal
97	      does not change it. 17 resets the 16-chain and vice versa.
98	    - Ex: "1b030000803b01", "1b0300008003e0a2dad405080100".
99	"brotli: context map run overflows"
100	    An RLE zero-run (symbol s in 1..RLEMAX) would pass the map end (64*NBLTYPESL or
101	    4*NBLTYPESD). Checked right after the extra bits.
102	    - Run length = (1<<s) + an s-bit extra value.
103	    - Ex: "1b0300008855f000" (RLEMAX=6, run 65 in a 64-entry map).
104	    - "Context map value out of range" is impossible (symbols are < NTREES+RLEMAX; IMTF keeps values <
105	      NTREES). The only related error is the simple-code range error.
106	"brotli: meta-block length mismatch"
107	    A command produces more than the remaining MLEN.
108	    (a) Insert overrun: all insert_len literals are decoded first, with no MLEN check during this.
109	        - Then the error is raised, without reading a distance.
110	        - So a truncated overrun gives "unexpected end of input" (node gives BLOCK_LENGTH_1 eagerly).
111	        - Ex: "1b02000020c202850000" (MLEN 3, insert 5).
112	    (b) Copy overrun: raised after the distance is read and validated.
113	        - Order: invalid short distance -> dictionary length -> dictionary transform -> MLEN.
114	        - For dictionary words, the TRANSFORMED length counts. Copy len 8 + OmitLast3 = 5 bytes fits
115	          MLEN 5.
116	        - Ex: "1b04000020c202998000", "1b03000020c262909006" (5-byte word, MLEN 4).
117	    - If the inserts end exactly at MLEN, the meta-block ends: the copy part is ignored and no distance
118	      is read.
119	"brotli: invalid short distance"
120	    Distance codes 4..15 (last+-1..3, second-last+-1..3) give a distance <= 0. Codes 0..3 can never
121	    fail.
122	    - Ex: "1b08000020c24a11410a2206" (last=1, code 4).
123	"brotli: invalid dictionary reference length"
124	    distance > max_distance, where max_distance = min(total bytes output so far, (1<<WBITS)-16), and
125	    copy_len is not in 4..24.
126	    - Includes implicit distance and codes 0..3 at stream start (ring buffer 4,11,15,16 > pos 0).
127	    - Ex: "1b01000020c202900000" (copy 2, distance 4 at pos 0).
128	"brotli: invalid dictionary transform"
129	    Dictionary reference with transform = word_id >> NDBITS[len] >= 121. word_id =
130	    distance-max_distance-1.
131	    - Ex: "1b03000020c242906809c8".
132	"brotli: block length exhausted with a single block type"
133	    For a category with NBLTYPES=1 the block length is an implicit 2^24 per meta-block. Needing symbol
134	    2^24+1 of that category in one meta-block raises this.
135	    - Only reachable via an insert overrun of > 2^24 literals, counted across commands of the
136	      meta-block. The counter resets per meta-block.
137	    - Exactly 2^24 literals with MLEN 1 gives "meta-block length mismatch".
138	    - Ex: "1b00000020c202bf807e4fff01" (vs "...7c4fff01" = 2^24 gives mismatch).
139	RangeError "Invalid typed array length"  (not a brotli message)
140	    Decode succeeded but output > 1,048,576 bytes. This is the runtime's 1 MiB cap on any
141	    TypedArray/Buffer; fs.readFileSync of > 1 MiB fails the same way.
142	    - The decoder itself is not limited: a brotli error found after > 1 MiB of output still wins.
143	    - Exactly 1 MiB is OK.
144	    - Ex: "9f0000100020c2e2b18074ef1f00" (1 MiB + 1). Valid 6-nibble meta-blocks always hit this.
145	
146	2. PARSE ORDER (first failing check wins; everything is sequential, deferred checks as noted)
147	--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
148	Stream header:
149	  WBITS (marker -> large-window error).
150	Meta-block header, loop:
151	  ISLAST; [ISLASTEMPTY -> stream ends]; MNIBBLES.
152	  Metadata branch:
153	    reserved -> MSKIPBYTES -> bytes -> exuberant byte -> padding -> overrun -> skip.
154	    If ISLAST, end.
155	  Data branch:
156	    nibbles -> exuberant -> [ISUNCOMPRESSED if !ISLAST].
157	    Uncompressed: padding -> overrun -> copy.
158	Compressed header (RFC order):
159	  NBLTYPES/btype code/bcount code/first count for L, I, D -> NPOSTFIX, NDIRECT -> cmodes ->
160	  NTREESL + cmap -> NTREESD + cmap -> literal, command and distance codes.
161	Commands until remaining <= 0:
162	  [I switch] -> cmd symbol + insert/copy extra -> literals (each with [L switch]) ->
163	  [insert MLEN check] -> [stop if done] -> distance (implicit, or [D switch] + symbol + extra) ->
164	  short-distance check -> dict(len, transform) or copy -> MLEN check.
165	Semantics all confirmed equal to node on valid data:
166	  - Window rule max_distance = min(pos, 2^WBITS-16) holds (WBITS=10: d=1008 copies, d=1009 is a
167	    dictionary word).
168	  - Dictionary refs and code 0 do not update the distance ring buffer.
169	  - Block-type ring buffer starts at (1,0); sym0 = second-to-last, sym1 = last+1 mod N, else sym-2.
170	  - All 26 block-count codes.
171	  - NBLTYPES 1..256 (varlen8 caps at 256; >256 is not encodable).
172	  - NTREES up to 256; RLEMAX 1..16 and IMTF.
173	  - Context modes 0..3 (MSB6 too, which node never emits).
174	  - NPOSTFIX 0..3 and NDIRECT up to 120.
175	  - Zero-length transformed words are accepted.
176	
177	3. EOF / TRUNCATION SUMMARY
178	--------------------------
179	Node streams q5/q11 (one meta-block, 344..7059 B) and flush-built 5-meta-block streams (490/497 B,
180	including an uncompressed block) were cut at every length.
181	- Every prefix gives "unexpected end of input".
182	- Exception: prefixes that end inside an uncompressed block's payload, with the header complete
183	  and 0..MLEN-1 payload bytes present, give "uncompressed block overruns input". Full length gives OK.
184	- 29k prefixes of 250 crafted valid vectors gave only those two messages, plus "metadata overruns
185	  input" inside metadata payloads. OK only appeared when nothing but trailing garbage was removed.
186	
187	4. LAX BEHAVIOURS / DIFFERENCES FROM NODE
188	----------------------------------------
189	- Final padding is NOT checked (node: ERR__ERROR_FORMAT_PADDING_2). This covers the bits after
190	  ISLAST+ISLASTEMPTY and after a compressed ISLAST block.
191	  - "deadbeef" -> OK empty. Also "fb" -> OK, "81ff" -> OK.
192	  - Example "1b040000a0cbd0d8de040a01488d" -> "hello".
193	- Trailing bytes after the stream end are ignored (node too).
194	- Otherwise exactly as strict as node: in 100k differential mutated streams there was no
195	  orig-OK/node-fail except PADDING_2, no orig-fail/node-OK, and no differing output.
196	- Message mapping to node codes:
197	  - CL_SPACE -> corrupt code-length code
198	  - HUFFMAN_SPACE -> under/over-subscribed, or run overflows alphabet for repeat overflow
199	  - BLOCK_LENGTH_1/2 -> meta-block length mismatch (or EOF, since literals are read first)
200	  - DISTANCE -> invalid short distance
201	  - DICTIONARY -> invalid dictionary reference length
202	  - TRANSFORM -> invalid dictionary transform
203	  - CONTEXT_MAP_REPEAT -> context map run overflows
204	  - PADDING_1 -> non-zero padding bits
205	  - RESERVED -> reserved bit set
206	  - EXUBERANT_NIBBLE / EXUBERANT_META_NIBBLE -> exuberant size nibble / metadata size byte
207	  - SIMPLE_HUFFMAN_ALPHABET / SAME -> out of range / duplicate
208	  - WINDOW_BITS -> large-window
209	  - Z_BUF_ERROR -> unexpected end of input, or the two overrun messages
210	- Order differences from node:
211	  - Insert overrun: node fails before reading literals.
212	  - Over-subscribed code: orig fails at once, node reads on (often EOF).
213	
214	5. VALID-STREAM CONFORMANCE
215	--------------------------
216	Every set matched byte-for-byte:
217	- 1880 node streams: q0..11, lgwin 10..24, modes 0..2, 12 inputs (0 B..40 KB).
218	- 69 large node streams up to 1 MiB output: LGBLOCK, NPOSTFIX/NDIRECT, disabled literal context modeling.
219	- 3150 random crafted valid streams: all header features, dictionary refs with all transforms,
220	  windows 10..24, mixed metadata/uncompressed/compressed blocks.
221	- An exhaustive set: 121 transforms x lengths 4..24 x 3 words.
222	
223	6. INPUT ARG (side note)
224	------------------------
225	- Input is converted like Buffer.from: strings as UTF-8; arrays and ArrayBuffer are accepted.
226	- A DataView decodes as empty input (gives "unexpected end of input").
227	- Number, null or undefined -> TypeError "Buffer.from: unsupported value".

steps.message:
I found 19 distinct brotli error messages plus one runtime `RangeError`, and mapped the trigger and check order for each. The decoder is as strict as node except for one lax behaviour: it never checks the final padding bits after the last meta-block.

**Deliverables**
- **`/tmp/agent_b/cases.json`**: 1021 vectors as `{name, hex, orig}`, all re-run against `/tmp/orig` with no mismatches. Inputs are at most 1.4 KB. The file is 2.7 MB because one OK case has a 1 MiB output. The `RangeError` cases also carry `"error_type": "RangeError"`.
- **`/tmp/agent_b/REPORT.txt`**: the full catalog below, with a node error-code mapping and an example hex per message.
- **Tools**: crafting libraries `/tmp/agent_b/br.py` and `/tmp/agent_b/enc.py`; batch runner `/tmp/agent_b/runner.js`, which works under both orig and node.

**Error object.** Every error is a plain `Error` whose message starts with `"brotli: "`. Its only own property is `message` (no stack, code or errno).

**Messages and triggers**

| Message | Trigger, and when it is checked |
|---|---|
| `brotli: unexpected end of input` | Any read that needs a bit past the end, raised at that read. Missing bits are never treated as zero. Empty input gives this. Huffman look-ahead past the end is safe; it only fails if the actual codeword is longer than the bits left. |
| `brotli: uncompressed block overruns input` | MLEN is larger than the whole bytes left, checked before copying (also when 0 bytes are left). |
| `brotli: metadata overruns input` | MSKIPLEN is larger than the bytes left. |
| `brotli: large-window streams are not supported` | WBITS pattern `0010001`, raised immediately whatever follows (even end of input). Every other WBITS pattern is valid. |
| `brotli: exuberant size nibble` | MNIBBLES is 5 or 6 and the top nibble is 0. Checked before ISUNCOMPRESSED is read. |
| `brotli: reserved bit set` | Metadata reserved bit is 1. |
| `brotli: exuberant metadata size byte` | MSKIPBYTES ≥ 2 and the top MSKIPLEN byte is 0. Checked before the padding. |
| `brotli: non-zero padding bits` | Fill bits before metadata data (even with MSKIPBYTES=0) or before uncompressed data are not zero. |
| `brotli: simple code symbol out of range` | Simple-code symbol ≥ alphabet size, checked as each symbol is read. |
| `brotli: duplicate simple code symbol` | Checked only after all symbols are read and range-checked, before the tree-select bit. |
| `brotli: corrupt code-length code` | The code-length-code lengths are over-full (fails immediately) or not full after all entries are read. Exactly one non-zero length is accepted and becomes a 0-bit code. |
| `brotli: code-length run overflows alphabet` | A 16/17 repeat would go past the alphabet end. This beats the over-subscription check. |
| `brotli: prefix code is under/over-subscribed` | Over-subscription fails immediately (node reads on and often reports end of input). Also raised if the alphabet runs out with the code incomplete, including all-zero and single-symbol complex codes. |
| `brotli: context map run overflows` | An RLE zero-run would pass the end of the map. |
| `brotli: meta-block length mismatch` | Insert overrun: all literals are decoded first, then this error, with no distance read; truncated literals give end of input (node fails before reading them). Copy overrun: checked after the distance is read and validated, using the transformed length for dictionary words. |
| `brotli: invalid short distance` | Distance codes 4..15 give a distance ≤ 0. |
| `brotli: invalid dictionary reference length` | Distance > min(output so far, 2^WBITS−16) with copy length outside 4..24. |
| `brotli: invalid dictionary transform` | Transform index ≥ 121. |
| `brotli: block length exhausted with a single block type` | With NBLTYPES=1 the block length is an implicit 2^24 per meta-block. Needing literal 2^24+1 raises this; it is only reachable through an insert overrun. |
| `RangeError "Invalid typed array length"` | Successful decode with output over 1,048,576 bytes. This is the runtime's general 1 MiB buffer cap (`readFileSync` fails the same way). Exactly 1 MiB is OK, and a brotli error found later still wins. |

**Check order.** Everything is parsed sequentially and the first failing check wins. Meta-block header:
- Metadata: reserved bit → MSKIPBYTES → size bytes → exuberant-byte check → padding → overrun.
- Data: nibbles → exuberant check → ISUNCOMPRESSED → padding → overrun.

For each distance, the checks run in this order: short-distance check → dictionary length → dictionary transform → MLEN check.

**Lax behaviours and other differences from node**
- Final padding after ISLAST+ISLASTEMPTY or after the last compressed block is not checked. `deadbeef`, `fb` and `81ff` all decode to empty; node rejects them with PADDING_2.
- Trailing bytes after the stream end are ignored (node does the same).
- Across 100k bit-mutated streams run through both, padding was the only case where orig accepted and node rejected. There were no cases the other way round and no differing outputs.

**Valid streams.** Everything decoded byte-identical to node:
- 1880 node streams: quality 0..11, lgwin 10..24, modes 0..2.
- 69 large node streams up to 1 MiB, with LGBLOCK, NPOSTFIX/NDIRECT and context modelling off.
- 3150 random crafted streams covering every feature.
- All 121 dictionary transforms at every word length 4..24.

**Truncation.** I cut node quality-5 and quality-11 streams, including 5-meta-block streams, at every byte length. Every prefix gives `unexpected end of input`. The exceptions are prefixes ending inside an uncompressed block's data, which give `uncompressed block overruns input`, and inside metadata data, which give `metadata overruns input`.

**Input handling (side note).** Input is converted like `Buffer.from`: strings as UTF-8, arrays and ArrayBuffers are accepted. A DataView is treated as empty. Numbers, null and undefined throw a TypeError.

    for x in sorted(keep):

print('valid frames', len(vl), 'bad', nbad)
json.dump(cases, open('/tmp/agent_c/cases.json', 'w'))
json.dump(annot, open('/tmp/agent_c/cases_annotated.json', 'w'))
print('cases', len(cases), 'bytes', os.path.getsize('/tmp/agent_c/cases.json'))
import collections
c = collections.Counter(x['orig']['message'] if not x['orig']['ok'] else 'OK' for x in cases)

ZSTD DECODER CATALOG: lumen (/tmp/orig) require('zlib').zstdDecompressSync
=============================================================================
Every error is a plain Error. Only .message matters, and every message starts with "zstd: ".
Decoding is all-or-nothing: the first error found is thrown and no partial output is returned.

How it was checked
  * cases.json has 3222 vectors (name/hex/orig). Every input is under 4 KB.
  * model.py (needs zt.py) is an executable Python model of the original. It reproduces the
    original exactly: message, precedence and output bytes. It was checked against:
      - all 3222 vectors;
      - 142k differential fuzz cases (118k random mutations, 24k structure-aware random frames);
      - 722 valid libzstd frames.
    There were 0 mismatches. Porting model.py to Rust gives the original's exact behaviour.
  * The precedence below is the order in which the model runs its checks.

FILES (/tmp/agent_c/)
  cases.json            deliverable vectors
  cases_annotated.json  same vectors plus libzstd 1.5.5's verdict for each
  model.py, zt.py       executable spec, plus the encoder/FSE/Huffman toolkit used to build vectors
  sweep_summary.json    full truncation sweeps
  res_<suite>.json      raw per-suite results (they include libzstd and the python-parser output)

------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A. DECODE ALGORITHM WITH CHECKS IN ORDER (this order is the precedence)
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
TOP LEVEL
  len(input) == 0                                   -> "zstd: empty input"   (libzstd returns empty)
  Loop while bytes remain (at the start, and after every frame or skippable frame):
    1-3 bytes remain                                -> "zstd: truncated frame"
    u32le & 0xFFFFFFF0 == 0x184D2A50 (skippable 0x50..0x5F):
        fewer than 8 bytes remain                   -> "zstd: truncated skippable frame"
        size(u32le) > bytes remaining after header  -> "zstd: truncated skippable frame"  (0xFFFFFFFF included)
        Otherwise skip it. Its content is NOT output.
        Input made only of skippable frames gives an empty Buffer with no error.
    u32le != 0xFD2FB528                             -> "zstd: bad magic number"
        This also covers legacy v0.1-v0.7 magics, 0x184D2A4F, 0x184D2A60 and trailing garbage.
  Trailing junk after a valid frame is always an error:
    1-3 bytes (zeros, 28, 28b5, 28b52f, ...) -> "truncated frame"
    4 or more bytes (zeros, random)          -> "bad magic number"
    a bare magic                             -> "truncated frame header"
  Multiple frames simply concatenate.

FRAME HEADER (read sequentially, each check right after its field)
  FHD missing                                       -> "zstd: truncated frame header"
  FHD bit3 (reserved) set                           -> "zstd: reserved frame header bit set"
      Checked before any truncation of the rest of the header.
  FHD bit4 (unused): ignored.
  Single_Segment == 0 and window byte missing       -> "zstd: truncated frame header"
  Window descriptor value: completely IGNORED.
      Any exponent (0xFF means 2^41) is accepted.
      There is no window limit on block sizes or match offsets.
  DID field (0/1/2/4 bytes) incomplete              -> "zstd: truncated frame header"
  DID != 0                                          -> "zstd: dictionary frames are not supported"
      Checked before the FCS field is checked for presence. DID == 0 (any width) is fine.
  FCS field incomplete                              -> "zstd: truncated frame header"
      FCS widths: SS=1 and flag 0 -> 1 byte; flag 1 -> 2 bytes (+256); flag 2 -> 4; flag 3 -> 8.
      FCS 2^64-1 is NOT treated as "unknown".
  Huffman table, the three FSE tables (LL/OF/ML) and repeat offsets [1,4,8] are reset per frame.

BLOCKS (3-byte header: bit0 last, bits1-2 type, bits3-23 size)
  fewer than 3 bytes                                -> "zstd: truncated block header"
      This includes a non-last block at the end of input.
  size > 131072 (any type, RLE and reserved too)    -> "zstd: block size exceeds maximum"
      The size check comes before the type check.
  type 3                                            -> "zstd: reserved block type"
  raw: size bytes missing                           -> "zstd: truncated raw block"
  RLE: the 1 content byte missing                   -> "zstd: truncated RLE block"
      The block outputs `size` copies of that byte.
  compressed: size bytes missing                    -> "zstd: truncated compressed block"
      The whole block must be present before any of its content is parsed.
  There is NO window or FCS-based block limit. With a 1 KiB window, a 1025..4000-byte raw or RLE
  block is fine. A single-segment block larger than its FCS fails only at the end-of-frame FCS check.
  Empty raw/RLE blocks and many of them are fine.
  If the checksum bytes follow a block whose last flag is missing, they are parsed as a block header.

END OF FRAME (after the last block)
  FCS present and frame output != FCS               -> "zstd: frame content size mismatch"
      Only checked here, never per block. So FCS=4 followed by a 5-byte non-last block and then a
      truncated header reports "truncated block header".
      This check comes before the checksum checks.
  checksum flag set: fewer than 4 bytes             -> "zstd: truncated content checksum"
  low 32 bits of XXH64(frame output, seed 0), LE, differ -> "zstd: content checksum mismatch"
      The checksum covers this frame's output only.
      An 8-byte checksum fails: the extra 4 bytes are read as the next magic, giving "bad magic number".

COMPRESSED BLOCK: LITERALS SECTION
  block content empty                               -> "zstd: missing literals section header"
  Raw (0) / RLE (1):
      Header size: bit2==0 -> 1 byte (size = b0>>3); sf=01 -> 2 bytes (12 bits); sf=11 -> 3 bytes (20 bits).
      header bytes missing                          -> "zstd: truncated literals section"
      regen > 131072                                -> "zstd: literals section too large"
          This comes before the content-availability check.
      raw: regen bytes missing / RLE: 1 byte missing -> "zstd: truncated literals section"
  Compressed (2) / Treeless (3):
      sf0: 1 stream, 3-byte header, 10-bit sizes; sf1: 4 streams, 3 bytes, 10 bits;
      sf2: 4 streams, 4 bytes, 14 bits; sf3: 4 streams, 5 bytes, 18 bits.
      header bytes missing                          -> "zstd: truncated literals section"
      regen > 131072                                -> "zstd: literals section too large"
      hdr + csize > block size                      -> "zstd: truncated literals section"
      type 2: parse the Huffman tree (below) from the start of the csize bytes.
      type 3 with no Huffman table yet in THIS frame -> "zstd: treeless literals without a previous Huffman table"
          The table persists across raw/RLE blocks and across blocks with raw/RLE literals.
          The latest table wins. It does NOT carry over to the next frame.
      1 stream: all remaining csize bytes form one stream that decodes `regen` symbols.
      4 streams:
          fewer than 6 bytes after the tree         -> "zstd: truncated literals jump table"
          6 + s1+s2+s3 > remaining                  -> "zstd: literals jump table exceeds section"
          seg = ceil(regen/4); 3*seg > regen        -> "zstd: corrupted 4-stream literals sizes"
              This fails only for regen 1, 2 and 5. regen 0, 3 and 4 are accepted (libzstd needs 6 or more).
              It is checked after the jump table and before any stream is decoded.
          Streams 1..4 are decoded strictly one after another (init, decode, end check, then the next).
          Stream 4 size = remaining - 6 - s1 - s2 - s3. Stream counts are seg, seg, seg, regen - 3*seg.
      Each Huffman stream:
          0 bytes, even when its count is 0         -> "zstd: empty bitstream"
          last byte 0                               -> "zstd: bitstream missing sentinel bit"
          a symbol needs more bits than remain      -> "zstd: Huffman stream overrun"
              Peek maxBits with zero padding; it fails only if the code length exceeds the remaining bits.
          bits left after the required count       -> "zstd: Huffman stream not fully consumed"
  The literals section (including all Huffman decoding) is fully processed before the sequences header is read.

  csize == 0                                        -> "zstd: missing Huffman tree header"
  hb >= 128 (direct): n = hb-127 4-bit weights, high nibble first.
      ceil(n/2) bytes missing                       -> "zstd: truncated Huffman weights"
  hb < 128 (FSE): hb bytes follow.
      1 + hb > csize                                -> "zstd: truncated Huffman tree description"
      NCount parse: max accuracy log 6, alphabet 255. See the NCount section; its errors come first.
      NCount bytes >= hb, so the bitstream size is 0 or less
                                                    -> "zstd: truncated Huffman weights bitstream"
          hb == 0 also gives this.
      bitstream last byte 0                         -> "zstd: bitstream missing sentinel bit"
      fewer than 2*AL bits                          -> "zstd: truncated Huffman weights bitstream"
      Decode with two interleaved states. Termination is exactly libzstd's: after a state update
      overflows, emit the other state's symbol and stop. The edge case of an nbBits=0 state at the
      end is handled the same way as libzstd (verified).
      more than 255 weights                         -> "zstd: too many Huffman weights"
  Weight validation, in this order:
      any weight > 11                               -> "zstd: Huffman weight too large"
      sum of 2^(w-1) == 0                           -> "zstd: empty Huffman table"
      tableLog = floor(log2(sum)) + 1 > 11          -> "zstd: Huffman code length too large"
          libzstd allows 12.
      2^tableLog - sum is not a power of two        -> "zstd: corrupted Huffman weights"
      The last symbol's weight is implied.
      There is NO libzstd-style "need an even number (2 or more) of weight-1 symbols" check:
      weights [11] (implied 11) and [2] (implied 2) are accepted.
  Codes are canonical, as in libzstd (verified on 722 libzstd frames).

SEQUENCES SECTION
  no bytes left after the literals                  -> "zstd: missing sequences section header"
  b0 < 128: nbSeq = b0.
  128..254: 2 bytes; second byte missing            -> "zstd: truncated sequences header"
  255: 3 bytes (nbSeq = b1 + b2<<8 + 0x7F00); missing bytes -> "zstd: truncated sequences header"
  Non-canonical forms are accepted. 0x80 0x05 means 5 sequences; 0x80 0x00 means 0 sequences.
  nbSeq == 0: any byte after the header           -> "zstd: trailing bytes after empty sequences section"
      Otherwise the literals are output.
  modes byte missing                                -> "zstd: missing sequence compression modes"
  modes & 3 != 0                                    -> "zstd: reserved sequence mode bits set"
      Checked before any table. libzstd ignores these bits.
  Tables are parsed in order LL (bits 7-6), OF (bits 5-4), ML (bits 3-2); the first error wins.
    0 predefined.
    1 RLE: byte missing                             -> "zstd: truncated RLE sequence table"
           symbol > 35 / 31 / 52 (LL/OF/ML)         -> "zstd: RLE sequence symbol out of range"
               OF 28..31 are accepted here.
    2 FSE: NCount with max accuracy log LL 9, OF 8, ML 9 and alphabet 36 / 32 / 53.
           parse errors first, then NCount bytes beyond the block end
                                                    -> "zstd: truncated FSE table description"
    3 repeat: no table yet for this field in this frame
                                                    -> "zstd: repeat mode without a previous sequence table"
           Predefined and RLE tables count as tables. A block with nbSeq=0 sets nothing and keeps
           earlier tables. Raw/RLE blocks keep tables. Tables reset at each frame.
  bitstream = rest of block; 0 bytes                -> "zstd: missing sequences bitstream"
      last byte 0                                   -> "zstd: bitstream missing sentinel bit"

NCOUNT (FSE table description) READER, shared by Huffman weights and LL/OF/ML
  AL = (low nibble) + 5; AL > max                   -> "zstd: FSE accuracy log too large"
  Bit parsing is the standard FSE_readNCount. Bits past the available bytes read as ZERO; the
  over-read is only judged after the parse (rules above).
  Alphabet size N = 255 (Huffman weights; only symbols 0..254 are usable), 36 (LL), 32 (OF), 53 (ML).
  Quirky boundary: during parsing ONE extra index (== N) is tolerated.
      count needed for index > N                    -> "zstd: too many symbols in FSE distribution"
      zero-repeat flags advancing past N            -> "zstd: too many symbols in FSE distribution"
      parse ends (remaining == 1) but the distribution uses index N
                                                    -> "zstd: corrupted FSE distribution"
  Over-subscription cannot be encoded. Under-subscription shows up as one of the two errors above.

SEQUENCE DECODE AND EXECUTE (interleaved per sequence)
  Initial states LL, OF, ML: not enough bits        -> "zstd: truncated sequences bitstream"
  For each sequence:
    1. Read OF extra bits, then ML extra bits, then LL extra bits.
       Any read past the start                     -> "zstd: truncated sequences bitstream"
       All of a sequence's bits are read before it executes.
    2. Resolve the offset. Repeat offsets work as in the RFC and persist across blocks; they reset per frame.
    3. LL > literals remaining                      -> "zstd: sequence literals overrun"
    4. offset == 0                                  -> "zstd: invalid repeat offset"
           Only possible with LL==0, OV==3 and rep1==1.
    5. Copy LL literals.
       offset > TOTAL bytes output so far in this call (all previous frames included)
                                                    -> "zstd: sequence offset too far back"
           Skippable frame content does not count.
    6. Running sum of this block's LL+ML > 131072   -> "zstd: block regenerated size too large"
    7. Copy the match.
    8. If this is not the last sequence, update the states LL, ML, OF.
       Out of bits                                  -> "zstd: truncated sequences bitstream"
           This happens AFTER the previous sequence executed.
  After the last sequence (no state update):
    bits left                                       -> "zstd: sequences bitstream not fully consumed"
  Then the remaining literals are appended. They are NOT counted in the 131072 limit.

Each trigger is in section A. Example vectors are in cases.json; names are given as group/name.

  Output larger than 1,048,576 bytes gives RangeError "Invalid typed array length".

  throw the same error. It is thrown only AFTER the whole input decoded without error, so any
  zstd error, including trailing garbage or a bad checksum, wins.
  The options argument is ignored; maxOutputLength has no effect.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------
C. LAX: the original accepts what libzstd or a strict spec reading rejects
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 1. Window descriptor ignored. Exponent up to 31 is fine (libzstd: "too much memory" above 2^27).
    Blocks larger than the window are fine (up to 128 KiB). Offsets larger than the window are fine.
 2. Matches can reach back into EARLIER FRAMES' output in the same call, back to the start of all
    output (extra/xframe_*, seq2/off_into_prev_frame). Skippable content cannot be reached.
 3. A block can output up to 128 KiB of sequence output plus up to 128 KiB of trailing literals.
    Example: seq3/lits131072_seq_ml1000 gives 132072 bytes, OK.
 4. 4-stream literals with regen 0, 3 or 4 are accepted.
 5. Huffman weights without the even, 2-or-more count of weight-1 symbols are accepted
    (huf/tree_two_w11, huf/tree_two_w2_no_rank1).
 6. The Huffman-weights FSE alphabet allows symbols up to 254; unused high symbols are fine.
 7. nbSeq in 2-byte form equal to 0 (0x80 0x00) is accepted; non-canonical nbSeq forms are accepted.
 8. FHD unused bit 4 is ignored.
 9. Offsets 28..31 are allowed in RLE mode and in the FSE alphabet; they fail later as "too far back".

STRICT: the original rejects what libzstd accepts
 1. RLE block larger than 131072 -> "block size exceeds maximum".
 2. Reserved bits in the sequence modes byte.
 3. Huffman maxBits 12.
 4. Every Huffman stream must be exactly consumed and have a sentinel.
    libzstd tolerates jump-table off-by-one, extra bits, wrong regen and zero last bytes in 4-stream mode.
 5. The sequences bitstream must be exactly consumed. Reading past its start is an error rather
    than zero-filled, for example the 16 ML extra bits of ML code 52 with an empty stream.
 6. More than 128 KiB of sequence output in one block (libzstd accepted 131073 in some cases).
 7. Offset 0 from a repeat (LL=0, OV=3, rep1=1) -> "invalid repeat offset".
 8. nbSeq=0 followed by extra bytes, in any nbSeq form.
 9. FCS = 2^64-1 is compared literally.
10. Empty input is an error (libzstd returns empty).
11. A non-zero DID is always rejected (libzstd says "Dictionary mismatch").
    Trailing garbage is rejected, the same as libzstd.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------
D. TRUNCATION SWEEPS (sweep/*, sweep_summary.json)
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Frames tested: libzstd level 1; level 3 with checksum; level 19 with checksum; level 3 multi-block
with checksum (4 compressed blocks + 1 raw); level 1 without content size, with checksum.
Each was truncated at every length 0..len-1. The message depends ONLY on the region where the cut falls:
  L = 0                                          -> empty input
  L = 1..3                                       -> truncated frame
  L = 4 .. end of frame header                   -> truncated frame header
  cut inside or at the start of a block header   -> truncated block header
  cut inside a compressed block's content        -> truncated compressed block
      The block is never partially parsed.
  cut inside a raw block's content               -> truncated raw block
  cut at or inside the 4 checksum bytes          -> truncated content checksum
  full frame                                     -> OK, output identical to the input

------------------------------------------------------------------------------
E. VALID DATA
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
722 libzstd 1.5.5 frames all decode byte-identically. They cover:
  * levels -7..22;
  * with and without checksum and content size;
  * windowLog 10/12/27 + LDM, minMatch 3, strategies 1/9, flushes giving 150 blocks;
  * concatenated frames, empty and 1-byte inputs, inputs from 0 B to 600 KB;
  * RLE literals, all four literal size formats, treeless literals, FSE-compressed Huffman weights;
  * every literals and sequence-mode combination, nbSeq 1- and 2-byte forms (3-byte form crafted).
359 of the small ones are in cases.json under valid/*.

Speed note: in this runtime, producing the output Buffer costs about 1 s per MiB, so outputs near
the 1 MiB cap are slow. That is not a zstd behaviour.

    3 repeat: no table yet for this field in this frame
                                                    -> "zstd: repeat mode without a previous sequence table"
           Predefined and RLE tables count as tables. A block with nbSeq=0 sets nothing and keeps
           earlier tables. Raw/RLE blocks keep tables. Tables reset at each frame.
  bitstream = rest of block; 0 bytes                -> "zstd: missing sequences bitstream"
      last byte 0                                   -> "zstd: bitstream missing sentinel bit"

NCOUNT (FSE table description) READER, shared by Huffman weights and LL/OF/ML
  AL = (low nibble) + 5; AL > max                   -> "zstd: FSE accuracy log too large"
  Bit parsing is the standard FSE_readNCount. Bits past the available bytes read as ZERO; the
  over-read is only judged after the parse (rules above).
  Alphabet size N = 255 (Huffman weights; only symbols 0..254 are usable), 36 (LL), 32 (OF), 53 (ML).
  Quirky boundary: during parsing ONE extra index (== N) is tolerated.
      count needed for index > N                    -> "zstd: too many symbols in FSE distribution"
      zero-repeat flags advancing past N            -> "zstd: too many symbols in FSE distribution"
      parse ends (remaining == 1) but the distribution uses index N
                                                    -> "zstd: corrupted FSE distribution"
  Over-subscription cannot be encoded. Under-subscription shows up as one of the two errors above.

SEQUENCE DECODE AND EXECUTE (interleaved per sequence)
  Initial states LL, OF, ML: not enough bits        -> "zstd: truncated sequences bitstream"
  For each sequence:
    1. Read OF extra bits, then ML extra bits, then LL extra bits.
       Any read past the start                     -> "zstd: truncated sequences bitstream"
       All of a sequence's bits are read before it executes.
    2. Resolve the offset. Repeat offsets work as in the RFC and persist across blocks; they reset per frame.
    3. LL > literals remaining                      -> "zstd: sequence literals overrun"
    4. offset == 0                                  -> "zstd: invalid repeat offset"
           Only possible with LL==0, OV==3 and rep1==1.
    5. Copy LL literals.
       offset > TOTAL bytes output so far in this call (all previous frames included)
                                                    -> "zstd: sequence offset too far back"
           Skippable frame content does not count.
    6. Running sum of this block's LL+ML > 131072   -> "zstd: block regenerated size too large"
    7. Copy the match.
    8. If this is not the last sequence, update the states LL, ML, OF.
       Out of bits                                  -> "zstd: truncated sequences bitstream"
           This happens AFTER the previous sequence executed.
  After the last sequence (no state update):
    bits left                                       -> "zstd: sequences bitstream not fully consumed"
  Then the remaining literals are appended. They are NOT counted in the 131072 limit.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------
B. ALL 55 MESSAGES
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Each message has "zstd: " in front.
Each trigger is in section A. Example vectors are in cases.json; names are given as group/name.

Frame level
  empty input
  truncated frame
  bad magic number
  truncated skippable frame
  truncated frame header
  reserved frame header bit set
  dictionary frames are not supported
  frame content size mismatch
  truncated content checksum
  content checksum mismatch

Block level
  truncated block header
  block size exceeds maximum
  reserved block type
  truncated raw block
  truncated RLE block
  truncated compressed block
  block regenerated size too large

Literals
  missing literals section header
  truncated literals section
  literals section too large
  treeless literals without a previous Huffman table
  truncated literals jump table
  literals jump table exceeds section
  corrupted 4-stream literals sizes
  empty bitstream
  bitstream missing sentinel bit
      Shared by Huffman streams, the weights FSE stream and the sequences stream.
  Huffman stream overrun
  Huffman stream not fully consumed

Huffman tree
  missing Huffman tree header
  truncated Huffman weights
  truncated Huffman tree description
  truncated Huffman weights bitstream
  too many Huffman weights
  Huffman weight too large
  empty Huffman table
  Huffman code length too large
  corrupted Huffman weights

FSE (NCount)
  FSE accuracy log too large
  too many symbols in FSE distribution
  corrupted FSE distribution
  truncated FSE table description

Sequences
  missing sequences section header
  truncated sequences header
  trailing bytes after empty sequences section
  missing sequence compression modes
  reserved sequence mode bits set
  truncated RLE sequence table
  RLE sequence symbol out of range
  repeat mode without a previous sequence table
  missing sequences bitstream
  truncated sequences bitstream
  sequences bitstream not fully consumed
  sequence literals overrun
  sequence offset too far back
  invalid repeat offset

Not from zstd:
  Output larger than 1,048,576 bytes gives RangeError "Invalid typed array length".
  This is a runtime-wide cap on typed arrays: Buffer.alloc(1048577) and new Uint8Array(1048577)
  throw the same error. It is thrown only AFTER the whole input decoded without error, so any
  zstd error, including trailing garbage or a bad checksum, wins.
  The options argument is ignored; maxOutputLength has no effect.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------
C. LAX: the original accepts what libzstd or a strict spec reading rejects
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 1. Window descriptor ignored. Exponent up to 31 is fine (libzstd: "too much memory" above 2^27).
    Blocks larger than the window are fine (up to 128 KiB). Offsets larger than the window are fine.
 2. Matches can reach back into EARLIER FRAMES' output in the same call, back to the start of all
    output (extra/xframe_*, seq2/off_into_prev_frame). Skippable content cannot be reached.
 3. A block can output up to 128 KiB of sequence output plus up to 128 KiB of trailing literals.
    Example: seq3/lits131072_seq_ml1000 gives 132072 bytes, OK.
 4. 4-stream literals with regen 0, 3 or 4 are accepted.
 5. Huffman weights without the even, 2-or-more count of weight-1 symbols are accepted
    (huf/tree_two_w11, huf/tree_two_w2_no_rank1).
 6. The Huffman-weights FSE alphabet allows symbols up to 254; unused high symbols are fine.
 7. nbSeq in 2-byte form equal to 0 (0x80 0x00) is accepted; non-canonical nbSeq forms are accepted.
 8. FHD unused bit 4 is ignored.
 9. Offsets 28..31 are allowed in RLE mode and in the FSE alphabet; they fail later as "too far back".

STRICT: the original rejects what libzstd accepts
 1. RLE block larger than 131072 -> "block size exceeds maximum".
 2. Reserved bits in the sequence modes byte.
 3. Huffman maxBits 12.
 4. Every Huffman stream must be exactly consumed and have a sentinel.
    libzstd tolerates jump-table off-by-one, extra bits, wrong regen and zero last bytes in 4-stream mode.
 5. The sequences bitstream must be exactly consumed. Reading past its start is an error rather
    than zero-filled, for example the 16 ML extra bits of ML code 52 with an empty stream.
 6. More than 128 KiB of sequence output in one block (libzstd accepted 131073 in some cases).
 7. Offset 0 from a repeat (LL=0, OV=3, rep1=1) -> "invalid repeat offset".
 8. nbSeq=0 followed by extra bytes, in any nbSeq form.
 9. FCS = 2^64-1 is compared literally.
10. Empty input is an error (libzstd returns empty).
11. A non-zero DID is always rejected (libzstd says "Dictionary mismatch").
    Trailing garbage is rejected, the same as libzstd.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------
D. TRUNCATION SWEEPS (sweep/*, sweep_summary.json)
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Frames tested: libzstd level 1; level 3 with checksum; level 19 with checksum; level 3 multi-block
with checksum (4 compressed blocks + 1 raw); level 1 without content size, with checksum.
Each was truncated at every length 0..len-1. The message depends ONLY on the region where the cut falls:
  L = 0                                          -> empty input
  L = 1..3                                       -> truncated frame
  L = 4 .. end of frame header                   -> truncated frame header
  cut inside or at the start of a block header   -> truncated block header
  cut inside a compressed block's content        -> truncated compressed block
      The block is never partially parsed.
  cut inside a raw block's content               -> truncated raw block
  cut at or inside the 4 checksum bytes          -> truncated content checksum
  full frame                                     -> OK, output identical to the input

------------------------------------------------------------------------------
E. VALID DATA
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
722 libzstd 1.5.5 frames all decode byte-identically. They cover:
  * levels -7..22;
  * with and without checksum and content size;
  * windowLog 10/12/27 + LDM, minMatch 3, strategies 1/9, flushes giving 150 blocks;
  * concatenated frames, empty and 1-byte inputs, inputs from 0 B to 600 KB;
  * RLE literals, all four literal size formats, treeless literals, FSE-compressed Huffman weights;
  * every literals and sequence-mode combination, nbSeq 1- and 2-byte forms (3-byte form crafted).
359 of the small ones are in cases.json under valid/*.

Speed note: in this runtime, producing the output Buffer costs about 1 s per MiB, so outputs near
the 1 MiB cap are slow. That is not a zstd behaviour.

def read_ncount(data, maxsym, maxlog):
    """zero-padded NCount reader. returns (norm, log, consumed_bytes)"""
    val = int.from_bytes(bytes(data), 'little')
    bitpos = 0
    def get(nb):
        return (val >> bitpos) & ((1 << nb) - 1)
    log = get(4) + 5
    bitpos += 4
    if log > maxlog:
        err('FSE accuracy log too large')
    remaining = (1 << log) + 1
    threshold = 1 << log
    nbBits = log + 1
    norm = []
    prev0 = False
    N = maxsym + 1   # alphabet size; the reader tolerates ONE extra symbol index (== N) during parsing
    while remaining > 1:
        if len(norm) > N:
            err('too many symbols in FSE distribution')
        if prev0:
            while True:
                r = get(2)
                bitpos += 2
                norm.extend([0] * r)
                if r != 3:
                    break
            if len(norm) > N:
                err('too many symbols in FSE distribution')
        mx = (2 * threshold - 1) - remaining
        low = get(nbBits - 1)
        if low < mx:
            count = low
            bitpos += nbBits - 1
        else:
            count = get(nbBits)
            if count >= threshold:
                count -= mx
            bitpos += nbBits
        count -= 1
        remaining -= abs(count)
        norm.append(count)
        prev0 = (count == 0)
        while remaining < threshold:
            nbBits -= 1
            threshold >>= 1
    if len(norm) > N:
        err('corrupted FSE distribution')
    return norm, log, (bitpos + 7) // 8

steps.message:
I've catalogued the original's zstd decoder: 55 distinct error messages, each with its exact trigger and its precedence over the others. I also wrote an executable Python model of it, `/tmp/agent_c/model.py` (it uses `zt.py`). The model matched the original exactly (message, precedence and output bytes) on all 3222 vectors, on about 142,000 fuzzed inputs (random mutations and randomly built frames), and on 722 valid libzstd frames. Porting `model.py` to Rust reproduces the original's behaviour exactly.

All messages start with `zstd: ` (omitted below). Errors are plain `Error`s, and the first error found aborts the whole call with no partial output.

**Precedence below is the order the checks run; the first one that fails wins.**

**Top level**
- Empty input → `empty input` (libzstd returns an empty result instead).
- At each frame boundary (the start, or after any frame):
  - 1–3 bytes left → `truncated frame`.
  - Skippable magic (`0x184D2A50`–`5F`), with fewer than 8 bytes or a declared size larger than the rest of the input → `truncated skippable frame`. Otherwise it is skipped and outputs nothing; skippable-only input gives an empty Buffer.
  - Any other magic that isn't `0xFD2FB528`, including legacy zstd magics → `bad magic number`.
- Trailing junk is always rejected: 1–3 bytes → `truncated frame`, 4 or more → `bad magic number`.

**Frame header** (fields read in order, each checked immediately)
1. Missing FHD byte → `truncated frame header`.
2. Reserved bit 3 set → `reserved frame header bit set`, before any truncation check. Unused bit 4 is ignored.
3. Window byte missing (when not single-segment) → `truncated frame header`. Its value is otherwise ignored: no window limit anywhere.
4. Dictionary ID incomplete → `truncated frame header`; non-zero → `dictionary frames are not supported`. This is checked before the content-size field. A zero ID of any width is fine.
5. Content-size field incomplete → `truncated frame header`.
- Huffman table, the three sequence tables and the repeat offsets reset at every frame.

**Blocks**
1. Fewer than 3 header bytes → `truncated block header`. This includes a non-last block at end of input.
2. Size over 131072, for any block type including RLE and reserved → `block size exceeds maximum`. This comes before the type check.
3. Type 3 → `reserved block type`.
4. Missing content → `truncated raw block`, `truncated RLE block` (1 byte) or `truncated compressed block`. A compressed block must be complete before any of it is parsed.
- After the last block:
  - Content size given but not equal to the frame's output → `frame content size mismatch`. Checked only here, never per block; `2^64-1` is compared literally.
  - Then fewer than 4 checksum bytes → `truncated content checksum`.
  - Then a wrong checksum (low 32 bits of XXH64 of this frame's output only) → `content checksum mismatch`.

**Literals section**
1. Empty block → `missing literals section header`.
2. Header bytes missing → `truncated literals section`.
3. Regenerated size over 131072 → `literals section too large`. This comes before checking that the content is present.
4. Raw bytes, the RLE byte, or the compressed size running past the block → `truncated literals section`.
5. Compressed type: parse the Huffman tree. Treeless type with no table yet in this frame → `treeless literals without a previous Huffman table`. The table survives raw/RLE blocks and the latest one wins.
6. Four streams:
   - Fewer than 6 bytes for the jump table → `truncated literals jump table`.
   - Jump-table sizes adding up past the section → `literals jump table exceeds section`.
   - With seg = ceil(regen/4), 3×seg > regen → `corrupted 4-stream literals sizes`. This only happens for regen 1, 2 and 5; 0, 3 and 4 are accepted.
   - Streams are then decoded strictly one after another.
7. Each Huffman stream:
   - 0 bytes, even if it decodes 0 symbols → `empty bitstream`.
   - Last byte zero → `bitstream missing sentinel bit`.
   - A code longer than the bits left → `Huffman stream overrun`.
   - Bits left over at the end → `Huffman stream not fully consumed`.
- The literals are fully decoded before the sequences header is read.

**Huffman tree**
1. Compressed size 0 → `missing Huffman tree header`.
2. Direct weights (header byte 128 or more) running past the section → `truncated Huffman weights`.
3. FSE-compressed weights:
   - Description longer than the section → `truncated Huffman tree description`.
   - FSE table parse errors (see below).
   - No room left for the weights bitstream, or fewer than 2×accuracy-log bits in it → `truncated Huffman weights bitstream`.
   - Last byte zero → `bitstream missing sentinel bit`.
   - The weights bitstream stops exactly where libzstd's does (checked, including its edge case).
   - More than 255 weights → `too many Huffman weights`.
4. Weight validation, in this order:
   - Any weight over 11 → `Huffman weight too large`.
   - Weight sum 0 → `empty Huffman table`.
   - Implied maximum code length over 11 → `Huffman code length too large` (libzstd allows 12).
   - Remainder not a power of two → `corrupted Huffman weights`.
- There is no libzstd "even number of weight-1 symbols" check.

**Sequences header and tables**
1. No bytes left → `missing sequences section header`.
2. Sequence count bytes cut short → `truncated sequences header`. Non-canonical count forms are accepted, including `80 00` meaning zero.
3. Count 0 followed by more bytes → `trailing bytes after empty sequences section`.
4. No modes byte → `missing sequence compression modes`.
5. Low two bits of the modes byte set → `reserved sequence mode bits set` (libzstd ignores them).
6. Tables are read in order literal-length, offset, match-length:
   - RLE: byte missing → `truncated RLE sequence table`; symbol over 35/31/52 → `RLE sequence symbol out of range`.
   - FSE: parse errors, then the description running past the block end → `truncated FSE table description`.
   - Repeat with no table yet in this frame → `repeat mode without a previous sequence table`. Predefined and RLE tables count; blocks with zero sequences keep the old tables.
7. Empty bitstream → `missing sequences bitstream`; last byte zero → `bitstream missing sentinel bit`.

**FSE table descriptions (shared by weights and sequences)**
- Accuracy log too big (6 for weights; 9, 8, 9 for literal-length, offset, match-length) → `FSE accuracy log too large`.
- Bits past the available bytes read as zero.
- Alphabet sizes are 255 for weights (only symbols 0–254 usable), 36, 32 and 53. One quirk at the boundary:
  - Needing a count beyond index N, or zero-runs skipping past N → `too many symbols in FSE distribution`.
  - A finished distribution that uses index N exactly → `corrupted FSE distribution`.

**Decoding and running sequences** (one sequence at a time)
- Not enough bits for the initial states, or for any sequence's extra bits (offset, then match length, then literal length) → `truncated sequences bitstream`.
- For each sequence, after its bits are read:
  1. Literal length beyond the remaining literals → `sequence literals overrun`.
  2. Offset 0 (literal length 0, offset value 3, first repeat offset 1) → `invalid repeat offset`.
  3. Copy the literals.
  4. Offset larger than everything output so far in this call, earlier frames included → `sequence offset too far back`.
  5. Running total of this block's literal + match lengths over 131072 → `block regenerated size too large`.
  6. Copy the match.
  7. Unless it's the last sequence, update the states (running out of bits → `truncated sequences bitstream`).
- After the last sequence, bits left → `sequences bitstream not fully consumed`. The remaining literals are then appended and are not counted toward 131072.

**More lenient than libzstd / the spec**
- The window descriptor is ignored, so blocks and offsets beyond the window are fine.
- Matches can reach into earlier frames' output in the same call (not into skippable content).
- A block can output up to 128 KiB from sequences plus up to 128 KiB of trailing literals.
- The other acceptances (4-stream sizes 0/3/4, the missing weight-1 rule, the 254-symbol weights alphabet, `80 00` as zero) are noted in the sections above.

**Stricter than libzstd**
- RLE blocks over 128 KiB are rejected.
- Reserved mode bits are rejected.
- Huffman code length 12 is rejected.
- Huffman and sequence bitstreams must be consumed exactly.
- Offset 0 is rejected.
- Bytes after a zero sequence count are rejected.
- Empty input is rejected.
- Any non-zero dictionary ID is rejected.

**Runtime, not zstd**
- Output over 1,048,576 bytes throws RangeError "Invalid typed array length". This is a cap on every typed array in the runtime (`Buffer.alloc(1048577)` throws the same). It only happens after the whole input decoded cleanly, so any zstd error wins.
- The options argument (e.g. `maxOutputLength`) is ignored.
- Producing the output takes about 1 second per MiB.

**Truncation sweeps** (libzstd frames at levels 1, 3 and 19, with and without checksum, multi-block, no content size; cut at every length)
- The message depends only on where the cut falls:

| Cut position | Message |
|---|---|
| length 0 | `empty input` |
| length 1–3 | `truncated frame` |
| inside the frame header | `truncated frame header` |
| at or in a block header | `truncated block header` |
| inside a block's content | `truncated compressed block` / `truncated raw block` |
| in the checksum | `truncated content checksum` |

LUMEN brotliDecompressSync -- ERROR CATALOG (black-box, /tmp/orig)
=====================================================================
Vectors: /tmp/agent_b/cases.json, 1021 cases, each {name, hex, orig}. All re-verified against /tmp/orig.
Inputs are at most 1.4 KB. One OK case (out_total_1048576) has a 1 MiB output, so the file is 2.7 MB.
For non-Error throws, "orig" also has "error_type".
Crafting library: /tmp/agent_b/br.py and enc.py. Batch runner: /tmp/agent_b/runner.js (works in orig and node).

Every brotli error is a plain Error with message "brotli: <text>". Its only own property is "message":
there is no stack, code or errno.

1. MESSAGES AND EXACT TRIGGERS (19 brotli messages + 1 runtime RangeError; no others in 120k fuzz cases)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
"brotli: unexpected end of input"
    Raised by any read that needs a bit beyond the end of the input, at the moment that field or symbol
    is read. Missing bits are never treated as zero.
    - Empty input gives this error.
    - Huffman decoding may look ahead past EOF safely. A 1-bit code that ends exactly at the last input
      bit decodes fine. It fails only if the actual codeword is longer than the bits that remain.
    - Probe: a stream whose remaining literals are all the zero-bit codeword still fails when
      truncated, so there is no zero-fill.
    - Ex: "" ; "0b0180616263" (uncompressed block, then no next header).
"brotli: uncompressed block overruns input"
    ISUNCOMPRESSED=1 and the padding is valid, but MLEN > number of whole bytes left. This is checked
    up front, before any data is copied, including when 0 bytes are left.
    - Ex: "0b0180" ; "5000106162636465".
"brotli: metadata overruns input"
    Metadata block whose padding is valid, but MSKIPLEN > bytes left.
    - Ex: "6b09007879".
"brotli: large-window streams are not supported"
    The 7-bit WBITS pattern 0010001: first bit 1, then 3 bits = 0, then 3 bits = 1.
    - Raised immediately. Following bits do not matter (reserved bit 0 or 1, any 6-bit window), and
      it is raised even if the input ends there.
    - Ex: "11", "91", "11ca".
    - Every other pattern is valid: 16, 17, 18..24, 10..15. There is no other WBITS error.
"brotli: exuberant size nibble"
    MNIBBLES = 5 or 6 and the last (most significant) nibble read is 0.
    - Checked right after the nibbles, before ISUNCOMPRESSED is read; "040000" errors even though the
      input ends there.
    - Applies to uncompressed, compressed and ISLAST blocks.
    - Ex: "2b0000084103".
"brotli: reserved bit set"
    MNIBBLES field = 3 (metadata) and the reserved bit is 1. Checked immediately.
    - Ex: "eb", "eb0003".
"brotli: exuberant metadata size byte"
    MSKIPBYTES >= 2 and the last (most significant) MSKIPLEN byte is 0. Checked right after that byte,
    before padding.
    - Ex: "6b160000".
    - MSKIPBYTES=1 with byte 00 (MSKIPLEN=1) is fine.
"brotli: non-zero padding bits"
    Fill bits up to the byte boundary are not all zero, either after the metadata header (also when
    MSKIPBYTES=0) or after ISUNCOMPRESSED=1.
    - Ex: "20003061626303", "8c03".
    - NOT checked for the final padding after the last meta-block (see section 4).
"brotli: simple code symbol out of range"
    A simple prefix code (HSKIP=1) symbol >= alphabet size. Symbols are ALPHABET_BITS =
    bitlen(alphabet_size-1) bits wide.
    - Checked as each symbol is read, so an invalid first symbol errors even if the input ends right
      after it.
    - Alphabet sizes:
        literal 256 (never triggers)
        insert&copy 704 (704..1023 invalid)
        distance 16+NDIRECT+(48<<NPOSTFIX) (e.g. NDIRECT=1: 65..127 invalid; NPOSTFIX=3,NDIRECT=120: 520+)
        block type NBLTYPES+2
        block count 26 (26..31 invalid)
        context map NTREES+RLEMAX
    - Ex: "1b0300118406" (block-count symbol 26).
"brotli: duplicate simple code symbol"
    Two equal symbols in a simple code.
    - Checked only after all NSYM symbols are read and range-checked. So range wins over a duplicate
      even if the duplicate comes first, and EOF while reading later symbols wins over a duplicate.
    - Checked before the NSYM=4 tree-select bit is read.
    - Ex: "1b010000a0c2c202820004".
"brotli: corrupt code-length code"
    Complex code: the code-length-code lengths (static 2..4-bit code, read in order 1,2,3,4,0,5,17,6,16,
    7..15 starting at index HSKIP) do not form a complete code.
    - Kraft space starts at 32; each length L subtracts 32>>L; reading stops as soon as space == 0.
    - space < 0 errors immediately (no more bits read).
    - Otherwise, after all 18-HSKIP entries, space != 0 errors unless exactly one length is non-zero.
      That covers under-full and all-zero.
    - Exactly one non-zero CL length is accepted: that symbol gets a 0-bit code (e.g. only sym 8 gives
      256 x len-8; only 16 also works).
    - Ex: "1b03000080db01" (1,2,1 over-full), "1b010000800d00000020200800" (2,2 then zeros).
    - HSKIP=2/3 that skips lengths the code needs gives this error too.
"brotli: code-length run overflows alphabet"
    A 16 or 17 repeat (including consecutive-repeat growth) would assign lengths past alphabet_size.
    - A run ending exactly at the alphabet end is OK.
    - This check precedes the space check.
    - Ex: "1b0300000080e3fe1f".
"brotli: prefix code is under/over-subscribed"
    Symbol code lengths are read until the alphabet is full or space (32768) == 0; reading stops at
    space == 0 and the rest are zero.
    - Over-subscription (space < 0) errors immediately. Node instead reads to the alphabet end, so it
      often reports EOF.
    - Errors if the alphabet is exhausted with space > 0. That includes the all-zero code and a complex
      code with a single used symbol.
    - Repeat semantics match RFC/node: 16 repeats the last non-zero length (initially 8). A 0 literal
      does not change it. 17 resets the 16-chain and vice versa.
    - Ex: "1b030000803b01", "1b0300008003e0a2dad405080100".
"brotli: context map run overflows"
    An RLE zero-run (symbol s in 1..RLEMAX) would pass the map end (64*NBLTYPESL or
    4*NBLTYPESD). Checked right after the extra bits.
    - Run length = (1<<s) + an s-bit extra value.
    - Ex: "1b0300008855f000" (RLEMAX=6, run 65 in a 64-entry map).
    - "Context map value out of range" is impossible (symbols are < NTREES+RLEMAX; IMTF keeps values <
      NTREES). The only related error is the simple-code range error.
"brotli: meta-block length mismatch"
    A command produces more than the remaining MLEN.
    (a) Insert overrun: all insert_len literals are decoded first, with no MLEN check during this.
        - Then the error is raised, without reading a distance.
        - So a truncated overrun gives "unexpected end of input" (node gives BLOCK_LENGTH_1 eagerly).
        - Ex: "1b02000020c202850000" (MLEN 3, insert 5).
    (b) Copy overrun: raised after the distance is read and validated.
        - Order: invalid short distance -> dictionary length -> dictionary transform -> MLEN.
        - For dictionary words, the TRANSFORMED length counts. Copy len 8 + OmitLast3 = 5 bytes fits
          MLEN 5.
        - Ex: "1b04000020c202998000", "1b03000020c262909006" (5-byte word, MLEN 4).
    - If the inserts end exactly at MLEN, the meta-block ends: the copy part is ignored and no distance
      is read.
"brotli: invalid short distance"
    Distance codes 4..15 (last+-1..3, second-last+-1..3) give a distance <= 0. Codes 0..3 can never
    fail.
    - Ex: "1b08000020c24a11410a2206" (last=1, code 4).
"brotli: invalid dictionary reference length"
    distance > max_distance, where max_distance = min(total bytes output so far, (1<<WBITS)-16), and
    copy_len is not in 4..24.
    - Includes implicit distance and codes 0..3 at stream start (ring buffer 4,11,15,16 > pos 0).
    - Ex: "1b01000020c202900000" (copy 2, distance 4 at pos 0).
"brotli: invalid dictionary transform"
    Dictionary reference with transform = word_id >> NDBITS[len] >= 121. word_id =
    distance-max_distance-1.
    - Ex: "1b03000020c242906809c8".
"brotli: block length exhausted with a single block type"
    For a category with NBLTYPES=1 the block length is an implicit 2^24 per meta-block. Needing symbol
    2^24+1 of that category in one meta-block raises this.
    - Only reachable via an insert overrun of > 2^24 literals, counted across commands of the
      meta-block. The counter resets per meta-block.
    - Exactly 2^24 literals with MLEN 1 gives "meta-block length mismatch".
    - Ex: "1b00000020c202bf807e4fff01" (vs "...7c4fff01" = 2^24 gives mismatch).
RangeError "Invalid typed array length"  (not a brotli message)
    Decode succeeded but output > 1,048,576 bytes. This is the runtime's 1 MiB cap on any
    TypedArray/Buffer; fs.readFileSync of > 1 MiB fails the same way.
    - The decoder itself is not limited: a brotli error found after > 1 MiB of output still wins.
    - Exactly 1 MiB is OK.
    - Ex: "9f0000100020c2e2b18074ef1f00" (1 MiB + 1). Valid 6-nibble meta-blocks always hit this.

2. PARSE ORDER (first failing check wins; everything is sequential, deferred checks as noted)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Stream header:
  WBITS (marker -> large-window error).
Meta-block header, loop:
  ISLAST; [ISLASTEMPTY -> stream ends]; MNIBBLES.
  Metadata branch:
    reserved -> MSKIPBYTES -> bytes -> exuberant byte -> padding -> overrun -> skip.
    If ISLAST, end.
  Data branch:
    nibbles -> exuberant -> [ISUNCOMPRESSED if !ISLAST].
    Uncompressed: padding -> overrun -> copy.
Compressed header (RFC order):
  NBLTYPES/btype code/bcount code/first count for L, I, D -> NPOSTFIX, NDIRECT -> cmodes ->
  NTREESL + cmap -> NTREESD + cmap -> literal, command and distance codes.
Commands until remaining <= 0:
  [I switch] -> cmd symbol + insert/copy extra -> literals (each with [L switch]) ->
  [insert MLEN check] -> [stop if done] -> distance (implicit, or [D switch] + symbol + extra) ->
  short-distance check -> dict(len, transform) or copy -> MLEN check.
Semantics all confirmed equal to node on valid data:
  - Window rule max_distance = min(pos, 2^WBITS-16) holds (WBITS=10: d=1008 copies, d=1009 is a
    dictionary word).
  - Dictionary refs and code 0 do not update the distance ring buffer.
  - Block-type ring buffer starts at (1,0); sym0 = second-to-last, sym1 = last+1 mod N, else sym-2.
  - All 26 block-count codes.
  - NBLTYPES 1..256 (varlen8 caps at 256; >256 is not encodable).
  - NTREES up to 256; RLEMAX 1..16 and IMTF.
  - Context modes 0..3 (MSB6 too, which node never emits).
  - NPOSTFIX 0..3 and NDIRECT up to 120.
  - Zero-length transformed words are accepted.

3. EOF / TRUNCATION SUMMARY
--------------------------
Node streams q5/q11 (one meta-block, 344..7059 B) and flush-built 5-meta-block streams (490/497 B,
including an uncompressed block) were cut at every length.
- Every prefix gives "unexpected end of input".
- Exception: prefixes that end inside an uncompressed block's payload, with the header complete
  and 0..MLEN-1 payload bytes present, give "uncompressed block overruns input". Full length gives OK.
- 29k prefixes of 250 crafted valid vectors gave only those two messages, plus "metadata overruns
  input" inside metadata payloads. OK only appeared when nothing but trailing garbage was removed.

4. LAX BEHAVIOURS / DIFFERENCES FROM NODE
----------------------------------------
- Final padding is NOT checked (node: ERR__ERROR_FORMAT_PADDING_2). This covers the bits after
  ISLAST+ISLASTEMPTY and after a compressed ISLAST block.
  - "deadbeef" -> OK empty. Also "fb" -> OK, "81ff" -> OK.
  - Example "1b040000a0cbd0d8de040a01488d" -> "hello".
- Trailing bytes after the stream end are ignored (node too).
- Otherwise exactly as strict as node: in 100k differential mutated streams there was no
  orig-OK/node-fail except PADDING_2, no orig-fail/node-OK, and no differing output.
- Message mapping to node codes:
  - CL_SPACE -> corrupt code-length code
  - HUFFMAN_SPACE -> under/over-subscribed, or run overflows alphabet for repeat overflow
  - BLOCK_LENGTH_1/2 -> meta-block length mismatch (or EOF, since literals are read first)
  - DISTANCE -> invalid short distance
  - DICTIONARY -> invalid dictionary reference length
  - TRANSFORM -> invalid dictionary transform
  - CONTEXT_MAP_REPEAT -> context map run overflows
  - PADDING_1 -> non-zero padding bits
  - RESERVED -> reserved bit set
  - EXUBERANT_NIBBLE / EXUBERANT_META_NIBBLE -> exuberant size nibble / metadata size byte
  - SIMPLE_HUFFMAN_ALPHABET / SAME -> out of range / duplicate
  - WINDOW_BITS -> large-window
  - Z_BUF_ERROR -> unexpected end of input, or the two overrun messages
- Order differences from node:
  - Insert overrun: node fails before reading literals.
  - Over-subscribed code: orig fails at once, node reads on (often EOF).

5. VALID-STREAM CONFORMANCE
--------------------------
Every set matched byte-for-byte:
- 1880 node streams: q0..11, lgwin 10..24, modes 0..2, 12 inputs (0 B..40 KB).
- 69 large node streams up to 1 MiB output: LGBLOCK, NPOSTFIX/NDIRECT, disabled literal context modeling.
- 3150 random crafted valid streams: all header features, dictionary refs with all transforms,
  windows 10..24, mixed metadata/uncompressed/compressed blocks.
- An exhaustive set: 121 transforms x lengths 4..24 x 3 words.

6. INPUT ARG (side note)
------------------------
- Input is converted like Buffer.from: strings as UTF-8; arrays and ArrayBuffer are accepted.
- A DataView decodes as empty input (gives "unexpected end of input").
- Number, null or undefined -> TypeError "Buffer.from: unsupported value".
