# Guide for subagents working on the lumen reimplementation

## The project
We are reimplementing, from scratch in Rust (std only, NO external crates), a JavaScript engine +
Node/Bun-like runtime called "lumen" (CLI `lumen-cli`). The ORIGINAL compiled binary is at
`/workspace/executable` (symlink `/tmp/orig`). Our reimplementation lives in the git repo `/workspace`
(you will be working in your own git worktree copy of it). Hidden tests will run JS programs through
both binaries and compare stdout, stderr and exit code EXACTLY, so fidelity to the original's
observable behavior (output formats, error messages, property orders, edge cases) is the goal.

## Rules (strict)
- You may RUN the original (`/tmp/orig file.js`, `/tmp/orig -e 'code'`) to observe behavior.
- You MUST NOT disassemble/decompile/read the original binary's bytes, use strace/ltrace/gdb on it,
  search the internet, or download anything. No network is available anyway.
- Do not copy JS source code text of the original's internal modules verbatim (some functions print
  their JS source via `String(fn)`; you may observe *behavior*, but write your own Rust implementation).
- Write Rust (std only). Keep any scratch scripts (shell/python/JS test files) OUTSIDE the repo, e.g.
  under `/tmp/<yourname>/`. Do not add non-Rust code files to the repo.
- Only edit the files assigned to you. If a core-engine bug blocks you, work around it in your files
  if possible and describe the bug precisely in your final report (file/function, repro JS). If you
  absolutely must touch a shared file, keep the change minimal and list it in your report.
- Never run `/workspace/compile.sh` and never write to `/workspace/executable`.
- Build with `cargo build --release` in YOUR worktree (binary: `target/release/lumen`). Commit your
  work in your worktree with clear messages when done (and at milestones).
- `console.log` in lumen prints values via `String(v)` (objects print as `[object Object]`), so when
  probing the original use JSON.stringify or explicit string building.

## Engine architecture (what you need to write builtins)
Key modules (in `src/`): `value.rs` (Value, JsStr, Sym, PropKey), `object.rs` (Obj, ObjKind, Prop,
PropDesc, Args, NativeFn, flags WRITABLE/ENUMERABLE/CONFIGURABLE, WEC, WC), `vm.rs` (Vm, JsResult,
calls, errors, frames, Job), `props.rs` (property internal methods on Vm), `ops.rs` (conversions),
`realm.rs` (intrinsics + helpers to define builtins), `builtins/*` (ECMAScript builtins),
`runtime/*` (node/web runtime), `runtime/mod.rs` (Host state, event loop), `modules.rs` (ESM).

### Values
```rust
enum Value { Undefined, Null, Bool(bool), Num(f64), Str(JsStr), Sym(Sym), BigInt(Rc<BigInt>), Obj(Obj), Empty /*internal*/ }
JsStr::from_str("x"), s.to_rust_string(), s.units() -> &[u16] (UTF-16), JsStr::from_units(vec), JsStr::concat(&a,&b)
Value::str("x"), Value::Num(1.0), v.is_undefined(), v.is_nullish(), v.as_obj() -> Option<&Obj>, v.truthy(), v.is_callable()
PropKey::from_str("name"), PropKey::Str(js), PropKey::Sym(sym), PropKey::from_index(i)
```
### Natives
```rust
type NativeFn = fn(&mut Vm, &Args) -> JsResult<Value>;   // JsResult<T> = Result<T, Value /*thrown*/>
// Args: a.this (Value), a.args (&[Value]), a.arg(i) -> Value (undefined if missing), a.callee (&Obj),
//       a.new_target (Option<Obj>, Some when called with `new`), a.slot(i) -> captured data (see native_closure)
vm.native_fn("name", length, f) -> Obj                         // function object
vm.native_closure("name", length, f, vec![slot0, slot1]) -> Obj // with captured Values (read via a.slot(i))
vm.def_method(&obj, "name", length, f) -> Obj                    // non-enumerable writable configurable method
vm.def_getter(&obj, "name", f); vm.def_accessor(&obj, "name", getter, setter)
vm.native_ctor("Name", length, f, &proto) -> Obj   // constructor; links proto.constructor & ctor.prototype
// In a constructor native: let p = vm.proto_from_nt(&a.new_target, &fallback_proto)?; Obj::new(Some(p), kind)
vm.make_ctor(&fobj)  // mark a native fn as constructible
vm.def_global("Name", Value::Obj(o)); vm.set_tag(&obj, "Tag") // Symbol.toStringTag
```
### Objects
```rust
vm.new_object() -> Obj (plain, Object.prototype); vm.obj_from(vec![("k", v), ...]) -> Obj (enumerable props)
vm.new_array(vec![...]) -> Obj; Obj::new(proto: Option<Obj>, ObjKind::Ordinary)
o.set_str("k", v, WEC); o.set_prop(PropKey, v, flags); o.get_own_str("k") -> Option<Value> (own data only)
o.borrow() / o.borrow_mut()  (RefCell — never hold a borrow across a call into JS!)
// custom native state: Obj::new(Some(proto), ObjKind::Host(Box::new(MyState{..}))) and later
//   if let ObjKind::Host(h) = &o.borrow().kind { if let Some(s) = h.downcast_ref::<MyState>() {..} }
//   (use Cell/RefCell inside MyState for mutation)
crate::runtime::reorder_enum(vm, &obj, &["a","b",...]) // force enumerable key order (missing -> noop fns)
```
### Property access / conversions (all on `vm`)
```rust
vm.get(&obj, &key, &receiver_value)?; vm.get_str(&obj, "name")?; vm.get_prop_of(&value, &key)? (works on primitives)
vm.set_prop_of(&value, key, v, /*strict*/ true)?; vm.create_data_property(&obj, key, v)?
vm.has_property(&obj, &key)?; vm.delete(&obj, &key)?; vm.own_property_keys(&obj)?; vm.enumerable_own_keys(&obj)?
vm.to_string(&v)? -> JsStr; vm.to_number(&v)?; vm.to_object(&v)?; vm.to_property_key(&v)?; vm.to_index(&v)?
vm.to_integer_or_infinity(&v)?; vm.to_int32/to_uint32; vm.to_primitive(&v, crate::ops::Hint::Default)?
crate::runtime::display_value(vm, &v) -> String   // what console.log prints for a value
crate::runtime::util::inspect_value(vm, &v, depth)? -> String  // util.inspect
crate::runtime::util::describe_received(vm, &v) -> String // Node-style "Received type number (5)"
vm.call(&f, this, &args)?; vm.construct(&ctor, &args, None)?; vm.iterate_to_vec(&iterable)?
crate::builtins::array::array_like_to_vec(vm, &v)?
```
### Errors
```rust
return vm.throw_type("message");   // also throw_range, throw_ref, throw_syntax, throw_error("URIError", msg)
let e = vm.make_error("TypeError", "msg"); if let Value::Obj(o) = &e { o.set_prop(PropKey::from_str("code"), Value::str("ERR_X"), WEC); } return Err(e);
```
### Promises / async / event loop
```rust
let cap = vm.new_promise_capability_intrinsic(); // Capability { promise, resolve, reject }
vm.call(&cap.resolve, Value::Undefined, &[v])?; return Ok(cap.promise);
crate::builtins::promise::promise_then(vm, &promise_obj, on_fulfilled_fn_value, on_rejected_fn_value)?
crate::builtins::promise::perform_then_internal(vm, &p, Handler::Native(f, data), Handler::Native(g, data), None)
   // f: fn(&mut Vm, Value /*result*/, &Value /*data*/) -> JsResult<Value>
vm.jobs.push_back(crate::vm::Job::Callback(f, args));      // microtask
vm.host.callbacks.push_back((f, args));                     // macrotask (setImmediate-like queue)
crate::runtime::timers::add_timer(vm, cb, delay_ms, args, repeat) -> id
crate::runtime::spawn_op(vm, move || { /* runs on a thread, return T: Send */ }, move |vm, t: T| { /* back on loop thread */ });
   // keeps the event loop alive until `then` runs. Never move Values/Objs into the thread closure.
```

```rust
crate::runtime::buffer::new_buffer_value(vm, bytes)?      // Node Buffer (Uint8Array subclass)
crate::runtime::buffer::bytes_of(vm, &v)?                  // bytes of string(utf8)/Buffer/TypedArray/ArrayBuffer/array
crate::builtins::typedarray::ta_bytes(&obj)                // bytes of TypedArray/ArrayBuffer/DataView

crate::runtime::buffer::{encode_string, decode_bytes, norm_encoding}   // node encodings
crate::runtime::encoding::{base64_encode, base64_decode_strict, hex_encode, utf16_to_utf8, utf8_to_utf16}
```
### EventEmitter helpers
`crate::runtime::events::{install_methods(vm,&proto), init_emitter(vm,&obj), emit_event(vm,&this_value,&Value::str("evt"),&args)?}`
and `create_module(vm)` returns the EventEmitter constructor (also cached via `crate::runtime::node::builtin_module(vm, "events")?`).

### Module registry
`crate::runtime::node::builtin_module(vm, "name")? -> Option<Value>` returns (cached) exports of a node
builtin (used by `require`, `import`, `process.getBuiltinModule`). The dispatch is in
`runtime/node.rs::builtin_module`; your module's `create_module(vm, name)` is already wired.
Globals are installed by `setup(vm)` functions called from `runtime/mod.rs::setup_runtime`.

# lumen

A from-scratch JavaScript **engine** in Rust — std only, zero dependencies — and a
**runtime** being built on top of it, the way Node/Deno/Bun wrap a JS engine with an event
loop and host APIs. Every crate in the workspace is std-only: no `tokio`, `mio`, `libc`,
`rustyline`, `serde`, or any other third-party dependency, anywhere.

## The engine (`crates/lumen`)

A lexer, parser, and **three execution tiers**:

- a **tree-walking interpreter** — the reference oracle: the spec semantics live here, and
  every other tier must match it observably (a differential fuzzer, `lumen-difftest`, holds
  them to that);
- an opt-in **bytecode VM** — functions compile whole (or not at all — no deoptimization) to
  a stack machine with slot-homed locals, per-site inline caches for property and free-name
  access backed by object shapes (hidden classes), and dense-array element fast paths;
- a **native template JIT** — bytecode lowers to real ARM64 machine code on macOS, Linux,
  and Windows, with a correctness-first x86-64 backend on Intel macOS, Linux, and Windows:
  per-op templates with the interpreter as the shared slow path, inline-cache reads baked
  into the instruction stream, fused compare-and-branch, exact-`ToInt32` bitops, and numeric
  *register chains* that keep runs of arithmetic entirely in FP registers. The full set of
  inline fast paths currently lives in the ARM64 backend; x86-64 starts with native control
  flow and checked per-op helpers. Other architectures degrade to the bytecode VM.

Tier selection: `--tier=interp|bytecode|jit` (**jit is the default**; where the JIT is
unavailable it degrades to the bytecode VM). Functions tier up after a call-count threshold —
immediately if the body contains a loop. Force the reference tree-walker with `--tier=interp`
(or `LUMEN_TIER=interp`).

The language surface: generators and `async`/`await` running on stackful coroutines (async
bodies suspend on the bytecode VM itself), full `RegExp` (including `\p{…}` and inline
modifiers), typed arrays, `Proxy`/`Reflect`, ES modules (top-level await, `import defer`,
source phase), `Intl`, and `Temporal`.

`Intl` (ECMA-402) and `Temporal` are behind the default-on `intl` and `temporal` Cargo features.
The CLDR data tables included by `intl` are the largest single contributor to binary size (~3 MB
of the release binary). Build with `--no-default-features` for a small engine: the `Intl` and
`Temporal` globals are absent, `Date.prototype.toTemporalInstant` is omitted, and the `toLocale*`
methods degrade to their locale-independent forms, the way engines built without i18n do. Either
feature can be enabled independently.

On dependencies and `unsafe`: the workspace stays std-only — the JIT maps executable memory
through raw platform declarations (`mmap`/`mprotect`, macOS `MAP_JIT`, or Windows
`VirtualAlloc`/`VirtualProtect`) rather than libc. Pages are writable only while code is copied,
then executable/read-only, and instruction caches are synchronized where required. The
interpreter and bytecode VM are safe Rust; `unsafe` is concentrated where machine
code meets the object graph (the JIT's executable pages and its templates' raw reads — every
baked offset is *measured at runtime* against the live types and fails closed to the checked
helper if anything doesn't hold) and in the N-API addon loader's `dlopen` bridge.

**Passes 100% of [tc39/test262](https://github.com/tc39/test262): 53,400/53,400** (including
annexB, intl402, and staging) — on the default JIT tier and under `LUMEN_TIER=interp`.

Extracted from — and used by — the [lucid-softworks/browser](https://github.com/lucid-softworks/browser)
engine as its JS backend (`backend-lumen`), with full git history.

## The runtime

A curated `embed` API on the engine exposes just enough — native-function registration, a
typed host-state slot, and event-loop hooks — for a runtime layer to be assembled from
independent op crates, without leaking the interpreter's internals into the published API.
On top of that:

- **Event loop** (`lumen-runtime`) — a single loop thread owns the (`!Send`) engine; blocking
  work runs on a std thread pool and completes back over `mpsc`. No epoll/kqueue reactor
  (that would need raw syscalls); the thread-pool-plus-completion model is libuv's own fs
  strategy. Each turn drains microtasks, queued callbacks, due timers, and I/O completions,
  then blocks until the next event.
- **Timers** (`lumen-timers`) — `setTimeout`/`setInterval`/`clearTimeout`/`clearInterval`/
  `setImmediate`, plus `queueMicrotask`.
- **`console` and `process`** — streaming `console.*`; `process.argv`/`env`/`platform`/
  `cwd()`/`exit()`/`nextTick()`.
- **Filesystem** (`lumen-fs`) — synchronous ops (`readFileSync`, `writeFileSync`,
  `existsSync`, `mkdirSync`, `readdirSync`, …), file handles via a resource table
  (`openSync`/`readSync`/`writeSync`/`closeSync`), and async `fs.promises.readFile`/
  `writeFile` on the thread pool.
- **Web platform** (`lumen-web`) — a growing slice of the WinterTC Minimum Common API:
  `Event`/`EventTarget`/`CustomEvent`/`AbortController`/`AbortSignal`/`DOMException`,
  `TextEncoder`/`TextDecoder`, `atob`/`btoa`, `structuredClone`, `URL`/`URLSearchParams`,
  `performance.now()`, `crypto.getRandomValues`/`randomUUID`/`subtle.digest` (SHA-256), and
  `fetch`/`Headers`/`Request`/`Response`. See the checklist at the top of
  `crates/lumen-web/src/lib.rs` for what's implemented vs. deferred (streams, `Blob`/
  `FormData`, `URLPattern`, …).

  `fetch` speaks HTTP/1.1 over `std::net`. **`https:` is not supported**: TLS cannot be
  implemented on std alone and no third-party crate is permitted, so `https` URLs reject with
  a clear error; plain `http` works.

  `Lumen.serve((request) => Response)` is the matching HTTP/1.1 **server** — not a WinterTC API,
  but the cross-runtime `serve(handler)` convention (Deno/Bun/Workers), so a Hono app runs with
  `Lumen.serve(app.fetch)`. v1 is single-accept, `Connection: close`, buffered bodies, http only
  (see `crates/lumen-web/src/server.rs`). Cold-start and usage: `examples/hono-app`.

- **Modules — both CommonJS and ESM.** `lumen-cli` picks the module kind the way Node does:
  `.mjs` is ESM, `.cjs` is CommonJS, `.js` follows the nearest `package.json` `"type"`. ES
  modules run through the engine's real module graph (linking, top-level `await`); `import`
  specifiers resolve against disk and `node_modules`, `node:` builtins are importable
  (named imports included), and CommonJS packages interop by default export. CommonJS files
  run as the program entry with `require.main === module`.

results.content:
run as the program entry with `require.main === module`.

- **`node:` compatibility** (`lumen-node`) — a CommonJS `require` with `node_modules`
  resolution and the module wrapper, `package.json` `main`/`exports`, the `node:path`/
  `node:os`/`node:fs` builtins, and `Buffer`, so packages written against the `node:` surface
  run. See the checklist at the top of `crates/lumen-node/src/lib.rs` for the deferred pieces
  (subpath-pattern exports, the full N-API surface).

  **Native addons** load too: `require('./addon.node')` dlopens the compiled library and runs its
  N-API registration, resolving the addon's `napi_*` symbols against the lumen executable — the
  same mechanism the `node` binary uses. The N-API surface is implemented from scratch (values,
  properties, functions, callbacks, errors, references, object wrap, classes, promises, buffers,
  typed arrays, async work); the loader reaches `dlopen`/`dlsym` through raw `extern "C"`
  declarations, so no third-party crate is added. See `examples/native-addon`.

  **`vite build` runs on lumen** (`examples/vite-app`): a full Vite production build, bundling
  through Rollup's native N-API addon, transforming with esbuild's service subprocess, over
  ESM↔CommonJS interop and the `node:` surface — building `dist/` and exiting cleanly.

- **REPL + CLI** (`lumen-repl`, `lumen-cli`) — an interactive shell with a persistent realm,
  parser-driven incomplete-input detection (multi-line continuation), top-level `await`, and
  loop-to-quiescence so timers and awaited promises settle before the next prompt. Line
  editing is line-buffered (raw-mode/history would need `termios`); use `rlwrap` for arrows
  and history.

### Workspace crates

```
lumen          engine (std-only, zero-dep; `embed` feature gates the runtime API)
lumen-host     substrate: OpState, ResourceTable, Extension, the thread-pool/callback primitives
lumen-timers   setTimeout/setInterval/queueMicrotask/setImmediate
lumen-fs       filesystem (sync + async)
lumen-web      WinterTC Minimum Common API (Event, URL, crypto, fetch, …)
lumen-node     node: compatibility (require, node:path/os/fs, Buffer)
lumen-runtime  the event loop; assembles the op crates; console + process
lumen-repl     interactive shell
lumen-cli      node/deno-style entrypoint

test262-runner   conformance harness (parallel workers over ./test262)
lumen-difftest   differential fuzzer across the three execution tiers
lumen-wasm       wasm build of the engine
```

The dependency graph is a strict DAG — `lumen ← lumen-host ← {op crates} ← lumen-runtime ←
lumen-repl ← lumen-cli` — so each op crate can be worked on in isolation.

## Install

Grab a nightly prebuilt runtime on macOS arm64/x86_64 or Linux x86_64/arm64 (tagged releases
also publish Windows x86_64 binaries):

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lucid-softworks/lumen/main/scripts/install.sh | bash
```

It installs the `lumen` CLI to `~/.lumen/bin` from the rolling `nightly` release
(`LUMEN_INSTALL` and `LUMEN_RELEASE` override the location and tag). Other platforms build from
source — see below.

## Usage

Run scripts / open a REPL through the runtime:

```sh
cargo build --release -p lumen-cli
./target/release/lumen-cli                 # REPL (or: lumen-cli repl)
./target/release/lumen-cli file.js [args]  # run a script to loop quiescence
./target/release/lumen-cli -e 'code'       # evaluate a string
```

The engine also ships a minimal standalone shell (the test262 host, no runtime/host APIs):

```sh
cargo build --release -p lumen --bin lumen
./target/release/lumen file.js [more.js ...]
```

## Conformance

```sh
scripts/test262-clone.sh    # one-time: clone the suite into ./test262
scripts/run-test262.sh      # run it (see crates/test262-runner for env knobs)
LUMEN_TIER=jit scripts/run-test262.sh    # same suite against the compiled tiers
```

The execution tiers are also held together by a differential fuzzer: every generated program
runs in all three tiers, which must agree on the completion value, thrown errors, the
observable side-effect trace, and final global state. Divergences are delta-minimized into a
regression corpus that replays on every run.

```sh
cargo run --release -p lumen-difftest -- --count 2000
```

#!/bin/bash
# usage: both.sh 'shell snippet using $L as the lumen binary'
# runs snippet with L=orig and L=ours (cwd /tmp/cliagent/work), compares stdout/stderr/exit
OURS=${OURS:-/workspace/.claude/worktrees/agent-ab227a21dcecddb9a/target/release/lumen}
mkdir -p /tmp/cliagent/work
cd /tmp/cliagent/work
T=$(mktemp -d /tmp/cliagent/run.XXXX)
L=/tmp/orig; export L; timeout 20 bash -c "$1" >$T/o1 2>$T/e1; c1=$?
L=$OURS; export L; timeout 20 bash -c "$1" >$T/o2 2>$T/e2; c2=$?
ok=1
if [ $c1 != $c2 ]; then echo "EXIT DIFF: orig=$c1 ours=$c2"; ok=0; fi
if ! cmp -s $T/o1 $T/o2; then echo "STDOUT DIFF:"; diff $T/o1 $T/o2 | head -${DL:-30}; ok=0; fi
if ! cmp -s $T/e1 $T/e2; then echo "STDERR DIFF:"; diff $T/e1 $T/e2 | head -${DL:-30}; ok=0; fi
if [ $ok = 1 ]; then echo "SAME (exit $c1)"; if [ -n "$SHOW" ]; then cat $T/o1; echo "--err:"; cat $T/e1; fi; fi
rm -rf $T

#!/bin/bash
# usage: suite.sh casesfile [filter]
# casesfile: blocks introduced by lines "### name"; block body is a bash snippet using $L
F=$1
FILTER=$2
name=""
body=""
pass=0; fail=0
run_block() {
  if [ -n "$name" ]; then
    if [ -z "$FILTER" ] || [[ "$name" == *$FILTER* ]]; then
      r=$(/tmp/cliagent/both.sh "$body")
      if [[ "$r" == SAME* ]]; then pass=$((pass+1)); [ -n "$VERBOSE" ] && echo "ok   $name";
      else fail=$((fail+1)); echo "FAIL $name"; echo "$r" | sed 's/^/     /'; fi
    fi
  fi
}
while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
  if [[ "$line" == "### "* ]]; then
    run_block
    name="${line#\#\#\# }"
    body=""
  else
    body+="$line"$'\n'
  fi
done < "$F"
run_block
echo "pass=$pass fail=$fail"

ok",

",

",

",

")

        while len(rest) < clen:
            chunk = conn.recv(65536)
            if not chunk:

            rest += chunk
        data = head + b"

" + rest
    except Exception as e:
        pass
    with open(logf, "ab") as f:

        path = parts[1] if len(parts) > 1 else b"/"

        if p == b"/echo":

" + body
        elif p == b"/redirectabs":

Content-Length: 0

"

" + body

slow"

import socket, sys, time

"),

4
abcd

efg
0

"),

"),
    ("http10", b"GET /old HTTP/1.0

"),
    ("badline", b"BLAH

"),
    ("lfonly", b"GET /lf HTTP/1.1
Host: y

"),
    ("abs", b"GET http://other.host/abs?x=1 HTTP/1.1
Host: z

"),
    ("dupheaders", b"GET /dup HTTP/1.1
Host: x
X-A: 1
X-A: 2
Cookie: a=1
Cookie: b=2

"),
    ("clbody", b"PUT /put HTTP/1.1
Host: x
Content-Length: 5

hello"),

Host: x:99

"),
    ("empty", b""),

Host: x

"),
    ("weirdmethod", b"FOO /weird HTTP/1.1
Host: x

"),
    ("noversion", b"GET /nov
Host: x

"),
    ("shutdown", b"GET /shutdown HTTP/1.1
Host: x

"),
]
only = sys.argv[2:]
for name, data in reqs:
    if only and name not in only:
        continue
    s = socket.socket()
    s.settimeout(3)
    try:
        s.connect(("127.0.0.1", port))
        if data:
            s.sendall(data)
        else:
            s.shutdown(socket.SHUT_WR)
        resp = b""
        while True:

        print("---", name)

    except Exception as e:

hello

``` ## `.tsx` — via esbuild TypeScript *type* stripping is not built in, so a `.tsx` file (with `interface`, `React.FC<…>` annotations) is transpiled with esbuild — which itself runs on lumen — before executing: ```sh ../../target/release/lumen-cli render.mjs app.tsx ``` `app.tsx` (a recursive component) renders a nested tree and reports its SSR time. ## How it works - **`.jsx` natively:** the runtime lowers `
hi
` to `React.createElement("div", { a: x }, "hi")` in a single scan (`crates/lumen-runtime/src/jsx.rs`) — classic runtime, so the component's own `import React` supplies the factory. The engine's parser is untouched (JSX text with apostrophes would break an up-front lexer), and the transform runs as a pre-pass on `.jsx` sources. - **`.tsx` via esbuild:** `render.mjs` runs esbuild's `tsx` loader (which strips types *and* lowers JSX). `ESBUILD_WORKER_THREADS=0` selects esbuild's subprocess path, since lumen has no worker threads. - **Module resolution:** the transpiled code keeps `import React` / `import { renderToString }` as ESM imports; lumen resolves them from `node_modules` and follows `react-dom/server`'s CommonJS re-export chain (`server.js → server.node.js → cjs/*.js`) to expose `renderToString` as a named ESM export. #!/usr/bin/env python3
import socket, sys, time
port = int(sys.argv[1])
reqs = [
    ("getbody", b"GET /gb HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: x\r\nContent-Length: 3\r\n\r\nabc"),
    ("headbody", b"HEAD /hb HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: x\r\nContent-Length: 3\r\n\r\nabc"),
    ("postempty", b"POST /pe HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: x\r\n\r\n"),
    ("postcl0", b"POST /pe0 HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: x\r\nContent-Length: 0\r\n\r\n"),
    ("expect", b"POST /ex HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: x\r\nContent-Length: 3\r\nExpect: 100-continue\r\n\r\nabc"),
    ("badclen", b"POST /bc HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: x\r\nContent-Length: abc\r\n\r\n"),
    ("twohdr", b"GET /two HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: x\r\nX-Y:no-space\r\nX-Z :  spaced  \r\n\r\n"),
    ("badhdr", b"GET /badhdr HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: x\r\nBad Header: v\r\n\r\n"),
    ("nocolon", b"GET /nocolon HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: x\r\nNoColonHere\r\n\r\n"),
    ("shutdown", b"GET /shutdown HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: x\r\n\r\n"),
]
only = sys.argv[2:]
for name, data in reqs:
    if only and name not in only:
        continue
    s = socket.socket()
    s.settimeout(3)
    try:
        s.connect(("127.0.0.1", port))
        s.sendall(data)
        resp = b""
        while True:
            try:
                c = s.recv(65536)
            except socket.timeout:
                resp += b"<<TIMEOUT>>"
                break
            if not c:
                break
            resp += c
        print("---", name)
        print(repr(resp))
    except Exception as e:
        print("---", name, "EXC", e)
    s.close()
    time.sleep(0.05)

    try:
        s.connect(("127.0.0.1", port))
        s.sendall(data)
        resp = b""
        while True:
            try:
                c = s.recv(65536)
            except socket.timeout:
                resp += b"<<TIMEOUT>>"
                break
            if not c:
                break
            resp += c
        print("---", name)
        print(repr(resp))
    except Exception as e:
        print("---", name, "EXC", e)
    s.close()
    time.sleep(0.05)

#!/bin/bash
# usage: jsxm.sh [bin] < file ; cases separated by lines '---'; each case is a JSX expression (may span lines)
# prints the transformed source (toString of an arrow returning it)
BIN=${1:-/tmp/orig}
mkdir -p /tmp/cliagent/jsxw
cd /tmp/cliagent/jsxw
run_case() {
  printf 'const f = () => %s;\nconsole.log(String(f).slice(6));\n' "$1" > m.jsx
  echo "#### $1"
  timeout 5 $BIN m.jsx 2>&1 | cat -A
}
cur=""
while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
  if [ "$line" = "---" ]; then
    run_case "$cur"; cur=""
  else
    if [ -z "$cur" ]; then cur="$line"; else cur="$cur"$'\n'"$line"; fi
  fi
done
[ -n "$cur" ] && run_case "$cur"

#!/bin/bash
# probe whether '<' is treated as JSX in various contexts; each line is a statement placed in a file
BIN=${1:-/tmp/orig}
mkdir -p /tmp/cliagent/jsxw
cd /tmp/cliagent/jsxw
while IFS= read -r line; do
  printf 'globalThis.React = { createElement: (...a) => "<" + a[0] + ">", Fragment: "F" };\nlet a = 1, b = 2, c = 3, n = 2, i = 0, x = 5, y = 6, r;\nfunction f(...z) { return z.join("|"); }\n%s\nconsole.log(String(r));\n' "$line" > c.jsx
  printf '%-40s => ' "$line"
  timeout 5 $BIN c.jsx 2>&1 | tr '\n' '|'
  echo
done

OURS=/workspace/.claude/worktrees/agent-a1153e7885bc0a64b/target/release/lumen

  rm -rf "$d"
done

# Split a bundle file into test files.  Lines "//// name.js" start a new file.
import sys, os
src = sys.argv[1]
outdir = sys.argv[2]
os.makedirs(outdir, exist_ok=True)
cur = None
buf = []
names = []
def flush():
    if cur:
        with open(os.path.join(outdir, cur), "w") as f:
            f.write("".join(buf))
        names.append(cur)
for line in open(src):
    if line.startswith("//// "):
        flush()
        cur = line[5:].strip()
        buf = []
    else:
        buf.append(line)
flush()
print(" ".join(os.path.join(outdir, n) for n in names))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# Split a bundle ("//// name.js" markers) into files and compare original vs ours.
# usage: run.py bundle.js [filter-substring...]
import sys, os, subprocess, difflib

OURS = "/workspace/.claude/worktrees/agent-a1153e7885bc0a64b/target/release/lumen"
ORIG = "/tmp/orig"
src = sys.argv[1]
filters = sys.argv[2:]
verbose = os.environ.get("V")
outdir = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(src)), "t_" + os.path.basename(src).replace(".js", ""))
os.makedirs(outdir, exist_ok=True)
files = []
cur, buf = None, []
def flush():
    if cur:
        p = os.path.join(outdir, cur)
        with open(p, "w") as f:
            f.write("".join(buf))
        files.append(p)
for line in open(src):
    if line.startswith("//// "):
        flush()
        cur = line[5:].strip()
        buf = []
    else:
        buf.append(line)
flush()

def run(binary, path):
    try:
        p = subprocess.run([binary, os.path.basename(path)], cwd=os.path.dirname(path), capture_output=True, timeout=float(os.environ.get("TO", "10")))
        return p.stdout.decode("utf-8", "replace"), p.stderr.decode("utf-8", "replace"), p.returncode
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as e:
        return (e.stdout or b"").decode("utf-8", "replace"), (e.stderr or b"").decode("utf-8", "replace") + "<<TIMEOUT>>", -999

npass = nfail = 0
for f in files:
    if filters and not any(x in os.path.basename(f) for x in filters):

    o1, e1, c1 = run(ORIG, f)
    o2, e2, c2 = run(OURS, f)
    if (o1, e1, c1) == (o2, e2, c2):
        npass += 1
        print("PASS", os.path.basename(f))

        for l in d[:lim]:
            print("   ", l)
print(f"pass={npass} fail={nfail}")

import unicodedata, sys
lines = [l for l in open('/tmp/intlagent/coll/dump_bmp.txt').read().split('\n') if l]
seq = []
for l in lines:
    cp, _, rel = l.partition(' ')
    seq.append((int(cp, 16), rel))

def nfd(c):
    return unicodedata.normalize('NFD', c)

def lower(ch):
    l = ch.lower()
    return l

def hyp_key(cp):
    c = chr(cp)
    d = nfd(c)
    prim = []
    sec = []
    ter = []
    for ch in d:
        if unicodedata.combining(ch) != 0 and prim:
            sec[-1].append(ord(ch))
            continue
        l = ch.lower()
        prim.append(tuple(ord(x) for x in l))
        sec.append([])
        ter.append(1 if ch != l else 0)
    return prim, sec, ter

# check primary order: consecutive elements must have nondecreasing primary in hypothesis, and equality iff rel[0]=='='
bad = 0
prev = None
for i, (cp, rel) in enumerate(seq):
    k = hyp_key(cp)
    if prev is not None:
        pk = prev[1]
        exp_eq = (pk[0] == k[0])
        got_eq = rel[0] == '='
        lt = pk[0] < k[0]
        if got_eq != exp_eq or (not got_eq and not lt):
            bad += 1
            if bad < 60:
                print('mismatch', hex(prev[0]), repr(chr(prev[0])), hex(cp), repr(chr(cp)), rel, pk[0], k[0])
    prev = (cp, k)
print('bad', bad, 'of', len(seq))

}

import sys
base = '/tmp/intlagent/loc/'
lang = []
und_s = []
for line in open(base + 'data1.txt'):
    p = line.split()
    if p[0] == 'L':
        k, v = p[1], p[2].split('-')
        assert v[0] == k, line
        if k == 'und':
            continue
        lang.append((k, v[1], v[2]))
    elif p[0] == 'S':
        k, v = p[1], p[2].split('-')
        und_s.append((k, v[0], v[2]))
und_r = []
lr = []
ls = []
sr = []
for line in open(base + 'combo.txt'):
    if line.startswith('#'):
        continue
    p = line.split()
    if 'Qaai' in line:
        continue
    kind, key, val = p
    v = val.split('-')
    k = key.split('-')
    if kind == 'LR':
        if k[0] == 'und':
            assert v[2] == k[1]
            und_r.append((k[1], v[0], v[1]))
        else:
            assert v[0] == k[0] and v[2] == k[1], line
            lr.append((key, v[1]))
    elif kind == 'LS':
        if k[0] == 'und':
            continue  # same as und_s
        assert v[0] == k[0] and v[1] == k[1], line
        ls.append((key, v[2]))
    elif kind == 'SR':
        assert v[1] == k[1] and v[2] == k[2], line
        sr.append((k[1] + '-' + k[2], v[0]))
lang.sort(); und_s.sort(); und_r.sort(); lr.sort(); ls.sort(); sr.sort()
out = []
out.append('//! Likely-subtags data of the original runtime (extracted by black-box')
out.append('//! queries of `Intl.Locale.prototype.maximize`; see locale.rs).')
out.append('')
def emit3(name, rows, doc):
    out.append('/// ' + doc)
    out.append('pub static %s: &[(&str, &str, &str)] = &[' % name)
    line = '   '
    for r in rows:
        item = ' ("%s", "%s", "%s"),' % r
        if len(line) + len(item) > 110:
            out.append(line)
            line = '   '
        line += item
    out.append(line)
    out.append('];')
    out.append('')
def emit2(name, rows, doc):
    out.append('/// ' + doc)
    out.append('pub static %s: &[(&str, &str)] = &[' % name)
    line = '   '
    for r in rows:
        item = ' ("%s", "%s"),' % r
        if len(line) + len(item) > 110:
            out.append(line)
            line = '   '
        line += item
    out.append(line)
    out.append('];')
    out.append('')
emit3('LANG', lang, 'language -> (script, region)')
emit3('UND_SCRIPT', und_s, 'und-Script -> (language, region)')
emit3('UND_REGION', und_r, 'und-Region -> (language, script)')
emit2('LANG_REGION', lr, '"lang-Region" -> script (where it differs from the language default)')
emit2('LANG_SCRIPT', ls, '"lang-Script" -> region (where it differs from the language default)')
emit2('UND_SCRIPT_REGION', sr, '"Script-Region" -> language (exceptions to und_R / und_S)')
open(sys.argv[1], 'w').write('\n'.join(out))
print(len(lang), len(und_s), len(und_r), len(lr), len(ls), len(sr))

// Bytecode definitions shared by compiler and VM.

use crate::ast::FuncKind;
use crate::value::*;
use std::rc::Rc;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum BindKind {
    Var,
    Let,
    Const,
    Class,
    Function,
    Param,
    CatchParam,
    /// internal bindings: this, arguments, new.target, home, private names
    Internal,
    /// the name of a named function expression (immutable, silently ignores writes in sloppy)
    FuncName,
    Import,
}

#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct ScopeInfo {
    pub names: Vec<JsStr>,
    pub kinds: Vec<BindKind>,
    pub is_function: bool,
}

impl ScopeInfo {
    pub fn find(&self, name: &JsStr) -> Option<usize> {
        self.names.iter().position(|n| n == name)
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum MethodTarget {
    Proto,
    Ctor,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum MKind {
    Method,
    Getter,
    Setter,
}

#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct TemplateData {
    pub cooked: Vec<Option<JsStr>>,
    pub raw: Vec<JsStr>,
    pub id: usize,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub enum Op {
    // constants
    Undef,
    Null,
    True,
    False,
    Int(i32),
    Const(u32),
    Empty,
    // stack
    Pop,
    Dup,
    Dup2,
    Swap,
    /// [a b c] -> [c a b]
    Rot3,
    /// [a b c d] -> [d a b c]
    Rot4,
    /// copy the value n below the top: [.. x a1..an] -> [.. x a1..an x]
    Pick(u16),
    // locals / env
    GetLocal(u32),
    GetLocalChk(u32, u32),
    SetLocal(u32),
    InitLocal(u32),
    ClearLocal(u32),
    GetEnv(u16, u32),
    GetEnvChk(u16, u32, u32),
    SetEnv(u16, u32),
    SetEnvChk(u16, u32, u32),
    InitEnv(u16, u32),
    GetName(u32),
    SetName(u32),
    TypeofName(u32),
    DeleteName(u32),
    /// pushes [this, func] for a call to an identifier (with-scope aware)
    GetNameCall(u32),
    GetGlobal(u32),
    SetGlobal(u32),
    TypeofGlobal(u32),
    /// declare global var (name, is_function)
    DeclareGlobalVar(u32),
    DeclareGlobalFunc(u32),
    DeclareGlobalLex(u32, bool),
    InitGlobalLex(u32),
    PushScope(u32),
    PopScope,
    CopyScope,
    PushWith,
    ThrowConst(u32),
    // function frame
    This,
    ThisChk,
    SetThis,
    NewTarget,
    GetArg(u32),
    GetRest(u32),
    CreateArguments(bool),
    Callee,
    Home,
    // properties
    GetProp(u32),
    GetPropOpt(u32),
    GetElem,
    SetProp(u32),
    SetElem,
    DeleteProp(u32),
    DeleteElem,
    GetSuper(u32),
    GetSuperElem,
    SetSuper(u32),
    SetSuperElem,
    GetPrivate,
    SetPrivate,
    PrivateIn,
    /// [obj] -> [obj, obj.key]  (for method calls: leaves this then func)
    GetMethod(u32),
    GetMethodElem,
    ToPropKey,
    // literals
    NewObject,
    NewArray(u32),
    ArrayPush,
    ArrayHole,
    ArraySpread,
    DefineField(u32),
    DefineFieldComputed,
    DefineAccessor(u32, MKind),
    DefineAccessorComputed(MKind),
    CopyDataProps,
    /// [target source excludedKeys...(n)] object rest
    CopyDataPropsExcept(u32),
    SetProtoLit,
    RegExp(u32),
    Template(u32),
    // functions & classes
    Closure(u32),
    /// [home] -> [home, closure]
    Method(u32),
    SetFunctionName(u8),
    /// [heritage?] -> [F, proto]
    CreateClass(u32, bool),
    /// [F proto (key)?] method definition
    DefineMethod(u32, MethodTarget, MKind, u32),
    DefineMethodComputed(MethodTarget, MKind, u32),
    /// [F proto key?] -> instance field registration (key idx or computed when u32::MAX)
    AddField(u32, u32, bool),
    AddFieldComputed(u32, bool),
    /// [F proto sym] private method/accessor for instances
    AddPrivateMethod(u32, MKind, bool),
    /// [F proto] run static field initializer with key
    StaticField(u32, u32),
    StaticFieldComputed(u32),
    /// [F proto sym]
    StaticPrivateField(u32),
    StaticBlock(u32),
    NewPrivateName(u32),
    // operators
    Add,
    Sub,
    Mul,
    Div,
    Mod,
    Exp,
    Shl,
    Shr,
    UShr,
    BitAnd,
    BitOr,
    BitXor,
    Eq,
    Ne,
    StrictEq,
    StrictNe,
    Lt,
    Le,
    Gt,
    Ge,
    In,
    InstanceOf,
    Neg,
    Plus,
    Not,
    BitNot,
    Typeof,
    Void,
    Inc,
    Dec,
    ToNumeric,
    ToStr,
    // control
    Jump(u32),
    JumpIfFalse(u32),
    JumpIfTrue(u32),
    JumpIfFalseKeep(u32),
    JumpIfTrueKeep(u32),
    JumpIfNullishKeep(u32),
    JumpIfNotNullishKeep(u32),
    /// jump if top is undefined (pops if not jumping? no: always pops)
    JumpIfNotUndef(u32),
    /// jumps if top is null or undefined (pops)
    JumpIfNullish(u32),
    Return,
    TryStart(u32),
    TryEnd,
    Throw,
    ThrowRef(u32),
    ThrowType(u32),
    // calls (stack: this, func, args...)
    Call(u32, u32),
    CallArray(u32),
    CallEval(u32),
    CallEvalArray,
    New(u32),
    NewArray_,
    SuperCall(u32),
    SuperCallArray,
    // iteration
    GetIterator,
    GetAsyncIterator,
    /// [iter next] -> [iter next value] or jump when done
    IterNext(u32),
    IterClose,
    IterCloseSilent,
    /// destructuring: [iter next done] -> [iter next done value]
    IterValue,
    IterRest,
    IterDone,
    ForInStart,
    ForInNext(u32),
    // generators / async
    Yield,
    /// after resume from yield: handles throw/return; return jumps to target
    GenResume(u32),
    Await,
    /// [iter next received] delegation step; done -> push value, continue
    YieldStar(u32, bool),
    AsyncIterValue,
    /// convert iterator result of async iteration: [iter next result] -> value or jump when done
    AsyncIterCheck(u32),
    // misc
    Debugger,
    ImportMeta,
    DynamicImport,
    Nop,
    /// [obj] -> [obj] throws if not object (iterator results etc.)
    CheckObj,
    /// push undefined if top is Empty (used by super calls)
    /// dispose resources at scope exit (using declarations)
    AddDisposable(bool),
    DisposeScope(u32),
    /// generator: suspend after prologue
    GenStart,
    GetImport(u32),
    SuperCallForward,
    /// [iter next] -> [iter next result] (no done check)
    IterCallNext,
    /// [iter next] -> [awaitable] calls return() for async iterator close
    IterCloseAsync,
    /// [F proto sym] instance private field
    AddFieldPrivate(u32),
    /// module: end of instantiation part
    ModuleBodyStart,
    /// set completion value slot (eval/repl)
    SetCompletion(u32),
    /// [exc iter next] close iterator ignoring errors then rethrow exc
    IterCloseThrow,
    /// object pattern: throw if value is null/undefined (keeps it)
    RequireObjCoercible,
    /// array destructuring: [value] -> [iter next done]
    DestructIter,
    /// store frame `this` (derived constructor after super)
    BindThis,
    /// [result F] run instance field initializers of F on result -> [result]
    InitFields,
    /// bind `this` in an env slot (derived constructor, captured this): errors if already bound
    BindThisEnv(u16, u32),
}

pub struct FunctionCode {
    pub name: JsStr,
    pub ops: Vec<Op>,
    pub consts: Vec<Value>,
    pub keys: Vec<PropKey>,
    pub funcs: Vec<Rc<FunctionCode>>,
    pub scopes: Vec<Rc<ScopeInfo>>,
    pub templates: Vec<Rc<TemplateData>>,
    pub regexps: Vec<(JsStr, JsStr)>,
    pub strings: Vec<JsStr>,
    pub nlocals: u32,
    pub length: u32,
    pub kind: FuncKind,
    pub is_async: bool,
    pub is_generator: bool,
    pub strict: bool,
    pub source: Rc<str>,
    pub src_start: usize,
    pub src_end: usize,
    pub is_arrow: bool,
    pub has_simple_params: bool,
    pub line: u32,
    /// a function with no own `prototype` (methods, arrows, async functions, ...)
    pub no_prototype: bool,
    pub class_source: bool,
    /// name set from a class/declaration (affects toString for default ctor)
    pub is_default_ctor: bool,
    pub is_script: bool,
    pub is_module: bool,
    pub is_eval: bool,
}

impl FunctionCode {
    pub fn is_constructor(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(self.kind, FuncKind::Normal | FuncKind::ClassConstructor | FuncKind::DerivedConstructor)
            && !self.is_async
            && !self.is_generator
    }
    pub fn source_text(&self) -> String {
        if self.is_default_ctor {
            return String::new();
        }
        self.source.chars().skip(self.src_start).take(self.src_end.saturating_sub(self.src_start)).collect()
    }
}

impl std::fmt::Debug for FunctionCode {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        writeln!(f, "function {} (locals={}, strict={})", self.name, self.nlocals, self.strict)?;
        for (i, op) in self.ops.iter().enumerate() {
            writeln!(f, "  {:4} {:?}", i, op)?;
        }
        for (i, func) in self.funcs.iter().enumerate() {
            writeln!(f, "-- nested #{}:", i)?;
            write!(f, "{:?}", func)?;
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

steps.message:
Intl.Locale, Intl.DisplayNames and tag canonicalization (`Intl.getCanonicalLocales`) are done. All my comparison and fuzz scripts now produce byte-identical output to the original.

**Branch / commits:** `worktree-agent-a7061a7026be45406`, head `30b2398` (on top of skeleton `259405d`; main commit `fe81f1d`).

**Files:**
- `src/builtins/intl/tag.rs` (new): tag parsing and canonicalization.
- `src/builtins/intl/locale.rs`: rewritten.
- `src/builtins/intl/displaynames.rs`: rewritten.
- `src/builtins/intl/locale_data.rs` (new, 186 KB): likely-subtags tables pulled out of the original by brute-force queries.
- `src/builtins/intl/mod.rs`: only the "BCP 47 language tags" section changed. It is now just `mod tag; pub use tag::{canonicalize_tag, parse_tag, LangTag};`. The LangTag fields, `base_name`, `keyword` and `to_canonical_string` are unchanged, and `locale_object_tag` is untouched. Merging should be conflict-free unless you edited that section.

**What matches:**
- **Canonicalization:** the original uses its own alias tables, a subset of CLDR that looks test262-driven, and I replicated them exactly. They were found by brute force over all 2–3 letter languages, regions, scripts and the `sgn-XX` sign languages, plus every u/t extension rule.
  - `SU`/`810` resolve via likely subtags; aliases are applied only once (`drw` → `prs`).
  - The Locale constructor canonicalizes twice (`drw` → `fa-AF`), while `getCanonicalLocales` does it once.
- **Intl.Locale:** internal property slots in the original's order, option read order and every error message, all getters and both brand-check errors.
  - `maximize`/`minimize` use the full extracted likely-subtags data; all 2.2M language×region/script combinations round-trip identically.
  - The `get*` info methods (calendars, hour cycles, week info, etc.) are trivial in the original and are reproduced as-is.
- **Intl.DisplayNames:** it is English-only in the original — every locale and style returns the same tiny table. Code validation, error messages, fallback canonicalization, slots and `resolvedOptions` all match.

**Fuzzing:** 4,000 random tags, 3,000 Locale option combinations, 3,000 DisplayNames configurations and 6,000 random subtag sequences — 0 diffs.

**Known differences:** none found in my scope. If `maximize` is called on a fake object whose tag is invalid, the original panics; we throw `RangeError` instead.

**Issues outside my files:**
1. **`mod.rs` `locale_list` (yours):** `null` locales now give "cannot convert undefined or null to object"; the original says "Cannot convert null to object". Repro: `Intl.getCanonicalLocales(null)`, which also affects every constructor. Fix: add `Value::Null => return vm.throw_type("Cannot convert null to object")` before the `to_object` call.
2. **`datetime.rs` region aliases:** its own parser still maps numeric regions the original keeps. Repro: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-724').resolvedOptions().locale` gives `en-ES` here and `en-724` in the original; same for 826 and 276. The original only maps 004 008 230 280 530 532 536 554 582 756 810 840 886 890. Since `locale_list` already hands dt canonical tags, its `REGION_ALIASES` should match that list or be dropped.
3. **Engine (`util.inspect`):** `showHidden: true` doesn't show non-enumerable own properties. Repro: `util.inspect(Object.defineProperty({a:1},'x',{value:2}),{showHidden:true})` gives `{ a: 1 }` here and `{ a: 1, x: 2 }` in the original. This hides the `__locale_*` / `__dn_*` slots.
4. **Engine (array iterators):** the original's array iterators carry own `__ai_target`, `__ai_index` and `__ai_kind` properties; ours have none. Repro: `Reflect.ownKeys([][Symbol.iterator]())`. This matters for Segmenter's segments iterator.

#!/bin/bash
# usage: run_split.sh casesfile ext ; split cases by '---' into files with extension ext and run both binaries
F=$1; EXT=${2:-ts}
OURS=/workspace/.claude/worktrees/agent-ab227a21dcecddb9a/target/release/lumen
D=/tmp/cliagent/split; rm -rf $D; mkdir -p $D; cd $D
python3 - "$F" "$EXT" <<'EOF'
import sys
src=open(sys.argv[1]).read()
cases=src.split("\n---\n")
for i,c in enumerate(cases):
    open("/tmp/cliagent/split/case%03d.%s" % (i, sys.argv[2]), "w").write(c if c.endswith("\n") else c + "\n")
EOF
pass=0; fail=0
for f in case*.$EXT; do
  timeout 10 /tmp/orig $f > o1 2> e1; c1=$?
  timeout 10 $OURS $f > o2 2> e2; c2=$?
  if [ $c1 = $c2 ] && cmp -s o1 o2 && cmp -s e1 e2; then pass=$((pass+1)); else
    fail=$((fail+1)); echo "FAIL $f (exit $c1 vs $c2)"; head -3 $f | sed 's/^/   | /'
    diff o1 o2 | head -6 | sed 's/^/   out /'; diff e1 e2 | head -6 | sed 's/^/   err /'
  fi
done
echo "pass=$pass fail=$fail"

const c = require('crypto');
const {publicKey, privateKey} = c.generateKeyPairSync('ed25519');
const privPem = privateKey.export({format: 'pem', type: 'pkcs8'});
const pubPem = publicKey.export({format: 'pem', type: 'spki'});
const encPem = '-----BEGIN ENCRYPTED PRIVATE KEY-----\nMIGbMFcGCSqGSIb3DQEFDTBKMCkGCSqGSIb3DQEFDDAcBAhk\n-----END ENCRYPTED PRIVATE KEY-----\n';
const tests = {
  'pass empty': () => c.createPrivateKey({key: privPem, passphrase: ''}).type,
  'pass null': () => c.createPrivateKey({key: privPem, passphrase: null}).type,
  'pass undefined': () => c.createPrivateKey({key: privPem, passphrase: undefined}).type,
  'enc pem': () => c.createPrivateKey(encPem),
  'enc pem pass': () => c.createPrivateKey({key: encPem, passphrase: 'x'}),
  'pub enc pem': () => c.createPublicKey(encPem),
  'export fmt xyz spki': () => publicKey.export({format: 'xyz', type: 'spki'}),
  'export fmt xyz cipher': () => privateKey.export({format: 'xyz', cipher: 'x'}),
  'export jwk pass': () => Object.keys(privateKey.export({format: 'jwk', passphrase: 'x'})).join(),
  'export der pass': () => privateKey.export({format: 'der', type: 'pkcs8', passphrase: 'x'}),
  'export der cipher only': () => privateKey.export({format: 'der', type: 'pkcs8', cipher: 'aes-128-cbc'}),
  'key obj with key ko': () => c.createPublicKey({key: publicKey}).type,
  'key obj with key ko priv': () => c.createPrivateKey({key: privateKey, format: 'pem'}).type,
  'buffer der': () => c.createPublicKey({key: publicKey.export({format: 'der', type: 'spki'}), format: 'der', type: 'spki'}).asymmetricKeyType,
  'arraybuffer pem': () => c.createPublicKey(new TextEncoder().encode(pubPem).buffer).type,
  'u16 pem': () => c.createPublicKey(new Uint16Array(4)),
  'dataview': () => c.createPublicKey(new DataView(new ArrayBuffer(2))),
  'string with spaces': () => c.createPublicKey('  \n' + pubPem + '\n  ').type,
  'two blocks': () => c.createPublicKey(pubPem + privPem).type,
  'priv from pub pem wrong label': () => c.createPrivateKey(pubPem),
  'pub from cert-ish': () => c.createPublicKey('-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nAAAA\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----'),
  'jwk missing kty pub': () => c.createPublicKey({key: {}, format: 'jwk'}),
  'jwk missing d priv': () => c.createPrivateKey({key: {kty: 'OKP', crv: 'Ed25519', x: 'AA'}, format: 'jwk'}),
  'jwk bad crv': () => c.createPublicKey({key: {kty: 'EC', crv: 'P-384', x: 'AA', y: 'AA'}, format: 'jwk'}),
  'jwk bad okp': () => c.createPublicKey({key: {kty: 'OKP', crv: 'Ed448', x: 'AA'}, format: 'jwk'}),
  'jwk null': () => c.createPublicKey({key: null, format: 'jwk'}),
  'equals': () => [publicKey.equals(c.createPublicKey(pubPem)), privateKey.equals(c.createPrivateKey(privPem)), publicKey.equals(privateKey)].join(),
};
for (const [k, f] of Object.entries(tests)) {
  try { const r = f(); console.log(k, 'OK', r); } catch (e) { console.log(k, '::', e.constructor.name, JSON.stringify(e.message), '::', String(e.stack).split('\n').slice(1).filter(l => !/compileCommonJS|\.js|runMain| anonymous$/.test(l)).join(' |')); }
}

steps.message:
Intl.Collator and String.prototype.localeCompare are done and match the original. The only remaining differences come from two things outside my files.

**Branch / commit:** `worktree-agent-a7a64ea381028e8a0` @ `0b8098b` (based on your skeleton `259405d`).

**Files changed:**
- `src/builtins/intl/collator.rs`: full rewrite (constructor, `resolvedOptions`, `compare` getter and the collation algorithm).
- `src/builtins/string.rs`: only `locale_cmp` and `locale_compare` changed. `localeCompare` now goes through the collator; `pub fn locale_cmp(a, b, sens)` is kept as a wrapper.
- `intl/mod.rs` is untouched.

**How the original sorts (it is not CLDR):**
- **Primary:** each character is decomposed (NFD) and lowercased, then compared by code point. Nothing is ignorable, `_` sorts after `@`, and ß, æ, Greek and Cyrillic sort after z.
- **Accents:** each base character counts as 0 and each combining mark as its code point, compared as one flat sequence.
- **Case:** an "is uppercase" flag per base character; titlecase digraphs like ǅ count as lowercase.
- There is no identical level, so canonically equivalent strings compare equal. Results are always -1/0/1.
- Accent order is primary then accents; case order is primary then case; variant is all three.
- **numeric:** only ASCII digit runs count, compared by value. Leading zeros show up at the accent and case levels because each digit adds an entry there.
- **ignorePunctuation:** drops ASCII punctuation/symbols, whitespace and U+2000–U+206F after decomposition. It defaults to true for `th`.
- **caseFirst upper** puts uppercase first.
- **German phonebook or `usage: 'search'`:** ä/ö/ü expand to ae/oe/ue with an accent difference. No other locale has any tailoring (sv, es and the rest sort like en).
- **Settings:**
  - Option read order, error messages, `-u-co/kf/kn` handling (including the original's quirks) and which collations each language supports all match.
  - Internal `__co_*` slots are read on every call, and the brand is checked again inside the bound compare.
  - `__co_bound` is returned as-is whenever it exists.

**Verification:**
- All BMP code points and a sample across all planes, at all four sensitivities, give byte-identical output.
- About 400k random string pairs over 256 option combinations match, as do 18 probe scripts and typical name, file and number sorts.
- It is faster than the original (a 50k-word sort takes about 1.4s versus 8–9s).

**Remaining differences, both outside my files:**
1. Bug in your `locale_list` in `mod.rs`: `null` locales should throw `TypeError: Cannot convert null to object`. It currently gives the engine's `cannot convert undefined or null to object`. Repro: `new Intl.Collator(null)`, `Intl.getCanonicalLocales(null)`, `'a'.localeCompare('b', null)`. The fix is one line: `Value::Null => return vm.throw_type("Cannot convert null to object")`.
2. `'ä'.localeCompare('ae', new Intl.Locale(...))` fails only because `Intl.Locale` is still a stub.

**Applies to your DateTimeFormat/NumberFormat getters:**
- If the cached bound slot exists, the original returns it even when it is `undefined`. Repro: `d = new Intl.DateTimeFormat(); d.__dtf_bound = undefined; typeof d.format` gives `"undefined"`, and the same happens with `__nf_boundformat`. Your getters treat `undefined` as missing.
- For Collator, the bound function re-checks the brand before converting its arguments: `f = c.compare; delete c.__co; f('a','b')` throws "method called on an incompatible receiver". I did not test whether `format` does the same.

No new core-engine bugs found.

n = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 1
resp = sys.argv[3].encode().decode('unicode_escape').encode('latin1') if len(sys.argv) > 3 else b"HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Type: text/plain\r\nX-B: 2\r\nX-A: 1\r\nX-A: 3\r\nContent-Length: 5\r\n\r\nhello"
s = socket.socket()
s.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
s.bind(('127.0.0.1', port))
s.listen(5)
for i in range(n):
    c, a = s.accept()
    c.settimeout(2)
    data = b''
    try:
        while True:
            chunk = c.recv(65536)
            if not chunk:
                break
            data += chunk
            if b'\r\n\r\n' in data:
                head, _, body = data.partition(b'\r\n\r\n')
                cl = 0
                for line in head.split(b'\r\n')[1:]:
                    k, _, v = line.partition(b':')
                    if k.strip().lower() == b'content-length':
                        cl = int(v.strip())
                if len(body) >= cl and b'chunked' not in head.lower():
                    break
                if b'chunked' in head.lower() and body.endswith(b'0\r\n\r\n'):
                    break
    except socket.timeout:
        pass
    sys.stdout.write(repr(data) + "\n")
    sys.stdout.flush()
    c.sendall(resp)
    c.close()
s.close()

steps.message:
Intl.Segmenter and Intl.ListFormat now match the original. Everything I probed is identical except one ListFormat edge case and one engine-level difference, both described below.

**Branch / commit:** `worktree-agent-a5ae4b20963c6fe50`, commit `6868bf3` (based on `259405d`). Only `src/builtins/intl/segmenter.rs` and `src/builtins/intl/listformat.rs` changed.

**How it was checked:** full sweeps over every code point (grapheme, word and sentence) give identical output to the original, and 25,000 random strings (all three granularities plus `containing()` at every index) match. Probe scripts are in `/tmp/intlagent/seg/`.

**ListFormat:**
- The original only has data for Spanish (`es` / `es-*`); every other locale uses its English patterns. Those include some odd ones that I copied: conjunction "narrow" joins with plain spaces ("A B C"), and Spanish unit/short is "A y B" but "A, B, C".
- There is no Spanish "y"→"e" / "o"→"u" adjustment.
- A tampered or unknown `__lf_type` / `__lf_style` value falls back to ", " separators, except that Spanish conjunction and disjunction ignore the style entirely.
- Only primitive strings are accepted. A non-string element closes the iterator and throws "Intl.ListFormat list elements must be strings". `undefined` gives an empty list, `null` throws the original's quirky "cannot read property ' 1' of null", and non-iterables throw "value is not iterable".
- Lone surrogates are preserved in the output.

**Segmenter:**
- Constructor, slot properties, `resolvedOptions` and error messages match the original.
- `segment()` returns a plain object with own `__seg_records`, `containing` and `[Symbol.iterator]` properties, with fresh functions on each call.
- `containing(n)` converts `n` first, then scans `this.__seg_records` with ordinary property reads (so tampered or inherited records behave as in the original).
- The iterator is `this.__seg_records.values()`.
- **Grapheme:** standard Unicode rules using the engine's Unicode 17 tables, with the original's deviations:
  - there is no Prepend class;
  - the newer Indic-conjunct rule is not applied;
  - every spacing mark counts, with no exceptions;
  - the emoji ZWJ rule allows extra ZWJs in the sequence;
  - unassigned code points are treated as ordinary characters.
- **Word:** standard Unicode rules but with a much simpler character table. Every non-ASCII character counts as a letter, so CJK and Thai runs and even non-ASCII spaces form single words. `_` and CR/LF are single-character segments. `isWordLike` means the segment starts with a letter or digit.
- **Sentence:** a segment ends after each ASCII `.`, `!` or `?` plus any following spaces or LF characters. An unknown granularity value uses these sentence rules; a missing or non-string one means grapheme.

**Known differences:**
- When the locale comes from an object with a non-canonical `__locale_tag` (e.g. "es-mx"), the original reports it verbatim but we report the canonical "es-MX". This comes from the shared `resolve_locale` in `intl/mod.rs`, which I didn't touch; it can't happen with real `Intl.Locale` objects.
- The iterator returned by a Segments object lacks the `__ai_target` / `__ai_index` / `__ai_kind` own properties. That is an engine-level difference, listed below.

**Core-engine differences found (not mine to fix):**
1. Array iterators in the original have own properties `__ai_target`, `__ai_index`, `__ai_kind`; ours have none. Repro: `Reflect.ownKeys([1][Symbol.iterator]())`.
2. Iterating `null` gives a different message. Repro: `for (const a of null) {}`, or `[...null]`, throws "cannot read property ' 1' of null" in the original; ours throws "value is not iterable". ListFormat works around this locally.

steps.message:
The web platform globals are implemented natively in Rust and match the original on everything I compared except `Blob.prototype.stream()`, which waits on the streams agent's `ReadableStream` (other known differences below). The work is on branch `worktree-agent-a530825df77f87f58`, last commit `b3c677c` (7 commits on top of `08ab09b`).

**How the original works, and what I copied:** most of these APIs are JavaScript classes in the original, with their state in ordinary own properties (`_c`, `_list`, `_listeners`, symbol-keyed blob bytes, and so on). My versions create the same properties in the same order and read them back through normal property access. So `Object.keys`, `JSON.stringify`, `util.inspect`, subclassing and the quirky setter behaviour all come out the same. Error stacks also show the original's internal function names (`at dispatchEvent`, `at _doAbort`, `at set port`, …).

**What's in place**
- **Events and messaging:** `DOMException` (it has no `code` property in the original); `Event` and its subclasses (`CustomEvent`, `MessageEvent`, `CloseEvent`, `ErrorEvent`, `PromiseRejectionEvent`); `EventTarget`; `AbortController`/`AbortSignal` including `abort`, `timeout` and `any`; `MessageChannel`/`MessagePort`/`BroadcastChannel`. Messages are delivered on `setTimeout(0)` like the original, which also consumes timer ids the same way.
- **URL:** the original's own simplified parser (no percent-encoding, non-ASCII hosts rejected, its exact error messages), plus `URLSearchParams` with its live link to the URL, and `URLPattern`. There is no `URL.createObjectURL` in the original, so none here.
- **Encoding:** `TextEncoder` (no `encodeInto`, as in the original), and `TextDecoder` (UTF-8 only; it rejects other encodings with RangeError and ignores `stream`). Also `atob`/`btoa`, `structuredClone`, `__serializeForClone`/`__deserializeClone`, and `Blob`/`File`/`FormData`.
- **Globals:** `performance` with mark/measure, `navigator` (only `userAgent: 'lumen'`), `self`, `queueMicrotask` (as `Promise.resolve().then(cb)`), `reportError`, `onerror` and `onunhandledrejection`.
- **Node modules:** `url` (including the legacy `url.parse`, punycode `domainToASCII`/`domainToUnicode`, and the original's odd `resolve`/`fileURLToPath`), `querystring`, and `timers/promises` (including the `setInterval` async iterator and abort signals).

**Testing:** about 45 comparison scripts in `/tmp/webagent/` plus randomized cross-checks of URL parsing, URL setters, `URLSearchParams`, `URLPattern`, `url`/`querystring`, punycode, encoding and the clone serializer. Apart from the items listed here, the outputs match the original.

**Shared files I changed (small)**
- `src/runtime/mod.rs`: errors thrown in timers and immediates now go through `web::report_task_error`. That calls `globalThis.onerror` first and then prints in the original's format (`Uncaught Error`, `Uncaught x` for strings). Unhandled rejections now go through `onunhandledrejection`, and calling `preventDefault()` suppresses the message.
- `src/runtime/timers.rs`: `queueMicrotask` now uses the promise-based version.
- `web.rs` became the directory `src/runtime/web/`. The existing entry points (`setup`, `create_timers_promises`, `create_url_module`, `create_querystring_module`) are unchanged.

**Global order:** my globals are installed in the original's relative order, but other modules' globals sit between them in the original. To make that easy I split setup into four phases that `web::setup` runs in sequence:

| Phase | Globals |
|---|---|
| `setup_core` | DOMException … URLPattern |
| `setup_blob` | Blob, File, FormData |
| `setup_platform` | navigator, self, Performance, performance |
| `setup_late` | queueMicrotask, onerror, onunhandledrejection, reportError |

Whoever owns `setup_runtime` can call the phases separately to interleave them. I also left helper functions in `web/` for the fetch and streams work (building Blobs, reading Blob/FormData contents, constructing events).

**Known differences**
- `Blob.prototype.stream()` will start working once the streams agent's global `ReadableStream` exists.
- `String(SomeClass)` shows native code instead of the original's JS source, which the rules don't let me copy.
- `performance.now()` at script start is about 0.17 ms, against about 0.0001 ms in the original.
- `require('timers').promises` is missing: `create_timers` in `node.rs` (not mine) needs `promises` pointing at the `timers/promises` module.

**Core-engine bugs found**
1. `JSON.stringify(new Uint8Array([7,8]))` gives `{}` in the original and `{"0":7,"1":8}` in ours.
2. `[...undefined]` throws TypeError `cannot read property '\u00001' of undefined` in the original; ours says `value is not iterable`. I handle this inside my own code.
3. These two are in `util.inspect`:
   - A generator object prints as `{}` in the original and `Iterator {}` in ours (`util.inspect((function*(){})())`).
   - A Map nested beyond the depth limit prints as `[Object]` in the original and `[Map]` in ours.

def load(cal):
    rows = []
    for part in ['_a', '', '_b']:
        txt = open(f'/tmp/temporalagent/tab_{cal}{part}.txt').read().strip()
        for r in txt.split(';'):
            a, b, c, d = map(int, r.split(','))

    return rows

B64 = 'ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/'

for cal in ['chinese', 'dangi']:

    first_year = -1000
    # consistency
    for i in range(len(rows) - 1):
        start, miy, mask, leap = rows[i]
        total = sum(30 if mask >> k & 1 else 29 for k in range(miy))
        if rows[i + 1][0] - start != total:
            print('inconsistent', cal, first_year + i, rows[i + 1][0] - start, total, file=sys.stderr)

steps.message:
Both files are implemented and committed on branch `worktree-agent-a1153e7885bc0a64b` (latest commit `554d7f1`, 7 commits). I compared them against the original with about 90 scripts that log interleaved microtasks. All of them match except three, and none of those three failures is in my code (listed below).

**Key finding:** the original's web layer is plain JS classes with a deliberately simple buffered model, not the WHATWG spec. Chunks sit in an array, `pull` runs synchronously and its result is ignored, writes go through one promise chain, and state lives in visible own properties (`_chunks`, `_state`, `_bodyBytes`, `_map`, …). So I copied that model rather than the spec. Instance state is real own properties and every step builds the same promise chain, so `Object.keys`, `JSON.stringify` and tick ordering match. Its behaviour includes quirks such as `Response.json()` ending up with `text/plain`, a double `writer.close()` emitting output twice, and missing `ReadableStream.from`, `Response.redirect` and `getSetCookie`.

**streams.rs**
- All the stream classes and controllers, BYOB reads, `pipeTo`/`pipeThrough`, `tee`, async iteration and `values({preventCancel})`, both queuing strategies, `TextEncoderStream`/`TextDecoderStream`.
- `CompressionStream`/`DecompressionStream` use `crate::compress` (gzip, deflate and deflate-raw only, as in the original), including its error messages and the 1 MiB cap. They match the original on every asset in `assets/test_runtime_compression`.
- Private UTF-8 helpers copy the original's lone-surrogate encoding (U+D800+k is written as U+10F800+k).

**fetch.rs**
- `Headers`, `Request` and `Response` with every body type, the body readers (`text`, `json`, `arrayBuffer`, `bytes`, `blob`, `formData` including multipart encode/decode), `clone`, `Response.json` and `Response.error`.
- `fetch` speaks HTTP/1.1 on a background thread with the original's exact request bytes. It follows at most 5 redirects, handles chunked bodies, `AbortSignal`, and the original's error texts. `https` reproduces the TLS-failure messages; `data:` and `ftp:` give "unsupported scheme".
- `Lumen.serve` matches the original's status lines, header order, 500/`onError` handling, the 400 "empty request" reply, `onListen`, `signal`, `finished`/`shutdown` timing and port errors. `Lumen.version` and `Lumen.upgradeWebSocket` are there too.
- `WebSocket` and `EventSource` work fully (handshake, frames, close, SSE parsing and reconnect).

**Known differences**
- No `String(fn)` source text.
- Exact ordering against timers for network events can differ; I added small delays so a failed fetch settles after `setTimeout(0)` and `finished` settles on a 0 ms timer, as in the original.
- Server-to-client WebSocket sends work here, while in the original they hang.

**Core-engine bugs (not my files)**
1. `JSON.stringify(new Uint8Array([1,2]))` gives `{}` in the original but `{"0":1,"1":2}` here; Buffer is correct (`{"type":"Buffer",...}`). This affects any test that stringifies a read result. Likely fix: skip typed-array element keys in `ser_object` in `src/builtins/json.rs`.
2. Breaking out of `for await`: when the iterator's `return()` returns a promise, the original only resumes after the whole microtask queue drains; when it returns a plain object it resumes without awaiting. Ours awaits one tick. Repro: `/tmp/streamsagent/fa.js` (a custom async iterator, then `break`, then a 20-step `.then` chain). This is the only stream-ordering mismatch I have left.

**For integration (other agents)**
- `require("stream/web")` goes to `nodestream.rs`. It should return `crate::runtime::streams::create_module(vm, name)`, which already has the original's key order.
- Blob, FormData, URL, URLSearchParams, EventTarget, Event/MessageEvent/CloseEvent, AbortController and DOMException are looked up on the global object when needed (internal fallbacks for URL, AbortController and DOMException). Response and FormData bodies read Blob bytes from a `Symbol("blobBytes")` own property holding a Uint8Array, as the original does. If that isn't there, they fall back to an already-settled `arrayBuffer()` promise, then to draining `blob.stream()` synchronously.

My test scripts and the comparison runner are in `/tmp/streamsagent/` (`python3 run.py bundleN.js`).

results.content:
# Express on lumen

A real-world [Express 4](https://expressjs.com) app — CommonJS, with third-party middleware —
running **unmodified** on the lumen runtime.

Unlike the Hono example (which is web-standard `Request`/`Response`), Express is built on Node's
`http.createServer` and the `req`/`res` stream objects, and pulls in a deep dependency tree. lumen
runs it through its `node:http` compatibility layer, which bridges to the `Lumen.serve` HTTP
server — so `app.listen(3000)` binds a real socket and `curl localhost:3000` works like any Node
server.

## What it exercises

- **Express core** — routing, route params (`/users/:id`), query parsing, `res.json`/`res.send`,
  status codes, `ETag` generation, the 404 fall-through.
- **`morgan`** — request logging middleware, writing the `tiny` format (with real response times)
  to `process.stdout`.
- **`cors`** — sets `Access-Control-*` headers, including the `OPTIONS` preflight.
- **`express.json()`** — parses JSON request bodies (via `body-parser` → `raw-body` → `iconv-lite`).

Behind the scenes this drove a lot of `node:` compatibility: `http`, `events`, `stream`, `util`,
`crypto` (the `etag` hash), `querystring`, `url`, `net`, `assert`, `string_decoder`, plus
`Buffer`, `process.stdout`/`hrtime`, and `Error.captureStackTrace`. See
`crates/lumen-node/src/js/` for the implementations.

## Run

```sh
npm install
cargo build --release -p lumen-cli        # from the repo root

../../target/release/lumen-cli server.js  # http://localhost:3000
```

Then, in another terminal:

```sh
curl localhost:3000/
curl localhost:3000/users/42
curl "localhost:3000/search?q=lumen&page=2"
curl -X POST localhost:3000/echo -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"hi":"there"}'
curl -i localhost:3000/teapot          # 418, custom header
curl -i -X OPTIONS localhost:3000/ -H 'Origin: http://example.com' \
     -H 'Access-Control-Request-Method: POST'   # CORS preflight
```

- `app.js` — the Express app (routes, middleware).
- `server.js` — `app.listen(port)`.

## Known limits

The `node:` layer targets the common server path, not 100% of Node. Notably: no `zlib`, so a
gzip/deflate-encoded request or response body is unsupported (identity encoding works); the
`node:http` **client** (`http.request`) isn't implemented (use the global `fetch`); and there's no
TLS, so `https` can't terminate. See the checklists at the top of each `crates/lumen-node/src/js/`
module for specifics.
# lumen

A from-scratch JavaScript **engine** in Rust — std only, zero dependencies — and a
**runtime** being built on top of it, the way Node/Deno/Bun wrap a JS engine with an event
loop and host APIs. Every crate in the workspace is std-only: no `tokio`, `mio`, `libc`,
`rustyline`, `serde`, or any other third-party dependency, anywhere.

## The engine (`crates/lumen`)

A lexer, parser, and **three execution tiers**:

- a **tree-walking interpreter** — the reference oracle: the spec semantics live here, and
  every other tier must match it observably (a differential fuzzer, `lumen-difftest`, holds
  them to that);
- an opt-in **bytecode VM** — functions compile whole (or not at all — no deoptimization) to
  a stack machine with slot-homed locals, per-site inline caches for property and free-name
  access backed by object shapes (hidden classes), and dense-array element fast paths;
- a **native template JIT** — bytecode lowers to real ARM64 machine code on macOS, Linux,
  and Windows, with a correctness-first x86-64 backend on Intel macOS, Linux, and Windows:
  per-op templates with the interpreter as the shared slow path, inline-cache reads baked
  into the instruction stream, fused compare-and-branch, exact-`ToInt32` bitops, and numeric
  *register chains* that keep runs of arithmetic entirely in FP registers. The full set of
  inline fast paths currently lives in the ARM64 backend; x86-64 starts with native control
  flow and checked per-op helpers. Other architectures degrade to the bytecode VM.

Tier selection: `--tier=interp|bytecode|jit` (**jit is the default**; where the JIT is
unavailable it degrades to the bytecode VM). Functions tier up after a call-count threshold —
immediately if the body contains a loop. Force the reference tree-walker with `--tier=interp`
(or `LUMEN_TIER=interp`).

The language surface: generators and `async`/`await` running on stackful coroutines (async
bodies suspend on the bytecode VM itself), full `RegExp` (including `\p{…}` and inline
modifiers), typed arrays, `Proxy`/`Reflect`, ES modules (top-level await, `import defer`,
source phase), `Intl`, and `Temporal`.

`Intl` (ECMA-402) and `Temporal` are behind the default-on `intl` and `temporal` Cargo features.
The CLDR data tables included by `intl` are the largest single contributor to binary size (~3 MB
of the release binary). Build with `--no-default-features` for a small engine: the `Intl` and
`Temporal` globals are absent, `Date.prototype.toTemporalInstant` is omitted, and the `toLocale*`
methods degrade to their locale-independent forms, the way engines built without i18n do. Either
feature can be enabled independently.

On dependencies and `unsafe`: the workspace stays std-only — the JIT maps executable memory
through raw platform declarations (`mmap`/`mprotect`, macOS `MAP_JIT`, or Windows
`VirtualAlloc`/`VirtualProtect`) rather than libc. Pages are writable only while code is copied,
then executable/read-only, and instruction caches are synchronized where required. The
interpreter and bytecode VM are safe Rust; `unsafe` is concentrated where machine
code meets the object graph (the JIT's executable pages and its templates' raw reads — every
baked offset is *measured at runtime* against the live types and fails closed to the checked
helper if anything doesn't hold) and in the N-API addon loader's `dlopen` bridge.

**Passes 100% of [tc39/test262](https://github.com/tc39/test262): 53,400/53,400** (including
annexB, intl402, and staging) — on the default JIT tier and under `LUMEN_TIER=interp`.

Extracted from — and used by — the [lucid-softworks/browser](https://github.com/lucid-softworks/browser)
engine as its JS backend (`backend-lumen`), with full git history.

## The runtime

A curated `embed` API on the engine exposes just enough — native-function registration, a
typed host-state slot, and event-loop hooks — for a runtime layer to be assembled from
independent op crates, without leaking the interpreter's internals into the published API.
On top of that:

- **Event loop** (`lumen-runtime`) — a single loop thread owns the (`!Send`) engine; blocking
  work runs on a std thread pool and completes back over `mpsc`. No epoll/kqueue reactor
  (that would need raw syscalls); the thread-pool-plus-completion model is libuv's own fs
  strategy. Each turn drains microtasks, queued callbacks, due timers, and I/O completions,
  then blocks until the next event.
- **Timers** (`lumen-timers`) — `setTimeout`/`setInterval`/`clearTimeout`/`clearInterval`/
  `setImmediate`, plus `queueMicrotask`.
- **`console` and `process`** — streaming `console.*`; `process.argv`/`env`/`platform`/
  `cwd()`/`exit()`/`nextTick()`.
- **Filesystem** (`lumen-fs`) — synchronous ops (`readFileSync`, `writeFileSync`,
  `existsSync`, `mkdirSync`, `readdirSync`, …), file handles via a resource table
  (`openSync`/`readSync`/`writeSync`/`closeSync`), and async `fs.promises.readFile`/
  `writeFile` on the thread pool.
- **Web platform** (`lumen-web`) — a growing slice of the WinterTC Minimum Common API:
  `Event`/`EventTarget`/`CustomEvent`/`AbortController`/`AbortSignal`/`DOMException`,
  `TextEncoder`/`TextDecoder`, `atob`/`btoa`, `structuredClone`, `URL`/`URLSearchParams`,
  `performance.now()`, `crypto.getRandomValues`/`randomUUID`/`subtle.digest` (SHA-256), and
  `fetch`/`Headers`/`Request`/`Response`. See the checklist at the top of
  `crates/lumen-web/src/lib.rs` for what's implemented vs. deferred (streams, `Blob`/
  `FormData`, `URLPattern`, …).

  `fetch` speaks HTTP/1.1 over `std::net`. **`https:` is not supported**: TLS cannot be
  implemented on std alone and no third-party crate is permitted, so `https` URLs reject with
  a clear error; plain `http` works.

  `Lumen.serve((request) => Response)` is the matching HTTP/1.1 **server** — not a WinterTC API,
  but the cross-runtime `serve(handler)` convention (Deno/Bun/Workers), so a Hono app runs with
  `Lumen.serve(app.fetch)`. v1 is single-accept, `Connection: close`, buffered bodies, http only
  (see `crates/lumen-web/src/server.rs`). Cold-start and usage: `examples/hono-app`.

- **Modules — both CommonJS and ESM.** `lumen-cli` picks the module kind the way Node does:
  `.mjs` is ESM, `.cjs` is CommonJS, `.js` follows the nearest `package.json` `"type"`. ES
  modules run through the engine's real module graph (linking, top-level `await`); `import`
  specifiers resolve against disk and `node_modules`, `node:` builtins are importable
  (named imports included), and CommonJS packages interop by default export. CommonJS files
  run as the program entry with `require.main === module`.

#!/bin/bash

f="$1"; shift
NEW=${NEW:-/workspace/target/release/lumen}
cd "$(dirname "$f")"
b=$(basename "$f")

if cmp -s /tmp/o1.txt /tmp/o2.txt && cmp -s /tmp/e1.txt /tmp/e2.txt && [ $c1 = $c2 ]; then
  echo "PASS $f"

    diff <(cat /tmp/e1.txt) <(cat /tmp/e2.txt) | head -${N:-20}

fi

def pat2str(pat):
    return ''.join('{0}' if p['type'] == 'NUM' else p['value'] for p in pat)

groups = ['en', 'en-IN', 'ar', 'de', 'es', 'fr', 'gv', 'hi', 'it', 'ja', 'ko', 'nl', 'pl', 'pt', 'ru', 'sl', 'th', 'zh', 'zh-TW']
# sanity: groups that should be identical
same = {'ar-MA': 'ar', 'pt-PT': 'pt', 'ln': 'hi', 'si': 'hi', 'sr': 'hi', 'sv': 'hi'}
for a, b in same.items():
    assert d['units'][a] == d['units'][b], (a, b)

def rs(s):
    out = []
    for ch in s:
        o = ord(ch)
        if ch == '"' or ch == '\\':
            out.append('\\' + ch)
        elif o < 0x20 or o >= 0x7f:
            out.append('\\u{%x}' % o)
        else:
            out.append(ch)
    return '"' + ''.join(out) + '"'

units = list(d['units']['en'].keys())
lines = []
lines.append('// Generated from the original runtime (unit patterns: one/other per display).')
lines.append('// Each entry: unit -> [short one, short other, long one, long other, narrow one, narrow other].')
lines.append('pub const UNIT_IDS: [&str; %d] = [%s];' % (len(units), ', '.join(rs(u) for u in units)))
lines.append('pub const UNIT_GROUPS: [&str; %d] = [%s];' % (len(groups), ', '.join(rs(g) for g in groups)))
lines.append('pub static UNIT_PATTERNS: [[[&str; 6]; %d]; %d] = [' % (len(units), len(groups)))
for g in groups:
    lines.append('    // %s' % g)
    lines.append('    [')
    for u in units:
        disps = d['units'][g][u]
        row = []
        for disp in ['short', 'long', 'narrow']:
            cats = disps[disp]
            other = pat2str(cats['other'])
            one = pat2str(cats['one']) if 'one' in cats else other
            row += [one, other]
        lines.append('        [%s],' % ', '.join(rs(x) for x in row))
    lines.append('    ],')
lines.append('];')
open('/tmp/intlagent/gen/units.rs', 'w').write('\n'.join(lines) + '\n')
print('ok', len(units), len(groups))
